note: Clustering of the 183 free-text requirements into candidate systems, then adversarial pruning. 108 proposed, 2 survived. ⚠ The pruner was told to DEFAULT TO REFUTING, so this is a floor. Many refutations cite work/rulings/DECISIONS.md — owner scope decisions the readers had never been shown.

systems.name: resistance-stacking-exceptions
systems.whatItIs: A named per-source exception to PF2e's take-the-highest rule: resistance from a gate junction and resistance from Thermal Nimbus must ADD rather than one superseding the other, with both sources shown in the breakdown.

refuted.name: ally-aura-modifier-publication
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The proposal's load-bearing requirement — the number automatically reaching the recipient — was already ruled on twice by the owner, and both rulings are implemented in code. It is a decided scope boundary, not an unbuilt lane.

1) RULING F, verbatim owner decision, C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/work/rulings/DECISIONS.md line 171 ("## F — Bonuses that land on someone else (17 + 3 from E) — DECIDED"): "if its an effect the effects a teamate and not you then dont do anything, if its active to a limited to an amount of time then add mode to the user that activated the thing that let the user knows its active but it wint actually do anything." Implementation notes: "The bonus goes to a teammate, not you -> NOTHING on your sheet. No star, no modifier. The feat's own description already says what the ally gets." Shipped 2026-07-30 across 20 records (feat ally modes keyed feat-<id>; item ally modes via fromItemId). So "the number never reaches the recipient" is the specified behaviour.

2) RULING M, C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts lines 84-89, states the reason in the owner's own terms: an aura "you might not be standing in" — "whether it includes you depends on where you stand, which the app can never know." There is no positional model anywhere in src/ (grep for distanceTo/withinFeet/inEmanation returns 0 files; the only position code in the repo is tracker/src/components/InitiativeTracker.tsx, a separate app). Emanation membership is battlefield state, which docs/mechanic-lanes.md explicitly excludes under NOT-lanes ("Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet").

3) The claimed empty receptacles are not empty. GIVER side already prints it: situationalBonuses.ts:606 ascended-celestial-dedication carries {when: "ALLIES inside your active nimbus — on saves against fear", bonus: "+1 status"}; :3196 aura-of-courage's condition marker names the ally step-down; thermal-nimbus in public/core.json carries effectChoices granting resistances value '@actor.level' AND a stances-bucket note stating the ally clause in full. RECIPIENT side already exists and is populated — Ruling M's chosen shape is a situational entry on the RECEIVING sheet with the positional condition in the note, and inbound-emanation entries ship today: situationalBonuses.ts:2213 leshy-familiar-secrets (+2 circumstance "while within the 15-foot emanation of your familiar's Purify Air"), :1761 paradise-light (+1 item "while inside the 30-foot Sanctum emanation"), :2104 viridian-crown ("you and allies in the emanation"). The mode lane is the other receptacle: src/rules/modes.ts:145 cat-inspire-courage (Courageous Anthem) carries the ally numbers as REAL modifiers (+1 status attack, +1 status damage, +1 status Will vs fear), and ModesPanel.tsx:123 (`ql || showAll`) lets a non-bard reveal and toggle it, so a recipient's own attack number moves with the source named in the breakdown. ModeDef.resistances/weaknesses/immunities/senses/speeds exist (src/rules/types.ts:2492-2498) and 75 of the 429 shipped modes grant resistances; 51 mention allies (e.g. item-elysian-dew: "The bonuses come from a 10-foot emanation"). The types.ts comment even names Triple Time's ally Speed bonus as the reason that half was built. Also note the gold entry for eternal-blessing claims "no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all" — MODE_TARGETS (modes.ts:17-27) has both `attack` and `damage`. That premise is simply false.

4) The "borrowed radius owned by another feature that other feats enlarge" would be a stored number with no reader — the project's own write-only-with-a-reader lesson. The sole consumer of an aura radius is a token/geometry engine, i.e. a VTT.

5) The proposed delivery target does not accept writes: party/campaign teammate sheets are read-only by design (src/sheet/PartyMembers.tsx:23,64; src/data/party.ts:32,94). The one cross-sheet channel that does exist is deliberately capability-and-display only, campaign-wide, with no geometry: PARTY_SHARED_FEATS = ['battleforger'] (src/sheet/partySummary.ts:28) plus src/data/partyCapabilities.ts, and partySummary.ts:59 already broadcasts `modes: c.activeModes.map(m => m.name)` so teammates SEE the nimbus running — exactly Ruling F's display-only publication.

Secondary refutation (not-one-system) also lands: the 6 entries (#34, #42, #60, #64, #88, #91) are three different receptacles plus two unrelated problems — a save bonus (already printed at :606 and :180), an attack bonus whose real blocker is hosting an always-on Bless at a level-derived rank (a spell-hosting problem), a resistance, a borrowed-radius geometry model, and a self-vs-ally value split. "Publish to allies in a radius" is the label, not one mechanism.

Honest residual, and it is NOT the proposed system: the only thing with no user-facing authoring route is hand-entering an INBOUND resistance. ModeEditor (src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:245+) exposes only MODE_TARGETS-shaped check/AC/damage modifiers, and the item editor's Advanced passive block (src/sheet/ItemEditorModal.tsx:148) covers ac/perception/saves/attack/speed/skills but not resistances — so a recipient of Thermal Nimbus must currently note it rather than toggle it. That is a one-field editor-surface gap on an existing lane (mode.resistances already works from data), not a missing cross-sheet publication system.

refuted.name: targeted-ally-grants
refuted.why:
The proposal is a disjunction in its own wording ("a reaction that appears on their sheet ... OR a one-shot fortune effect placed on their next roll"), and the 4 entries are really 2 records (vantage-shot, guide-the-timeline) covering 3 unrelated capabilities with no shared storage, consumer, or lifetime. Each collapses separately against an existing route.

(1) The vantage-shot reaction. A reaction in this app is `grantsActions` plus a prose `trigger` string that is NEVER evaluated — `Feat.trigger?: string` at src/rules/types.ts:1434, and MainTab.tsx:224-247 merely collects granted action records and lists them. So "triggered by my Strike" is not a capability at all; every reaction the app ships (Shield Block, Reactive Strike) is a listed entry whose trigger the player reads. What is left is only WHOSE list it appears on — and Vantage Shot is symmetric: its second sentence puts the identical reaction on the holder ("Similarly, when your spotter successfully makes a ranged Strike against a foe, YOU can use a reaction to attempt a Stealth check"), so `grantsActions` fully covers the holder's copy. For the partner's copy the app already ships a cross-character grant lane: `PARTY_SHARED_FEATS` (src/sheet/partySummary.ts:28) + `partyHasFeat()` (src/data/partyCapabilities.ts:45), whose documented purpose is "a capability any member can use because one member has it," consumed live at src/sheet/ItemEditorModal.tsx:1191 as `character.feats.some(f => f.featId === 'battleforger') || partyHasFeat('battleforger')`. That IS a record on one character granting a usable capability on a different player's sheet — the exact thing gold entry 177 says "has no expression." Battleforger's own comment even says it "prepares another character's gear." The reviewer's stated blockers (grantsAction grants to the holder; companion covers only creatures I own) simply omit this third route. And the reaction's payload is "the foe is off-guard," which the lane manual's NOT-lanes list rules out explicitly ("Effects on enemies ... rather than on your own sheet").

(2) The guide-the-timeline fortune. A transient one-roll, one-round roll-MODE shares nothing with (1) — building either gives you nothing toward the other. Its route is the already-decided ruling F (project_hh_rulings_dfgh): ally-instant -> nothing at all; ally-timed -> a display-only mode on the ACTIVATOR, which shipped ~29 ally-facing modes in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, including `tweak-appearances` whose note reads "The target you tweaked has +1 item ... Your own checks are unchanged" — a mode on the activator whose entire content lands on someone else. Fortune itself is likewise an expressed lane, as `situational` prose: ~15 entries render "fortune: roll twice and take the higher result" (derring-do, incredible-luck, acrobats-staff, starsong-nectar, laurel-of-the-empath), and the lane already carries ALLY-scoped when-clauses ("ALLIES inside your active nimbus — on saves against fear" on ascended-celestial-dedication, situationalBonuses.ts:606). The feat is on the sheet already (actionCost 1 action, plus `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` from effect-backfill.json:74001); the roll-twice instruction is the internal step of an activity, which the manual excludes by name ("Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane"). Note also that guide-the-timeline's other gold entries (115/116/118/119) were filed as three DIFFERENT needs — a named chronoskimmer DC, and a 24-hour per-target immunity list — so the reviewer took one clause out of a record the audit itself refused to treat as one system.

(3) A third strand smuggled in: gold entries 176 and 178 ask for a persistent stored reference to another specific character ("your spotter"). That is a data-model relationship, not a grant, and the app's established handling of this very archetype is prose in the situational `when` — situationalBonuses.ts:629, sniping-duo-dedication: "on the damage roll of your next Strike against a target your spotter just hit…". So even the reviewer's own source entries split the cluster into a relationship slot, an action grant, and a roll-mode.

Finally, the literal reading is foreclosed by architecture rather than by a missing lane: teammate sheets are read-only mirrors published to `campaign_characters` (src/data/party.ts), and only the GM has a write path (`GmEdit`). "My feat writes a reaction onto another user's character" is not one absent lane, it is a permissions subsystem — which is why the app's answer is to surface the capability on the reader's side (partyHasFeat) rather than to push a grant across.

refuted.name: named-ally-relationship-slot
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The app already has a persistent, per-record slot for a player-typed designation the app has no data for: FeatChoiceDef with kind: 'text' (src/rules/types.ts:1340-1346 — "free text the player types, for picks whose vocabulary the app has no data for"). It is live in three renderers — src/builder/Builder.tsx:285 (feat sub-choices), src/builder/shared.tsx:2518 (heritage choices), src/sheet/CharacterSheet.tsx:751 — the answer persists on the character, and src/rules/dailyChoices.ts:86 returns the typed string as its own label. The in-code comment at CharacterSheet.tsx:752 names its existing use for a record pointing at a thing the player names: "Call Gun's bonded weapon". So the reviewer's load-bearing claim — "nothing on the sheet can resolve the phrase 'your spotter' to a person" — is factually wrong. A `choice` with prompt "Choose one willing, non-minion ally to act as your spotter", kind 'text', hung on Sniping Duo Dedication, stores and displays the name, and reaches every clause that reads it.

Two further errors in the framing.

(1) Wrong record. The pointer is not created by Vantage Shot. Sniping Duo Dedication (feat-3258/8763 in the archive) creates it: "When you take this dedication, choose one willing, non-minion ally to act as your spotter" — and the same paragraph says "your spotter doesn't need to spend any feats of their own," so there is nothing to place on the spotter's sheet either. Changing spotter costs 3 days of downtime, i.e. GM adjudication. The proposal is aimed at a feat that only consumes the designation.

(2) Nothing computes with the identity, so `note` is not the near-miss they claim. I read all nine Sniping Duo feats. Every clause reading "your spotter" resolves to a table fact, never a value derived on the holder's sheet: lesser cover between the two of you (map); +1 circumstance/damage die vs a target the other just hit (whose hit); Triangulate — "both of you can see the target" (line of sight); Targeted Redirection — "treat your spotter's position as your own" (position); Tag Team — "within the other's melee reach or first range increment" (map + their gear); Concentrated Assault — use the higher of the two attack rolls (their roll); Duo's Aim — target within the spotter's reach/range increment (map + their gear); Vantage Shot — a reaction on the other's turn; Eagle Eyes — "as long as you can see or hear each other" (line of sight). Substituting the string "Valeros" for "your spotter" changes no number the sheet derives. The identity's only sheet-side residue is print — which is exactly `note`, "a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable," and the rest is the lanes doc's own exclusions (battlefield/positioning, and the internal steps of an activity).

And the app already carries the mechanically-real halves of this archetype today, with "your spotter" left in the prose qualifier and working: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:629 sniping-duo-dedication (+1 circumstance per weapon damage die, "against a target your spotter just hit"), plus exploit-opening (+2), duos-aim (+2) in the same table, and eagle-eyes at line 3224 as an off-guard note. Those read no differently from any other accepted situational qualifier ("against a frightened creature", "while in your favored terrain"), and Vantage Shot's own holder-facing half is a reaction — `grantsAction`.

Cluster evidence is also weaker than stated: "2 of 183" is one feat counted twice, once under lens 'resources' and once under 'unmodellable' (the other three vantage-shot entries are the separate outward-grant claim). The only other relationship-pointer entry in the file, guarded-domain, points at a PLACE shared with a companion, not at another PC. So: designation → `choice` (kind 'text'); clauses that read it → `situational` / `note` / `grantsAction`, four of them already built.

refuted.name: feat-to-owned-item-binding
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The reviewer examined the wrong mechanism. `InventoryItem.designations` is the class-ROLE tag lane (innovation / weapon-implement / bonded / ikon / rune-source) and their objection to it is correct — but the app has a SECOND, separate lane that is exactly a per-record pointer into the character's own inventory, and it is live today on six feats.

The lane: the `choice` lane (mechanic-lanes.md section G) with `kind: 'open'` and `from: { type: 'own-item', itemType: 'weapon' }`. `OpenChoiceFrom.type` has an entire family of `own-` sources whose declared purpose is precisely this — C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\types.ts:1048-1084 says "the `own-` kinds search the CHARACTER, because several records pick from what you already have". `openChoiceOptions` case 'own-item' (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\openChoice.ts:163) walks `ch.inventory`, filters by `itemType` (and optionally `investedOnly`), and returns the owned items as the picker's options. The answer is stored per-record in `build.featChoices[key]` (build.ts:5007), so it is a pointer held BY THE RECORD, not a tag shared across a kind — which is the exact defect the reviewer said blocked designations. Both halves are wired: the picker renders at build time (Builder.tsx:302) and at daily preparations when `daily: true` (dailyChoices.ts:53).

The reader half, which the gold entry demands ("a feat-to-item attachment the strike breakdown can read"), also already exists: `StrikeDamageRider.fromChoiceFlag` — types.ts:2867, "Restrict to the weapon the PLAYER chose, named by the flag of the choice that asked" — consumed in derive.ts:2461-2464, where the rider is skipped unless the recorded answer equals the Strike's own weapon id. So a record's later clauses DO resolve to the chosen object and only its Strike. Gird Champion ships on this pair today (`choice.flag: 'godlingWeapon'` + `strikeDamage[].fromChoiceFlag: 'godlingWeapon'`).

Six live records in public/core.json are the identical printed shape as the ikon Usage line: `fused-staff` ("Which weapon is your staff fused into?"), `signature-weapon` ("Which of your weapons is your signature weapon?"), `celestial-armaments` ("Which weapon carries your celestial blessing?"), `autonomous-arms` ("Spear or polearm infused today"), `warshard-warrior-dedication` ("Warshard weapon today"), `built-in-tools` (own-item/equipment, picks:2, distinct). branched-tree-of-pain's "imbued into a weapon ikon" is the same sentence as "infused today", and it needs no new machinery.

On the damage-type filter, their one concrete technical objection: `OpenChoiceFrom` already carries per-type narrowing fields (`weaponCategory`, `rarity`, `maxLevel`, `itemType`, `investedOnly`), so a `damageType` filter is one more field on an existing filter object — not a system. And the app's own DOCUMENTED convention for a printed narrowing the picker cannot express is `FeatChoiceDef.note` (types.ts:1385-1392: "a caveat shown WITH the picker, for a choice that works but whose printed restriction can't be enforced"). `autonomous-arms` uses it verbatim for the same shape of restriction: "choose a spear or polearm - the proficiency and intelligent/artifact limits aren't checked here." "piercing or slashing" lands in exactly that slot.

Two residual imprecisions, both inside the lane rather than absent from the app: (1) `own-item` dedupes on `item.id`, so the pointer names the weapon KIND you own rather than one `instanceId` — two identical longswords collapse to one option; note the app ALREADY has instance-precise per-strike matching where it wanted it (`weaponMatches` looks up `strike.instanceId` and reads that instance's designations, derive.ts:2393-2396), so instance precision is a wiring choice inside the lane, not a missing capability. (2) `signature-weapon` carries an `inert` string conceding its crit-spec is not yet narrowed to the chosen weapon — that is an unbuilt consumer of a built lane (crit-spec has no `fromChoiceFlag` equivalent yet), which is the classic per-record backfill gap, not a new system. The cluster is also 3 entries from ONE clause read through three lenses, so its true size is one record's Usage line.

refuted.name: crit-range-widening
refuted.why: The `situational` lane (mechanic-lanes.md section J; src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, rendered via explain.ts's `strikeAttack` case into the strike breakdown's star list) already carries this exact rule, word for word, for another feat. Line 2755: "savage-critical": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'strikeAttack' }], when: "with a weapon or unarmed attack you have legendary proficiency in", bonus: "a natural 19 that would be a success is a critical success instead" }] — the widened die face AND the "would already be a success" qualifier, both present. Both of the reviewer's blockers are false against the app's own data. (1) "situational cannot scope to one weapon": the `bonus` field is free prose and the `when` field routinely carries scope the engine cannot compute — that is the owner's standing ruling (Ruling M singing-shortbow scopes positionally; Ruling N artillerist-dedication scopes to a siege weapon you crew; both documented in the header comments of situationalBonuses.ts). The imbued-weapon-ikon case specifically is already done: line 2706 "compliant-gold": kind 'strikeAttack', when "while your divine spark is in this ikon (immanence active), with the imbued melee weapon", bonus = a reach/trait rule, not a number. That is the same feat family, the same per-weapon binding, the same non-numeric rule statement. There is also a hard per-item route: explain.ts's authoredSituational() reads db.items[id].situational and only surfaces it while the item is equipped/worn/invested, and types.ts's ItemDesignation includes 'ikon' with play.ts markDesignation binding one owned item as the character's ikon — so a situational entry can be scoped to the actual bound weapon, not just described. StrikeDamageRider.strikeName is not the only per-weapon mechanism. (2) "the roller's crit flag is hard-wired to a natural 20": src/rules/dice.ts is 76 lines and its signature is roll(label, count, sides, modifier) — it never receives a DC or a target AC. Its d20.outcome nat-20/nat-1 flag is a dice-tray highlight, not a degree-of-success engine; the app computes degree of success nowhere, for any check, for any feat. So there is no per-strike threshold to add, and "as long as that result would be a success" is unknowable to this sheet because it depends on the target's AC — squarely inside mechanic-lanes.md's "NOT lanes" (effects that need the enemy's numbers / the GM's adjudication). Two further points. The cluster is not 3 records: gold-freetext.json entries 1, 3 and 5 are all the same clause of the same feat (branched-tree-of-pain) seen through the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses. And degree-of-success remapping generally is already a populated lane, not an absent one — situationalBonuses.ts carries dozens: hydraulic-maneuvers (2655, "a critical failure becomes a failure"), brine-may (2698), cantorian-reinforcement (2700), irrepressible and its three variants (2740-2743), jungle-strider (2744), agile-mind, anvils-hardness, battle-hardened, battlefield-intuition, blast-dodger, divine-will, dogged-will, earned-resilience, evasive-reflexes, explosion-dodger (2784-2834). What is actually true is narrower and much cheaper: branched-tree-of-pain has no entry in situationalBonuses.ts and nothing in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. That is a "promised but empty" record in an existing lane — one authored line following the savage-critical and compliant-gold templates — not a missing system.

refuted.name: mythic-proficiency-rank
refuted.why: The `situational` lane covers it, and is ALREADY carrying this exact capability 23 times in live data. (1) The premise is wrong on the rules: War of Immortals p.76 (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/rules/rules-3322.json) says "Unlike trained, expert, master, and legendary proficiency, you use mythic proficiency only when an ability tells you to" — no statistic on any sheet ever holds rank=mythic, so PROFICIENCY_RANKS (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:63) is correctly closed at legendary. Adding a sixth rung would be the wrong build: it would poison skillIncreaseCap/nextRank in Builder.tsx (a skill increase could offer 'L -> Mythic') and the companion maturity ladder in src/rules/companions.ts, both of which index that array. (2) The app's actual route is src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts — a display-only registry of {targets, when, bonus} where `bonus` is a free phrase, keyed by record id, surfaced as a `*` on the stat plus a line in that stat's detail popup via featSituationalLines/statHasSituational in src/rules/explain.ts. Because it is display-only, the underlying skill keeps its real rank — precisely what the reviewer says is needed. (3) It is already used for this exact sentence, on live records verified present in public/core.json: acrobats-calling and sagas-calling and sages-calling and handlers-calling and hunters-calling and runelords-calling and thespians-calling and bookkeepers-calling and caretakers-calling and demagogues-calling and doomsayers-calling and dreamers-calling and echoes-of-the-scrolls ('attempt the check at mythic proficiency'), become-shadow and avoid-fates-gaze and binds-that-tie ('roll at mythic proficiency'), plus the two hard shapes the reviewer thought impossible — steadfast-grip stores it as a save-DC entry (dcOnly: true, 'calculated at mythic proficiency') and prescient-parry stores it against AC ('AC is also recalculated at mythic proficiency'). src/rules/explain.ts:197 collects both c.feats ids and ownedFeatureIds(class features), so a feat like Guarded Domain reaches the Diplomacy popup by the same route the 18 callings already use. (4) guarded-domain simply has no row: grep for it across src/rules/*.ts returns nothing. That makes it a promised-but-empty defect in an existing lane (one authored line: targets skill/diplomacy, when 'a creature has been in your guarded domain 1 hour and you commune for 1 minute', bonus 'attempt the Gather Information check at mythic proficiency (10 + level instead of your Diplomacy proficiency)'), not a missing system. (5) The companion half is likewise routed: COMPANION_MODS.note in src/rules/companionGrants.ts is 'a rules note shown on the companion card', and the repo already has a stated ruling for exactly this shape — the stealthy-companion entry is deliberately note-only with the comment that the app has no conditional-skill lane for companions and an unconditional skillGrant 'would hand master Stealth to every companion — an over-grant is worse than the gap'. So the companion clause takes the companion-note route by existing policy, not a new subsystem. (6) Secondary refutations, if 5 were not enough: mechanic-lanes.md rules the target out twice over — 'A bonus to one specific roll is situational, not a flat bonus' and 'the internal steps of an activity ... the app lists the action; the player performs it'. The check here is a downtime/exploration Gather Information gated on a week of downtime establishing the domain and the target having lingered an hour — GM-adjudicated, never rolled by the app — and its Mythic Point cost is already tracked (MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS pips, src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:933). Nothing on the sheet needs a new number; the star plus the clause is the whole affordance, and 23 records prove the app can already write it.

refuted.name: resource-cost-declarations
refuted.why:
The cluster is 3 feats x 3 lenses = 9 entries, and the three feats need three unrelated mechanisms that share only the English word "cost". A single "cost line" field would do nothing useful for any of them.

FIRST, the premise is factually false. The reviewer writes "no field anywhere says 'spend from THAT pool', so nothing decrements, nothing blocks the action at zero, [and] the rank ... cannot feed the effect's magnitude." All four clauses are wrong: that exact system is shipped, as the `charges` lane (manual section I: `counters`, `itemUses`, `capacity`). In C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/itemUses.ts, `chargeCounterId(item)` names WHICH pool an activation spends from (a staff's shared 'pool' vs a wand's 'freq') — a pool the individual spell record does not own; `chargeCostToCast(item, rank)` is a cost declaration whose magnitude is DERIVED FROM RANK ("a staff spends the spell's rank"); `canCastFromItem` returns false when `u.current < cost`; and C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:1449 wires that straight to `castDisabled: !canCastFromItem(itemDef, itemInv, rank)`, then decrements via `setItemCounter(p, ..., chargesFor(u, u.current - cost))`. Declare-a-cost, spend-from-a-foreign-pool, rank-feeds-magnitude, block-at-zero: all four exist. So the proposal is not a missing capability, it is at most a request to widen an existing lane's reach.

Now the three feats, which come apart completely:

(1) guarded-domain — MYTHIC POINT. There is nothing per-record to declare. The record ALREADY carries the tracked half: `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}`, spent against `Character.featUses`. The point itself is a uniform charge of exactly 1 against a pool that already exists, is already displayed, and already refills: `PlayState.mythicPoints` / `MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS` (src/rules/play.ts:43,580), pips at src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:959, refilled by daily preparations. The universal rule is already stated in-app, in src/sheet/MythicRules.tsx:154-159: "many mythic feats, calling actions, and mythic activities cost 1 mythic point to use. Spend from the same shared pool ... use the mythic panel to spend them." So the reviewer's "two independent costs for a single activation" already has two independent trackers on the sheet, both of which decrement. The only genuine gap is that tapping one does not auto-tap the other — an automation policy the app deliberately does not have for ANY character-level pool: focus (`focusUsed`, pips at SpellsTab.tsx:1364 titled "Spend focus point"), hero points (`setHeroPoints`), spell slots (`toggleExpendedSlot`/`setSlotsUsed`), innate uses (`toggleInnateCast`), and class resources (steppers at VitalsRail.tsx:857). play.ts's own header declares PlayState to be the hand-edited runtime layer. Item charges auto-decrement precisely because an item owns its pool and "Cast" is one unambiguous trigger; a 3-action teleport has no such trigger. Adding a declaration to 9 records would make them the only records out of ~43,686 that behave differently from every pool the app tracks.

(2) energetic-resonance — NOT A COST PROBLEM. Read the real text: "Expend one of your spell slots of a rank equal to or higher than that of the triggering spell. You gain resistance to one of the triggering effect's damage types equal to twice the expended spell slot's rank." The expenditure is already one tap (`toggleExpendedSlot` for index-addressed prepared slots, `setSlotsUsed` for per-rank spontaneous pools) and is the identical tap whether the slot is burned by casting or by this. The only interesting part — a temporary resistance whose value and damage type the player parameterizes — is the `mode` lane (manual section J), and the app already does this exact shape 75 times. `deitys-protection` in public/core.json is the same feat structurally: `resistances:[{type:'all', value:'floor((@actor.level+1)/2)'}]` with a note reading "Turn this on after you cast a domain spell. The resistance equals the rank of the domain spell you cast." `adept-benefit-amulet` shows a player-chosen type is expressible: `{type:'chosen damage type', value:'5+5*min(1,...)'}`. A player-chosen resistance type is also an existing BUILD lane (`resistanceChoice`, src/rules/build.ts:183). What the reviewer calls "the rank feeds the magnitude" is heightening/upcast machinery sitting DOWNSTREAM of the cost, not the cost line — and it has nothing whatever in common with tapping a mythic pip.

(3) blood-and-spirit — the "unresistable" flag has NO REFERENT, so there is nothing to express. `applyDamage(play, amount, max, deathBase)` (src/rules/play.ts:538) takes a raw number and never consults resistances, weaknesses or immunities; every caller (VitalsRail.tsx:253, :287, :1123) hands it the number the player typed. The IWR chips in HpNumpadModal are OPTIONAL player-tapped shortcuts that pre-reduce a figure before entry, and they are themselves switchable off (`hpIwrButtons === false`). So typing 6 into the HP field IS already "1d6 damage that can't be resisted in any way" — the clause is a table-facing clarification for the GM, not a sheet capability. Meanwhile HP-as-a-price already has an in-app precedent handled this way: `sanguimancy-hp` in src/rules/classResources.ts, whose note reads "Temporary HP you can also SPEND to power sanguimancy feats" — a stepper plus prose. And the feat's actual mechanical payload (Strikes with the coated weapon deal +1d6 spirit until end of turn, gated on your own persistent bleed) is `mode` + `strikeDamage`/`weaponRider`, with the bleed gate as the mode's `duration`/`note` — the same construction as `battle-scars` and `armored-resistance`, both of which gate on a live circumstance via prose plus a switch.

The three needs are: a uniform pip decrement against an existing pool (nothing to declare); a formula-valued toggleable resistance (the `mode` lane); and a die-rolled write to an HP tracker whose exemption clause describes behaviour the app already has by default. Bundling them as one "resource-cost-declarations" system merges a resource ledger, an upcast formula, and a damage application. Even granting the reviewer their best single point — no auto-decrement of mythic points — that is one narrow automation ask about one pool, not a system, and it does not generalize to the other two feats.

refuted.name: player-named-place-attunement
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The lane is `choice` (section G) — FeatChoiceDef with `kind: 'text'` — paired with `note` (section J) for the uncomputable clause. It is not merely expressible; the app already ships a player-named-place designation on a live record, and Guarded Domain is simply an unwired one.

1) THE SAME SYSTEM IS ALREADY BUILT AND POPULATED. `public/core.json` → feats/thaumaturges-demesne carries `choice: {flag:'demesne', kind:'text', prompt:'Name your demesne (the area you have claimed)'}`. Its printed text is the same shape as Guarded Domain's: "You have claimed an area or location as your demesne... choose a demesne, an area of no more than 2,000 square feet", and later clauses refer back to it (a permanent arcane Peaceful Bubble on it, three unseen custodians, an elemental sentinel on an object in it). Player-authored, one slot, size the player writes in, later clauses reference it — all three of the proposal's properties, shipped. 45 records use kind:'text' today. The typedoc at src/rules/types.ts:1340 says the lane exists for exactly this: "free text the player types, for picks whose vocabulary the app has no data for", because enumerating the vocabulary "would be inventing content". It renders and persists (build-time at src/builder/shared.tsx:2518 and Builder.tsx:285 into `build.featChoices`; daily at CharacterSheet.tsx:751 into `PlayState.dailyChoices`), with `note` and `inert` printed beside the field.

2) THE SINGLE-SLOT HALF IS FREE, NOT MISSING. A choice flag holds exactly one value (`picks` defaults to 1), so typing a new place overwrites the old — that IS "selecting a new guarded domain immediately ends your protection over the previous one". The reviewer's requirement (gold-freetext entry 81) that switching "must clear the previous designation and everything keyed to it" is vacuous: nothing derives from the string, so there is nothing keyed to it to clear. No exclusiveGroup machinery is needed; the reviewer reached for modes and thereby imported an exclusivity problem the text lane doesn't have. Claim Cardinal Domains already uses the same lane for "Which claimed domain is active today?".

3) "NOTHING KEYS OFF THAT WORD" IS TRUE AND HARMLESS — NOTHING NEEDS TO. Read Guarded Domain's later clauses (full text in public/core-descriptions.json): (a) "If a creature has been in your guarded domain for at least 1 hour while you or your companion are also inside" → Gather Information at mythic proficiency; (b) "once per day as a 3-action activity you can spend a Mythic Point to teleport... within your domain". Neither computes anything from the place's identity — whether a creature is inside a 5-mile radius, and for how long, is a table fact. The mechanical residue of both clauses lands in OTHER clusters in the same audit file: mythic proficiency (entries 76, 77, 82, 85) and the Mythic Point pool (78, 83, 86). The once/day resource is already on the record (`limitedUses: {max:1, per:'day'}`). So refusing to build a place-attunement system orphans nothing mechanical.

4) THE LAPSE/RENEWAL HALF IS A NOT-LANE, AND THE APP HAS ALREADY RULED ON IT. Whether the character "spent more than 1 month outside" a 5-mile radius needs the campaign's geography and travel log — GM adjudication and narrative access, explicitly a NOT-lane in the manual. A clock would not help: the sheet still could not know the answer, so any automated expiry would be wrong. The app's settled home for this exact clause shape is the choice's own `note`: Cape of Justice carries a functionally identical lapse ("let 24 hours pass without slaying or capturing them — and you take a -1 item penalty to Perception for 24 hours") as `note` text; Witch's Charge carries "lasts until your next daily preparations" the same way; ModeDef.duration (types.ts:2535) is the same ruling for modes. Note also that "a week of downtime" is a cost paid at the table, not a sheet resource — the app models no downtime ledger anywhere, and the audit's separate experienced-professional cluster is where that question actually lives.

5) THE CLUSTER IS ONE RECORD COUNTED FOUR TIMES. All four entries (79, 80, 81, 84) are guarded-domain, split across the `resources` and `unmodellable` lenses. There is no cross-record generality behind the proposal, while the existing lane already serves 45 records including a claimed area.

What guarded-domain actually needs is a data edit, not a system: add `choice: {flag:'guardedDomain', kind:'text', prompt:'Name your guarded domain (a settlement, or a natural area with a 5-mile radius)', note:'One at a time — naming a new one ends your protection over the old. It lapses if you spend more than 1 month outside it; another week of downtime re-attunes you.'}`. That is the manual's "promised but empty" bucket, not "no lane at all".

refuted.name: always-on-hosted-spell-effects
refuted.why:
Both members already reach the sheet today through two existing lanes, and neither needs a new one.

ETERNAL-BLESSING → the `mode` lane. It is not a hypothetical fit: `feat-eternal-blessing` is already a shipped mode in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json (429 modes) from C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/toggle-modes.json:869 — `feats: ['eternal-blessing']`, `duration: 'permanent — you may Dismiss it…'`, `modifiers: [{target:'attack', type:'status', value:1}]`, plus a note carrying the derived rank, the 15-foot radius and the can't-increase clause. This is the decided ally-bonus mechanism from ruling F (a feat has no 'Use one' button, so a feat's ally mode uses the `feats:[id]` gate rather than `fromItemId`).

The reviewer's central claim — 'the vocabulary has no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all (acBonus, saveBonus, perception, skills exist — attack does not)' — is simply wrong. `attack` is a first-class mode target (src/rules/modes.ts:23, MODE_TARGETS) AND it is read by the strike engine: src/rules/derive.ts:2653 and :2921 call `modeTypedMods(c.activeModes, {kind:'attack'})` and pool it with PF2e cross-source stacking; explain.ts:944 puts it in the breakdown. The +1 status to attack rolls reaches the number.

CONSTANT-LEVITATION → the `speed` lane. Its feat record in public/core.json already carries `speeds: {fly: 40}`, and derive.ts:3147-3150 pushes every selected feat into `grantSources` unconditionally, so the fly Speed appears on the Speeds line. 'Affected by a constant Fly spell' has exactly one mechanical output on your own sheet: a permanent fly Speed. That is built.

The three sub-claims that are supposed to make the lane inadequate all collapse on inspection:
(1) 'the derived rank has nowhere to live' — the rank changes no number. Neither `bless` nor `fly` carries any `heightened` entry in public/core.json, because neither scales with rank in PF2e. A rank on a non-cast effect has exactly one rules use, counteract level, and `grep -ri counteract src/` shows the app models no counteract anywhere, for anything. So the rank is text, and the text is present verbatim in the mode's note. Separately, level-derived VALUES do have a home when they affect a number: `resolveFormula` resolves `@actor.level` in speeds/resistances (jelly-body uses it), so 'a derived value has nowhere to live' is false as a general claim too.
(2) 'nothing marks the effect dispellable' — a mode is toggleable, and that IS the app's dispel/expiry model by explicit design: the ModeDef.duration doc-comment (src/rules/types.ts) says 'The app has no clock — this tells the player what they are tracking; they switch it off.' Dismiss-and-returns-after-1-minute is recorded in this mode's own `duration`.
(3) the 15-foot fixed radius 'override' — bless.baseArea in public/core.json is already `{value:15, kind:'emanation'}`. That is the spell's printed radius, not an override. The suppressed half (bless's Sustain-to-expand) is a per-round in-play action the app tracks for no spell, for anyone.

Secondary refutation, if the above were somehow waved off: not-one-system. The 4 entries are 3 lenses on one clause of eternal-blessing plus 1 on constant-levitation, and the two feats want unrelated capabilities — an ally-facing aura publishing a check bonus versus a self-only movement grant with no aura, no ally facing and no level-derived rank at all. 'A hosted spell object at a derived rank' describes the flavour text both share, not a mechanism either one needs.

refuted.name: borrowed-effect-overrides
refuted.why:
The premise is false on all three examples, and each has a named existing lane.

(1) hybrid-study-spell — the reviewer's headline ("nothing expresses 'pick this option but take only part of it', which is what keeps hybrid-study-spell from silently handing over a full subclass") is ALREADY BUILT, in the shipped data, by the `choice` + `effectGrant` lanes. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json carries the feat with `focusPoolBonus: 1` and an `effectChoices` menu of eight hybrid studies, each option's payload being exactly `grant: { focusSpells: [<that study's conflux spell>] }` and nothing else. Twelve sibling records do the identical thing (basic-bloodline-spell, first-revelation, order-spell, order-magic, domain-fluency, advanced-elemental-spell, diverse-mystery, …). The claim that "the choice lanes grant whole options" is wrong about this engine: an EffectChoice option's `grant` is an authored EffectGrant, and C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/build.ts:3136 (`applyAlwaysOn` → `mergeEffect(chosenEffects, g)`) merges only that payload. Nothing anywhere expands the referenced `hybridStudy` record — partial import is the ONLY behaviour the app has. There is no whole-option inheritance to subtract from, so no subtractive facility is needed. The printed clause "you don't gain any of the hybrid study's other benefits" is a specification of the additive payload, not a mechanic.

(2) critter-shape — the fly denial subtracts nothing, because Pest Form never confers a fly Speed at 1st rank and never derives statistics from the copied animal. Pest Form's own text (core-descriptions.json) says the chosen animal "has no effect on the form's Size or statistics", and the fly Speed lives solely in its **Heightened (4th)** entry. So "you still don't gain a fly Speed" restates the base spell's default; the permission ("unlike normal for 1st-rank pest form") is an access clause, an explicit NOT-lane. The route for the form itself is `mode`: ModeDef payloads are authored field-by-field (`speeds`, `senses`, `weaknesses`, `modifiers`, `duration`, `note`) — 429 modes ship, 23 of them write `speeds`, and denying fly means not writing `speeds.fly`. The app even has the mirror idiom: bloodline-mutation's option is `{ label: 'Fly Speed equal to your land Speed', note: 'Only if the creatures associated with your bloodline can fly.', grant: { speeds: { fly: '@actor.speed.land' } } }` — a fly Speed gated on a property of the associated creature, expressed as an authored option plus an option-level note (rendered at Builder.tsx:1662 / shared.tsx:3851). critter-shape currently has no mode row at all, which is a 'promised but empty' defect on one record, not a missing lane.

(3) eternal-blessing — there is no per-instance area override, because 15 feet IS bless's printed area: the spell record already carries `baseArea: { value: 15, kind: 'emanation' }`. The only thing removed is Sustain-to-expand ("Once per round on subsequent turns, you can Sustain the spell to increase the emanation's radius by 10 feet"), which is an internal step of an activity the player performs — the manual's NOT-lanes list rules it out explicitly — and which the app never computes: `baseArea` is read only by the heightening display (src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:180, src/rules/heightening.ts:132). You cannot be missing a facility to suppress a mechanic the app deliberately does not model. The clause is the `note` lane verbatim ("a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable"), which renders on feats at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:75 and src/builder/Builder.tsx:1495.

The general premise also fails: subtraction is not absent from this engine. `ClassArchetype.suppressFeatures` plus `armorCap`/`weaponCap` (src/rules/types.ts:779-787) are a shipped subtractive route, applied at src/rules/build.ts:3106 and `ownedFeatureIds.delete(id)` — the app already takes class features and proficiency ranks AWAY where that genuinely is the right model.

Secondary refutation, if the above did not already settle it: the cluster is not one system either. It bundles a shipped additive choice payload, a clarification about a battle-form the app models as a mode, and a note about a Sustain action — three unrelated routes sharing only the grammatical shape 'a sentence containing a negation'. A single 'borrowed-effect-override' facility would serve none of the three: the first needs nothing, the second would need polymorph battle-form modelling built first (a different question entirely), and the third would need a spell-area/Sustain clock the manual places out of scope.

refuted.name: character-creature-traits
refuted.why: REFUTED. (1) The cluster is 2 clauses from 1 record, not 4 — gold-freetext indices 15, 20 and 22 are the identical clause 'You gain the undead and zombie traits' re-emitted under three lenses; index 17 is the negation. (2) The claim 'nothing holds traits on the character' is contradicted by the app: holy and unholy ARE creature traits, and sanctificationOf(c) (src/rules/derive.ts:969) resolves the character's own one out of effectPicks, with choiceOptionAdditions.addIfSanctified (types.ts:579, applied derive.ts:1003) as a record that keys off it — ~20 records branch on the character's holy/unholy trait and all work. The capability 'a character creature trait other records key off' exists, built for the traits this data actually reads. (3) Nothing reads undead. Zero feats in public/core.json carry the 'undead' trait, so the app's only computed consumer of character traits — the feat-slot trait gate at src/rules/featSlots.ts:87-98, whose widening route is Heritage.extraAncestryFeatTraits — could never use it. The 8 zombie follow-on feats (numb, unkillable, shamble, seize, feast, ...) gate on archetype:'zombie' + prerequisite 'Zombie Dedication' and are already reachable. (4) Every named consumer that lands on the character's own sheet already has a field on the very record: zombie-dedication carries immunities:[death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep], and the healing inversion is negativeHealing (types.ts:655, on DefenseGrants so any feat can carry it), aggregated derive.ts:1756-1759 from heritage OR feat OR invested item and surfaced at DefensesPills.tsx:81 + VitalsRail.tsx:744 — dhampir uses it today. All six undead dedications simply omit it: a promised-but-empty defect on an existing lane, not a missing system. (5) The negation is a no-op — 'mindless' is not among the app's 44 conditions and no route grants it to a PC, so there is nothing to negate; audit index 17 concedes this ('Only worth carrying as printed text if character traits are not modelled at all'). (6) What remains after (4) is stripped out is a pure TARGETING HANDLE: the trait exists so an incoming heal spell, an undead-bane weapon, or a 'target 1 undead creature' line can decide whether it applies. This app resolves no incoming effect against the character for ANY property — conditions are toggled by the player, damage is typed in by the player, and every 'If you are undead / If you aren't undead' branch in the data (horns-of-naraga, the-kardosian-fragments, necrobinding-serum, aeon-stone-amber-sphere) is rendered as printed text the player applies. That is GM/VTT resolution, the mirror of the lanes doc NOT-lane at line 159 ('Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet'). A stored trait list would have zero readers. Actionable residue, all on existing lanes: add negativeHealing:true to ghost-/ghoul-/lich-/mummy-/vampire-/zombie-dedication, plus speedAdjust (-5 all Speeds) and an unarmedTraits rider dropping 'nonlethal' from the fist on zombie-dedication, authored into C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\scripts\data\effect-backfill.json so they survive npm run data.

refuted.name: healing-source-inversion
refuted.why:
The lane is `negativeHealing`, and the reviewer inspected the wrong field. It is declared on DefenseGrants (src/rules/types.ts:655) with the comment 'Grants void (negative) healing — harmed by vitality, healed by void (dhampir-style). Surfaced on the Defenses card', and DefenseGrants is extended by Heritage (types.ts:1212), Feat (types.ts:1412) and ClassFeature (types.ts:1609). deriveDefenses aggregates it at src/rules/derive.ts:1756-1759 from heritage OR feats OR invested items, and it renders in two places: DefensesPills.tsx:81-88 ('Void healing — healed by void, harmed by vitality') and VitalsRail.tsx:744-753 with the InfoTerm 'You are healed by void (negative) energy and harmed by vitality (positive) energy, as if you were undead.' It is also an accepted data-patch field (scripts/audit/apply-patches.ts:198 validates category `negativeHealing`). Five records carry it today: heritage dhampir plus items emerald-fulcrum-lens, pierce-the-veil, aon-pierce-the-veil, aeon-stone-mottled-ellipsoid. The claim 'IwrEntry is {type,value}: a reduction' is true but irrelevant — void healing was never modelled as an IwrEntry; it is the boolean sibling in the same interface, rendered on the same Defenses card. The reviewer is likely echoing this project's own older audit notes (scripts/audit/covered-batch1.json, batch3.json, chunks-extract/chunk-123.json) which say 'negativeHealing is Heritage-only (derive.ts:515)'; that was true when those were written and is now stale — derive.ts:1758 reads db.feats[f.featId]?.negativeHealing.

The second half of the objection — 'the package has no home as a single applicable grant — it would have to be re-authored field by field on every record' — is refuted twice over. (a) It has ALREADY been authored on these records via the existing `immunity` lane: public/core.json zombie-dedication carries immunities:['death effects','disease','paralyzed','poison','sleep'], the entire immunity half of the basic undead benefits, and so do vampire-dedication, ghoul-dedication, mummy-dedication, lich-dedication (ghost-dedication carries the same five with 'unconscious' for 'sleep'). Only the one boolean is absent. (b) A named reusable bundle applicable as a single grant is an established, exercised pattern: `sneak-attack` is granted by 3 different feats and each deviant-ability classification by 4 (grantsClassFeatures, 50 feats use it), and for feats build.ts:2843-2849 pushes every grantsFeats target into the character's feat list as a bonus feat, transitively with a visited guard. So one authored `basic-undead-benefits` feat carrying negativeHealing:true + the five immunities + a note, referenced by grantsFeats from each undead dedication, resolves all three through paths that already run.

The remaining pieces of the proposed cluster are covered elsewhere: 'ordinary healing does not work' IS void healing and is exactly what the rendered InfoTerm states; immunity to sleep/death effects/disease/paralyzed/poison is the `immunity` lane and already present; and 'no need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep' is the `note` lane by the lane doc's own definition ('a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable') with the identical idiom already in use — scripts/data/consumable-modes.json carries note:'You don't need to breathe for the duration' on three records — since the sheet tracks no air, hunger, thirst or sleep clock for it to move. There is also no rules engine feeding typed damage in: HpNumpadModal.tsx offers Damage/Heal/Temp/Set as player-chosen modes over a number the player types, so nothing arrives that a sign-flip could act on; the pill tells the player which button to press.

What survives is a promised-but-empty data defect, not a missing system: add negativeHealing:true to the ~6 undead dedication feats (zero feats in the database carry it today, which is what makes a data-only audit conclude the lane cannot reach feats). One genuine adjacent code defect found while verifying, worth its own fix: negativeHealing is aggregated from heritage/feats/invested items but NOT from class features, unlike breathesWater immediately beside it at derive.ts:1763-1767 which does walk ownedFeatureIds — so a bundle authored as a ClassFeature would surface its immunities and drop its void healing. The feat route works today.

refuted.name: per-source-iwr-stacking-exceptions
refuted.why:
WRONG LANE CONSIDERED. The reviewer weighed `resistance` and concluded IwrEntry's {type,value} shape (src/rules/types.ts:310) cannot carry a stacking flag. Correct — but a stacking exception is not a property of a resistance entry, it is a property of the RELATIONSHIP between two records, and mechanic-lanes.md section F already lists the lane for that: `modifiesGrant` — "changes what ANOTHER record already granted", satisfied by `modifiesGrant`. GrantModification (src/rules/types.ts:754) keys on `from` (a feat/class-feature id, "Applied only when the character has it"), already carries a numeric delta to another record's grant (`innateUsesPerDay`), and already carries a display rider that renders through the TARGET record's existing row rather than a second display path (`actionRider`). Thermal Nimbus's clause is verbatim what types.ts:247 says the lane was built for: "a record whose whole content is 'the thing you already have gets better' had nowhere to go and could only be stated in prose."

THE APP ALREADY DOES THIS OPERATION ON RESISTANCES, TWICE, FOR SHIPPED CONTENT. (1) `resistanceLevelUpgrade: 'inventor-initial'` (types.ts:1627; derive.ts fullLevelResistanceTarget + withFullLevelResistance, lines ~1408-1455): Enhanced Resistance is a DIFFERENT record that rewrites Phlogistonic Regulator's `floor(@actor.level/2)` to `@actor.level`, and derive.ts:1533 applies it "to that record as it is pushed — keeping its own name in the breakdown". That is a named cross-record resistance recomputation with source attribution preserved. (2) `armorSpecBonus` (types.ts:2031) plus the armour-spec access `bonus` and `bonusWhileStance` (types.ts:687-690): derive.ts:1689 computes `armorSpecValue(...) + access.bonus + itemBonus` — literal ADDITION of same-type resistance contributions from a second named source (Reinforced Surcoat's +2 on top of the chain armour specialization), and `bonusWhileStance` sources that top-up from an ACTIVE STANCE, which is precisely Thermal Nimbus's shape (it carries the `stance` trait). So "two named sources whose same-type resistance adds" is not absent from this app; it ships and is exercised.

HALF THE PROPOSAL IS ALREADY BUILT. "With both sources shown in the breakdown" is `DefenseSource` (derive.ts:1241-1256), whose `applied: false` flag exists specifically so a source that lost to a bigger one stays visible — the doc comment names the exact use case, and VitalsRail.tsx:89 confirms superseded sources are "still shown".

IT IS NOT A SYSTEM — MEASURED. I scanned every description in public/core-descriptions.json: 19,245 records with text, split into sentences, keeping every sentence containing "resistan". Exactly ONE sentence in the whole dataset asserts a resistance-stacking exception — thermal-nimbus's. Zero sentences pair the word "stack" with resistance at all. The reviewer's own cluster is 3 entries that are three lenses on that one sentence in one feat. A one-record exception with a shipped lane that targets records by id is a payload key, not a system.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN (narrower, and two unrelated things). The number is wrong: gates-threshold / fire-gate offer `fire-elemental-resistance` granting cold+fire at `@actor.level`, thermal-nimbus grants its chosen type at `@actor.level`, and derive.ts:1641-1646 does `res.set(type, Math.max(...))`, so a level-10 fire kineticist shows fire 10 where the printed rule gives 20. Separately, attribution is wrong for BOTH of them for a reason that has nothing to do with stacking: build.ts mergeEffect (~3042) concatenates every effectChoices grant into one `chosenEffects` bag, which derive.ts:1604 pushes as a single source labelled "Your chosen effect" — so neither record is named, and because both resolve to the same value neither is even marked superseded. That attribution bug hits every effectChoice-granted resistance in the game (dragon tattoo, energy heart, Energy Robe), not kineticists. Fixing the arithmetic is a resistance payload on `modifiesGrant`; fixing the labels is a source-naming fix inside a lane that already exists. Neither requires a per-source stacking matrix on IWR.

refuted.name: emanation-statistics
refuted.why:
REFUTED by the `mode` lane (mechanic-lanes.md §J line 124), whose own definition explicitly names "an aura" as a mode, backed by `note` (line 127) and `choice`/`effectChoices` (§G). The reviewer's blocker claim — "an aura the character DEALS has no number anywhere" — is factually false, and I verified every component of it against the shipped data and the shipped renderer.

Thermal Nimbus, component by component. RADIUS: `public/core-descriptions.json` → actions/channel-elements reads "Your kinetic aura is a 10-foot emanation"; Channel Elements is a granted action hanging off the Kinetic Aura class feature (kinetic-aura carries r:[{label:'Channel Elements',key:'actions'}]), so the radius is on the sheet. DAMAGE AMOUNT + TYPE + BOTH POSITIONAL TRIGGERS: `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/stances.json` → thermal-nimbus already carries note: "Choose cold or fire; you and allies in your kinetic aura gain resistance equal to your level to that type, and creatures starting or moving into the aura take half-your-level damage of the chosen type." That is the payload, the type, and both triggers (starts-turn-in / moves-into). It RENDERS: `src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:878-879` prints content.stances[character.activeStance].note in a .stance-note div, gated on the stance toggle. TYPE CHOICE: `scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` gives thermal-nimbus a real structured effectChoices (cold/fire) each granting resistances @actor.level. Notably the app's note carries MORE than the printed text does — the AoN source text degrades to "takes damage" with no amount, and the authored note supplies "half-your-level".

This is not a one-off workaround; it is the established, load-bearing home for exactly this shape. ~20 kinetic-aura stances in stances.json carry radius+payload notes, including crowned-in-tempests-fury ("Creatures entering or ending their turn in your kinetic aura take 2d12 electricity damage") — literally the proposed system, already stored and displayed — plus steam-knight, ravel-of-thorns, drifting-pollen, and divine-presence ("a 5-foot aura emanation … Sustain to grow up to 15 feet", a stored radius). toggle-modes.json does the same for feat-aegis-for-the-innocent (a NIMBUS mode carrying nimbus-area-halving and ally effects), defiant-banner, and warcallers-chime-of-resistance. modes.ts:135 cat-bless does it for a spell aura.

The design decision is written down, not improvised. `src/rules/modes.ts:126-127`: "where it's variable/non-numeric (stances, attunements, apparitions) it's a toggle state with a descriptive `note` rather than an invented number." And the owner has already adjudicated this precise class of problem twice — `src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:86` Ruling M ("an aura you might not be standing in … whether it includes you depends on where you stand, which the app can never know") and Ruling N ("a bonus belonging to something that is not your sheet") — choosing an existing surface plus a positional note over building a new object. A structured radius-plus-payload object would compute nothing (no map, no tokens, no positions, so no trigger can ever fire and no target set can ever be resolved); its entire deliverable is a rendered line stating radius/damage/type/trigger, which is exactly what the note already delivers. The proposal is a schema preference, not a missing capability.

Two supporting refutations, either of which would also have sunk it. (1) NOT-ONE-SYSTEM: the 2-entry cluster is one entry per unrelated capability — an offensive area effect resolved on enemies (thermal-nimbus) and an illumination radius (ascended-celestial-dedication). They share nothing but a distance in feet: light has no damage, no type, no trigger, and no target set. The proposal's own "or a light radius" gives the seam away. (2) OUT-OF-SCOPE for the light half: gold-candidates.json records Foundry's implementation as `Aura` + `TokenLight` — both scene-canvas constructs, and TokenLight is literally a token's map-lighting config, i.e. a VTT concern, not a sheet statistic. mechanic-lanes.md:159 already excludes "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet". Note also that thermal-nimbus has foundryRules:[] and realFoundryMechanic:false — even the mature reference implementation leaves the damaging aura as prose. The one thing genuinely missing is a data row: ascended-celestial-dedication has no toggle-modes.json entry, so its "bright 30 / dim 60, suppress-or-reestablish, allies +1 status vs fear" nimbus is unmodelled. That is promised-but-empty on one record in a lane that exists and is used for this shape (feat-aegis-for-the-innocent is the template) — a data defect, not a missing system.

refuted.name: per-creature-tracked-state
refuted.why:
The cluster is exactly 3 gold entries (2x guide-the-timeline "the target becomes temporarily immune for 24 hours", 1x cornered-fury "that foe is off-guard to you for 1 round"), and both halves are state about a creature other than the one holding the sheet.

HALF 1 - cornered-fury. The reviewer's premise inverts where the number lives. Off-guard is not a bonus to me: the app's own condition data (dist/core.json conditions['off-guard'], and src/rules/conditions.ts:55 -> {type:'circumstance', amount:2, slots:['ac']}) defines it as a -2 circumstance penalty to the OFF-GUARD creature's AC. "That foe is off-guard to you" lowers the FOE's AC; no statistic of mine changes, and the sheet never holds a target's AC (grep for targetAC/enemyAC across src/ returns nothing). mechanic-lanes.md line 159 excludes exactly this: "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet" is explicitly NOT a lane. The app already carries a whole family of these as prose and has never needed a system for them - Feint (src/rules/actions.ts:77 "to make it off-guard against your melee attacks until your next turn"), sword critical specialization (src/rules/critSpec.ts:30 "The target is off-guard until the start of your next turn."), Nature's Precision and Cryptid (src/rules/companionGrants.ts:280, src/rules/companions.ts:147). Cornered Fury is one more member, and its description already carries a tap-through ref-link to the off-guard condition (dist/core-descriptions.json feats['cornered-fury'].r = [{label:'off-guard', key:'conditions'}]), so the player reads the condition inline. Foundry's own pf2e module - the most complete PF2e automation that exists, and one that DOES have actor-to-actor targeting - models Cornered Fury as a bare Note rule element (.import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/ancestry/ratfolk/level-5/cornered-fury.json: key:'Note', selector:'damage-received'), nothing more.

And the "per-foe modifier with a round timer" is not absent from this app at all - it exists in the right place. The embedded tracker (src/integration/CampaignTracker.tsx -> tracker/) applies conditions per combatant with a round duration that auto-decrements each turn (tracker/src/store/combatStore.ts:493 `duration: c.duration - 1`, dropped at <=0 on line 501) and folds off-guard into that combatant's AC as -2 circumstance (tracker/src/utils/conditionEffects.ts:128). The GM ticks the foe, exactly as the rules intend.

HALF 2 - guide-the-timeline. Temporary immunity is a property of the TARGET and is explicitly source-agnostic. The app already ships the rule text (public/data/rules.json, "Temporary Immunity"): "Unless the effect says it applies only to a certain creature's ability, it doesn't matter who created the effect." Guide the Timeline carries no such restriction, so a list "keyed to who I targeted" is not merely off-sheet, it is the WRONG model - the flag sits on the creature and blocks any chronoskimmer, not just mine. There is no PC statistic it could ever be. It belongs on the other creature's sheet, or the GM's notes, or the tracker (which already supports custom named conditions with a name, notes and a duration - tracker/src/components/ConditionPanel.tsx applyFromTemplate/addCondition). mechanic-lanes.md line 163 also excludes "Restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere", which the clause is.

The reviewer's supporting argument is factually false on the data. They say "a use-counting reader expects a counter that has nothing to count." guide-the-timeline already carries limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} (dist/core.json feats['guide-the-timeline'], authored in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json) and draws real use pips through src/rules/featUses.ts + FeatsTab/FeatDetail. The countable resource is the printed "Frequency once per day"; the 24-hour immunity is a separate, target-side restatement. Nothing is left uncounted.

Also note the reviewer's third framing collapses on its own: they concede situational "is one of my own statistics", but situationalBonuses.ts is documented DISPLAY-ONLY ("It is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number") - it flags a stat and prints a when-clause. For off-guard-to-me there is no stat of mine to flag, which is the same conclusion by a different road: nothing to compute, only text to print, and the text already prints.

FALLBACK, if out-of-scope were somehow rejected: this is not-one-system. A 24-hour source-agnostic bookkeeping flag living on a target creature, and a one-round -2 circumstance AC penalty on a foe in an encounter, share only the word "creature". They need different storage, different lifetimes (24 real-world hours vs 1 combat round), and different readers (a re-target gate vs an AC computation on somebody else's stat block). Building them as one system would be a modelling error.

refuted.name: named-derived-dc-statistics
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The cluster is 2 records, not 4 items: 3 of the 4 entries are the SAME clause of guide-the-timeline re-flagged under three lenses (numbers/resources/unmodellable); the 4th is on-my-best-day. The two halves are opposite sides of a check and share only the token "DC", so no single system exists — and each half dies on its own.

HALF 1 ("chronoskimmer DC") — ALREADY-EXPRESSIBLE, and the reviewer's derivation is factually wrong. The rule text is in the app's own data at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json under feats.chronoskimmer-dedication: "The DC for these abilities is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your chronoskimmer DC". It is NOT "proficiency + key attribute + level" from the archetype — it is an ALIAS for max(class DC, spell DC), two numbers the app already computes and already displays side by side. src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:294-301 pushes { label: 'Class DC', value: classDc.dc, ref: { kind: 'classDc' } } unconditionally and { label: 'Spell DC', value: sc.dc, ref: { kind: 'spell', ..., which: 'dc' } } whenever the character casts; both derive in src/rules/derive.ts (deriveClassDc line 438, deriveSpellcasting line 452) and both open a StatDetailModal breakdown. The number the player quotes to the GM is the higher of two adjacent on-screen tiles. The `situational` lane is the exact route for the alias label, and it is already populated with structurally identical entries whose "bonus" is a rule restatement rather than a number — src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2871 powerful-alchemy: targets [{ kind: 'classDc' }], bonus: "you may use your class DC as the item's DC"; line 3030 dragon-transformation: targets [{ kind: 'classDc' }], bonus: "the DC is your class DC". Same shape, same target kind, already rendering. Also, the claim that "nothing DEFINES a new named DC statistic belonging to an archetype" is simply false: that lane is BUILT. `classDcGrant` (src/rules/types.ts:613) + `classDcRank` (types.ts:1539) → src/rules/build.ts:3499-3522 computes dc = 10 + profBonus(rank, level, pwl) + abilityMod(keyAbility) per archetype, stores Character.secondaryClassDcs (types.ts:3388), and src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:805-820 renders a "Multiclass DCs" card showing "<name> DC  <value> (KEY, rank)". That is verbatim "an archetype's own named DC built from its proficiency, key attribute and level, displayed". Scale check: a regex over all of core-descriptions.json for /called your … DC/ returns exactly ONE record corpus-wide (chronoskimmer-dedication), and every other non-class "your X DC" in the data (impulse DC ×7, deviation DC ×2, kineticist/thaumaturge/inventor class DC) is likewise an alias for classDc, which `overrides.proficiencies` can even force-set by the 'classDc' key (types.ts:3271).

HALF 2 ("a very hard DC of your level") — OUT-OF-SCOPE, and unrelated to half 1. Full text of on-my-best-day: "Attempt an Incarnation Lore check against a very hard DC of your level." This is the target number for a check the CHARACTER rolls, i.e. the GM's side of the roll, sitting inside the internal steps of an activity. mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list rules out both explicitly: "Anything the GM adjudicates" and "The internal steps of an activity — 'make a Strike', … 'attempt an Athletics check'. The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane (grantsAction)." The app's own convention says the same in its shipped prose: src/rules/skillActions.ts:765 documents Recall Knowledge as "(GM-set, usually level-based DC)", and lines 229/297/733 treat Crafting/Identify Alchemy/Earn Income level-based DCs the same way. Nothing on the sheet changes with this number — no statistic is possessed, no modifier moves. The record is already carried correctly (limitedUses 1/hour) and its text prints for the player. Half 1 needs a derived-statistic definition plus a display tile; half 2 needs a 21-row GM reference table plus five adjustment constants. Implementing either yields none of the other, which is the definition of not-one-system.

refuted.name: cross-instance-choice-uniqueness
refuted.why:
The 7 entries bolt a build-time legality gate onto three unrelated runtime mechanics, and the runtime half is already built.

1) The "accumulates into a menu" half is not a property of repeatability — it is each feat's OTHER unbuilt mechanic, and gold-freetext.json catalogues all three separately. divine-access's accumulation is "widen the repertoire add/swap picker" (entries 108/110/112). precious-alloys' is "a precious material on an unarmed Strike" (entries 144/148/149 — explicitly 'the material lane is item-only and an unarmed attack is not an inventory item'). energized-spark's is "an elective source-scoped spirit→X damage rewrite" (entries 153/155/156). Strip those three and repeatability contributes no menu at all. A build-time option filter and a runtime damage-type rewrite share nothing but the word "repeatable".

2) Merging every copy's answer already ships. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\build.ts:2708-2721 pushes ONE entry per taking, each carrying its own slotKey and its own answer ('The slot key travels with the feat so a REPEATABLE feat's per-taking answers can be told apart. Keyed by feat id alone, take 2 and take 3 shared one answer.'). build.ts:1948-1951 then contributes one focus spell per taking, so domain-initiate / domain-acumen (maxTakable: null) already turn N copies' N answers into a cast-time menu of N focus spells. Same shape on wormskin (mt 3 → per-taking resistance) and natural-senses (mt 5 → per-taking sense). eidolonInnateSpells (build.ts:3356-3362) is the same collector, deduping across keys.

3) A validator that reads SIBLING takings also already ships, in the pick-a-feat lane: build.ts:2754-2757 — `const already = feats.reduce((n, f) => (f.featId === chosen ? n + 1 : n), 0); if (already >= maxTakes(content.feats[chosen])) continue;` with the comment 'Count against the pick's OWN cap rather than "is it taken at all", so two takings of a repeatable grant can legitimately name the same repeatable feat.' That is literally 'validate this pick against picks made by other copies of the same feat', and it covers the largest sub-family of the 29 records whose text carries a distinctness clause (general-training, advanced-general-training, elemental-overlap, awakened-power, greater-awakened-power). src\rules\featSlots.ts:48 counts siblings for offer-eligibility too.

4) The residue — 'grey out the metals/senses/damage types the other takings already used' — is the existing `choice` lane's `distinct` flag fed a wider answers array. `choiceOptionsFor(options, def, answers, idx)` (build.ts:442-452) is a pure function of an answers array; it has no idea the answers came from one slot. src\builder\Builder.tsx:305 and :340 already perform exactly this exclusion. Wider input to the same function, not a new system.

5) And for all three named feats the gate is idempotent: two takings of silver, or fire, or the same cleric spell, produce the identical sheet a legal build produces (a set union — the app dedupes exactly this way in derive.ts applySplinter, `const chosen = [...new Set(picked)]`). The cost of not enforcing it is a wasted feat slot, not a wrong number. mechanic-lanes.md puts that class of clause outside lanes ('Prerequisites, access clauses') and the app has a designed home for it: FeatChoiceDef.note, 'a caveat shown WITH the picker, for a choice that works but whose printed restriction can't be enforced' (src\rules\types.ts ~1385-1392).

6) divine-access is a promised-but-empty FIELD defect, not a missing system. 93 feat descriptions say 'you can select this feat more than once'; 89 carry maxTakable; the 4 that do not are divine-access plus three Kingmaker kingdom feats. Its `choice` is already `kind: 'text'` + `inert` ('Heroes Heaven's deity data doesn't record which cleric spells a deity grants'). Adding `maxTakable: null` is one field in an existing lane.

One genuine defect found while measuring, also inside an existing lane: effectChoices answers are keyed `<recordId>:<choiceId>` (build.ts:3056, Builder.tsx:1635), not by slotKey — so natural-senses (mt 5) and wormskin (mt 3) share ONE grant answer across every taking, and five takings grant the same sense five times. The repo has already fixed this identical bug twice with a slotKey-first / feat-id-fallback read (build.ts:2719-2721 and :2751); this lane just never got the same treatment.

refuted.name: runtime-resolved-spellcasting-grant-parameters
refuted.why: Covered by the existing `spellcasting` lane (`spellcastingGrant`, mechanic-lanes.md §E) working together with `innateSpell` — and the runtime resolution the reviewer asks for is already the code path, not a missing one. In src/rules/build.ts:4062-4076 the innate entry is assembled as: `tradition = (majority vote over grants/spells) ?? caster?.tradition ?? 'arcane'`; `profile = spellcastingGrants.find(g => g.tradition === tradition) ?? spellcastingGrants[0]`; `keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility ?? profile?.keyAbility ?? 'cha'`; `proficiency: maxRank(caster?.proficiency ?? 'untrained', profile?.proficiency ?? 'trained')`, where `caster = spellcasting.find(e => e.type === 'prepared' || e.type === 'spontaneous')` (build.ts:3898) — i.e. 'could you already cast spells'. That `caster?.X ?? profile?.X` precedence IS the printed branch, so all three parameters are already resolved from the character rather than stored as literals on the grant. (1) The claim that 'the branch that creates a trained, Intelligence-keyed casting statistic for an otherwise non-caster cannot be expressed at all' is flatly false: 36 records carry `spellcastingGrant` in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, six of them exactly `keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'` (spellshot-dedication, crystal-ward-spells, words-of-unraveling, entities-from-afar, oatia-skysage-dedication, classFeature palatine-detective). The profile applies only when `caster` is absent, so it fires only in the no-existing-spellcasting branch, and `maxRank` keeps an existing caster's better rank — precisely Lore Seeker's text. Lore Seeker just does not carry the field (verified in public/core.json: its keys end at `innateSpells`); a one-field data addition, not a new system. (2) The tradition claim misreads what `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` does. It is not the value that reaches the sheet — it is one vote in a per-build tally, and the tally's own fallback is `?? caster?.tradition`, i.e. inheritance from the character is already in the chain. There is no per-spell innate tradition for ANY grant: heritage, background, invested-item, feat and effect-choice grants are all pooled into a single `innate-casting` entry with one tradition. And that tradition is a display label only — spell attack/DC come solely from keyAbility + proficiency (src/rules/derive.ts:455), the tradition-filtered spell picker (src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:291) runs only for prepared/spontaneous repertoires, innate cards are read-only (SpellsTab.tsx:1430), and the tradition surfaces only at SpellsTab.tsx:1518, DetailsTab.tsx:144 and explain.ts:776. (3) Where a finished entry's tradition or key attribute genuinely must be rewritten from the character, `entryRetune` (types.ts:543, applied build.ts:4118) already does it with `scope:'innate'`, and its `keyAbilityFromClass` already resolves a key attribute off another entry at runtime (ancestral-mind, razmiran-priest-dedication) — the exact 'read it off the character' shape the reviewer says does not exist. The cluster is also arguably not-one-system: its 5 gold-freetext entries are only 2 distinct claims, all on one feat, welding a fully built casting-profile lane to a header-label precedence question. Residual real defect, inside a lane the record already carries: lore-seeker's stored `'arcane'` literal will label the pooled entry Arcane for e.g. an occult bard, because the vote consults the grant literal before `caster?.tradition` (translate/see-the-unseen are arcane/divine/occult and sound-body is divine/occult/primal, so even omitting the literal would not reach the caster fallback). Fix = add `spellcastingGrant {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}` to lore-seeker and reorder the tradition fallback ahead of the spell's own traditions. That is a value/precedence defect, which docs/mechanic-lanes.md §'What this method cannot catch' explicitly names as invisible to the promise-vs-carry comparison — not an absent capability.

refuted.name: deferred-prerequisite-validation
refuted.why:
Covered by the existing `grantsFeatChoice` lane (`featPickGrants`), whose implementation is already deferred and order-independent by construction. Both premises of the proposal are false in the code.

PREMISE 1 — "featPickGrants validates against the build as it stands when the slot is filled, so a legal pick that depends on a later choice is rejected."
