The pick lane does not check prerequisites AT ALL. `pickableFeats()` in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\featPickGrants.ts filters on exactly six axes — explicit `ids`, feat level vs. `maxLevel`, `category`, required `traits`, `dynamicTrait`/`excludeDynamicTrait` (class/ancestry), and `exclude`/`excludeTraits`. `feat.prerequisites` is never read. The file's own header states the convention: "the picker is at worst slightly permissive, never blocking a legal pick." Measured against the data: Natural Ambition on a human cleric offers all 11 level-1 cleric class feats, INCLUDING the six carrying prerequisites — deadly-simplicity ("deity with a simple or unarmed attack favored weapon"), syncretism ("you follow a deity"), harming-hands ("harmful font"), healing-hands ("healing font"), divine-castigation, false-faith — all of which depend on choices made after the ancestry-feat step. None is filtered out; none is even greyed. `PopupSelect` supports a per-option `disabled` flag (rendered as `.prereq-unmet`, src/builder/shared.tsx:964), and every one of the five pick-grant call sites (Builder.tsx:1235, 1355, 1608; shared.tsx:2546, 2730) maps only `{value,label,description}` — `disabled` is never passed. The scenario the reviewer describes cannot occur.

PREMISE 2 — "an unanswered slot reads as incomplete." There is no completeness gate anywhere. In `buildCharacter` (src/rules/build.ts:2751-2757) an unresolved pick is `if (!chosen || !content.feats[chosen]) continue;` — silently skipped, no error, no throw, no flag. The pick-grant `SubCard` renders no `lvl-pending` "!" marker (that marker exists only for subclass, umtFeatId, and top-level feat slots at Builder.tsx:1313/1425/1469), and a grep for a save/finish gate (`canSave`, `incomplete`, `disabled={!…complete}`) across src/builder returns nothing. The character saves and the sheet renders with the slot blank.

WHY THE ORDERING RULE IS ALREADY SATISFIED — there is no "build state at the moment the pick was offered" to be wrong about. The stored answer is a bare feat id in `build.pickFeatChoices`; nothing snapshots the surrounding state. Legality is re-derived from scratch against the CURRENT whole build on every render and on every rebuild — `pickableFeats(spec, build, content)` is called with the live `build` at each of the five UI sites and again at each of the three resolution sites in buildCharacter. Where prerequisites ARE enforced (ordinary feat slots, not pick-grants), the judge is `checkPrerequisites(feat, featPrereqChar, content)` where `featPrereqChar = useMemo(() => buildCharacter(build, ovContent), [build, ovContent])` (Builder.tsx:255) — the FINISHED build, recomputed on every change. That is literally "evaluated against the finished build," and it is order-independent because it is stateless, not because anything is marked "evaluate this one last." A late edit that breaks an earlier pick is handled by the documented policy at Builder.tsx:1430-1438: "Warn only — never auto-remove — and respect a deliberate override," with the Overrides "Taken despite prerequisites" ledger (shared.tsx:2042, `overrides.allowedFeats`) as the explicit waiver.

FINALLY, by the classifier's own manual this clause is not a lane: docs/mechanic-lanes.md, "NOT lanes — do not classify these as mechanical," lists "Prerequisites, access clauses, crafting requirements, price and bulk lines." Natural Ambition's clause is a procedural note addressed to a human filling in the CRB's fixed step-by-step creation order; the mechanical content of the feat is "you gain a 1st-level class feat," which is `grantsFeatChoice` and is registered (featPickGrants.ts, 'natural-ambition', with its 12-id exclusion list). The cluster is 3 of 183 entries and all three are the same single clause of the same single feat re-emitted under the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses — one clause, zero records with an unmet need.

refuted.name: timed-states-and-cooldowns
refuted.why:
The cluster is one name over three unrelated mechanisms, and the proposal itself gives the tell by naming three different nearest lanes (mode / limitedUses / dailyChoice). The 7 entries are really 3 clauses re-described once per lens. Each piece has an existing route.

(1) critter-shape (#120/121/123 — 10-min duration, auto-revert, 1-hour lockout). The lockout IS the printed Frequency: the description's first line is "Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape", and the record ALREADY carries limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'} — authored for this exact clause in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\scripts\data\effect-backfill.json. Sub-daily periods are first-class (LimitedUses.per includes 'hour', types.ts:1183) and get pips plus a player-driven refill (src/rules/featUses.ts: isSubDaily/resetEncounterUses; "the app has no turn tracker, so this is a deliberate player action"). "Measured from when it ENDED" vs "per hour" is a 10-minute value difference in a hand-tracked timer, and mechanic-lanes.md's own "What this method cannot catch" says presence, not value. The duration + auto-revert-to-hybrid-shape is the FORM half of the mode lane: core.stances[id].form=true renders an exclusive Form bar (src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:835-881), setActiveStance (src/rules/play.ts:1410) holds ONE slug so entering another shape ends this one in a tap, and the stance note prints the 10-minute limit. The identical printed shape already ships that way — bat-form ("Once per hour, transform into a bat, gaining the effects of a 4th-rank Pest Form") and form-of-the-bat each have BOTH limitedUses {1,hour} and a form:true stance entry. critter-shape simply lacks its stance entry: a promised-but-empty `mode` defect on one record, not an absent system.

(2) on-my-best-day (#125/126/130 — Sustain-to-extend, capped). "Frequency once per hour" is already limitedUses {1,'hour'} on the record. "Sustain up to 1 minute" is not unexpressed: it already ships in this app's data as core.stances['furnace-play'] — precisely, furnace-form's note reads "…until the end of your next turn. While you Sustain the impulse (up to 1 minute)…", and Sustain is a listed action (src/rules/actions.ts:47). More importantly the round clock this needs DOES exist in this app, on the encounter surface: tracker/src/store/combatStore.ts nextTurn() (lines 482-510) holds conditions with a duration in ROUNDS, ticks them at end of turn, drops them at 0, honours isPermanent for "until removed", refills per-round/per-turn ability uses, and line 663 re-sets a duration — extend-by-Sustain is bumping the rounds. It even has a named cooldown lane: "can't use again for 1d4 rounds" renders a cooldown roller that applies a condition named after the ability for the rolled rounds (tracker/src/components/StatBlock.tsx:641-705). PCs are combatants there (src/integration/README.md: pcPaneContext renders HH's own sheet, pcStatsContext feeds real stats). Round-scoped states are not missing; they live where rounds are counted.

(3) zombie-dedication (#24 — daily upkeep). This shares no machinery with either of the above; it is the rest boundary. The printed text says "You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations" — literally the dailyChoice lane, of which 71 already ship. The objection that dailyChoices "records an answer rather than an obligation" is factually wrong: the Rest dialog's "Prepare for the day" button is DISABLED until every daily choice is answered (src/sheet/CharacterSheet.tsx:846-853, title "Make each of today's choices first"), and answers grant live mechanics via dailyChoiceGrants (src/rules/derive.ts:1048). The deteriorated Slowed 1 is a first-class ActiveCondition the sheet already applies mechanically (types.ts:2767, play.ts:895-915).

Residue, and why it is out of scope rather than missing: a wall clock counting exploration minutes/hours on the character sheet. The app deliberately models the only two time boundaries a player can assert — the rest/day boundary (per-day uses refill at rest, item modes clear unless survivesRest, daily choices re-asked) and the round boundary (tracker). Ten minutes of in-world exploration time is GM narration that no sheet can infer, which is exactly why ModeDef.duration is a printed string (types.ts:2534-2538) and why 211 consumable modes are switched off by hand. Filing all five behaviours under one "clock" hides that two are already built, one is already built on the adjacent surface, and the leftover is a design decision.

refuted.name: proficiency-gate-relaxation
refuted.why:
The lane is `situational` (mechanic-lanes.md §J, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts / FEAT_SITUATIONAL), used with targets `[{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'all' }]`. That target is character-wide across every skill (targetMatches, situationalBonuses.ts:3042 returns true for any skill on detail 'all'), and the `bonus` field is documented and used for non-numeric effect phrases, not just modifiers. Three siblings of this very cluster ALREADY ship exactly this: situationalBonuses.ts:246 `"innate-understanding": [{ targets: [{kind:'skill',detail:'all'}], when: "attempting a trained-only skill action while untrained", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]` — the identical printed clause, routed through this lane; :2630 `"keen-recollection": ... when: "Recall Knowledge with a skill you're untrained in", bonus: "counts as trained (add your level)"` — a pure rank/permission statement with NO numeric bonus, proving the lane carries gate relaxation and not only bonuses; :796 starstone-aspirant-dedication (same clause) and :566 halfling-ingenuity. The render path is real, not theoretical: characterSituationalIds (explain.ts:197) walks feats AND ownedFeatureIds (so the investigator's deductive-improvisation routes the same way), explain.ts:554 attaches featSituationalLines to every skill breakdown, StatDetailModal.tsx:106-135 prints them under "Situational (apply when it fits)" immediately ABOVE the "Actions you can take" list the reviewer is worried about, with a "Full text" click-through to the feat, and MainTab.tsx:724 stars every skill row via statHasSituational. Nothing about the modifiers changes. The reviewer considered skillTrained and RECORD_MARKERS and missed this lane entirely.

The "actively HIDDEN" premise is also overstated. src/rules/actions.ts ACTIVITIES has no rank field at all, and MainTab.tsx:301-304 filters it only by text query and action cost — so Treat Wounds, Decipher Writing, Identify Magic, Learn a Spell, Pick a Lock, Disable a Device, Steal, Palm an Object, Squeeze, Track, Craft, Earn Income, Feint, Treat Poison and Treat Disease are all listed unconditionally, for every character, on the sheet's actual action page (the code comment calls it "where a player looks for something to DO on their turn"), fully described, cross-referenced and pinnable. Nothing in the app prevents attempting or rolling any of them. SKILL_ACTIONS.minRank filters ONE per-skill reference panel whose own header comment calls it "Per-skill action lists for the stat detail panel" and whose section label reads "Actions you can take at <rank>" — an authored by-rank reference list, not the app's model of legality, and not a lane in the manual.

The numeric half is already live, so the feat is not inert: featFeatGrants.ts:42 `'clever-improviser': ['untrained-improvisation']` grants the general feat, whose `untrainedProficiency: {levelMinus: 2}` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json) is read by untrainedSkillBonus() at derive.ts:322; eclectic-skill, which carries the identical gate clause, already ships levelMinus 0.

Residual: clever-improviser, ceremony-of-knowledge, deductive-improvisation, eclectic-skill, ive-had-many-jobs, follow-the-expert and host-spirit have no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry yet. That is the manual's "promised but empty" bucket — a data backfill into a lane already in production for the same sentence — not a missing system.

refuted.name: target-conditioned-strike-gates
refuted.why:
The reviewer only checked the two COMPUTATIONAL strike lanes (grantsStrike/GrantedStrike and weaponRider/StrikeDamageRider) and never looked at the lane the manual itself designates for exactly this shape: `situational` (docs/mechanic-lanes.md section J, and the NOT-lanes rule 'A bonus to one specific roll is situational'). SituationalBonus (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:15-77) is {targets[{kind}], when, bonus}, and `kind` includes 'strikeAttack' and 'strikeDamage'. `when` is free prose and `bonus` is documented as '+2 circumstance ... or a phrase' — shipped entries include pure non-numeric restrictions ('you can't critically fail', 'armor check penalty does not apply', 'ignore the volley trait's attack penalty').

Every condition the reviewer claims is inexpressible already ships in that registry:
- degree of success: `chain-of-command` (:2596) — when 'on a critical hit with the chain of command', bonus '+1d6 mental'. That is shame-the-sin's exact shape — crit gate, extra dice, mental type, on strikeDamage. Also `brutal-critical` (:2699) 'on a critical hit with a melee Strike'.
- target creature trait: `demonbane-warrior` (:498) 'against demons' — the very same trait. Also `undead-slayer` (:704) 'against undead ... doubled vs. creatures with the vampire trait', `mountain-strategy` (:481) 'creatures with the giant, goblin…'.
- absence/presence of a named target property: `striking-retribution` (:655) 'against alghollthus and creatures that serve them (GM decides who serves)'; `flamboyant-cruelty` (:646) 'a foe with at least two of clumsy, drained, enfeebled…'.
- level-banded value: `deadly-aim` (:516) '+4 circumstance (+6 at 11th level, +8 at 15th)' — covers 1d6 → 2d6@13 → 3d6@17.
- grabbed/restrained target state: `advantageous-assault` (:507) 'against a grabbed, prone, or restrained creature' — literally zombie-dedication's jaws condition.

It also RENDERS on the strike: MainTab.tsx:402-409 puts a situational star beside a strike row's attack numbers and beside its damage, and explain.ts:944/985 lists every matching feat line with the source's name and its `when` inside the strikeAttack/strikeDamage breakdown. The instanceId is deliberately not used to narrow (featSituationalFor ignores it) with the reason stated in code: 'The `when` clause on each line is what tells the player whether it applies to this weapon.' So the reviewer's stated minimum bar — 'at minimum it must print the restriction on the strike itself rather than offering it unconditionally' — is met by the existing lane, and authored per-character entries are supported too (authoredSituational/ExtraSituational).

Two further routes the reviewer dismissed without checking. (1) `note` on the record (types.ts:235) is NOT inert — FeatsTab.tsx:75-77 renders it as '**Note:** …' under the description, and its own comment cites 'Caustic Nectar's critical-hit rider' as one of the clauses it carries. (2) RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3167) hangs a value+note on an action row; `berserkers-cloak` (:3184) already puts granted jaws/claws there, and `the-harder-they-fall-ranger` (:3188) already encodes degree-of-success + target-size conditioned extra damage ('+1d8 bludgeoning', 'a foe larger than you takes 1d8 (2d8 on a critical success)').

Separately, shame-the-sin is misdiagnosed as a passive rider at all. Its printed text is 'Frequency once per hour / Trigger You critically hit a demon with a Strike' and the record already carries actionCost {actions:1} + limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'}, so it reaches the action list as an action whose detail popup prints the crit-and-demon gate verbatim. Its payload lands on the enemy ('the demon also suffers the effects of its special vulnerability'), which the manual's NOT-lanes list excludes twice ('Effects on enemies' and 'the internal steps of an activity').

Finally the cluster is not one capability: a legality gate on whether a granted Strike may be used (zombie jaws — no number, changes nothing) and conditional extra damage dice keyed to a degree of success (shame-the-sin — purely a number) share only the word 'target'. The reviewer's own writeup names two different nearest lanes for them, which is the tell. Either half alone lands in `situational`; together they are not a system.

refuted.name: level-banded-values-inside-records
refuted.why:
The `situational` lane (manual section J, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts) already covers this, including for strike damage, and does so at scale. 47 entries in that file band a value at named character levels inside the `bonus` string, three of them on `{ kind: 'strikeDamage' }`: deadly-aim ("+4 circumstance (+6 at 11th level, +8 at 15th)"), adept-benefit-regalia ("+2 status, rising to +3 at 11th level and +4 at 17th"), and sly-striker, which bands DICE not a flat ("+1d6 precision (2d6 at 14th level if you'd deal 3d6+ sneak attack)"). The display path is complete end to end: src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:407 puts the star on the strike via statHasSituational({kind:'strikeDamage'}), and src/sheet/StrikeDetailModal.tsx:77 opens the breakdown that lists the `when` and `bonus`. The same convention runs through `note` as well - 23 notes in public/core.json name their bands, e.g. stances/ironblood-stance "resistance 2 to all damage, increasing to 3 at 12th, 4 at 16th, and 5 at 20th level".

The proposal's load-bearing premise - "a static note is simply wrong at 13th and 17th" - is false as stated. It is only wrong if you author "1d6 mental" and drop the rest of the sentence. A note reading "1d6 mental (2d6 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th)" is correct at every level from 1 to 20 and needs no recomputation, which is precisely why the owner's existing 47 entries are written that way. Beyond that, shame-the-sin's own description already renders the full band table on the sheet verbatim (it is a 1-action record with a Trigger, so it reaches the encounter action list on its own actionCost, and descriptions are rendered and pinnable), so the player is never shown a wrong number - they are shown all three bands, exactly as Paizo prints them.

The "no numeric fields at all" objection also misses an existing general mechanism. resolveFormula (src/rules/derive.ts:1330) is a CSP-safe arithmetic evaluator over `@actor.level` (plus ability mods and Speeds), already resolving IwrEntry.value formula strings per character - stances/ironblood-stance stores resistance `"2 + floor((@actor.level - 8) / 4)"` and StanceDef.resistances is documented at types.ts:2574 as taking `@actor.level` formulas. Level-banded shapes are likewise already generic across the codebase: StanceStrike.strikingByLevel ({level, extraDice}[] - dice count by character level), LimitedUses.maxByLevel, dailyItems countByLevel / spellRankByLevel, ChoiceGrant.pickByLevel, critSpecLevel, whileActive[].minLevel, SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel, and Feat.precisionDice.upgradeAt ({level, die}) - which is literally a level-banded damage die stored on a feat. So if a computed value were ever wanted here, it is one field widening on StrikeDamageRider (let `flat`/`dice.n` accept the same formula string IwrEntry.value already accepts), not a new system.

Two further reasons this does not survive as a system. (1) The cluster is not two records - both audit rows (gold-freetext.json entries 94 and 95) are the SAME feat and the SAME clause, shame-the-sin, filed under two lenses; the only other level-touching entry, precious-alloys, is a level-gated OPTION LIST, a different capability that SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel/pickByLevel already model. A one-record cluster is not a system. (2) The number in question is unreachable by any computed lane regardless of storage: it fires only on a CRITICAL hit, only against a target with the demon trait, and only if that target LACKS a special vulnerability - three facts that live on the other creature's stat block, which the manual's NOT-lanes list rules out ("effects on enemies", "the internal steps of an activity"). The feat's own primary effect ("the demon also suffers the effects of its special vulnerability") is pure GM/target adjudication. So prose that names the bands is not a fallback here, it is the correct terminal representation.

What is actually true is a defect, not a hole: shame-the-sin carries only `limitedUses` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:73136; public/core.json has nothing else on it). It has no `situational` entry and no `note`. That is exactly the manual's "promised but empty" bucket - a record failing to carry a lane the app built - and the fix is one FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry, e.g. "shame-the-sin": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'strikeDamage' }], when: "on a critical hit vs a demon with no special vulnerability (once per hour)", bonus: "+1d6 mental (2d6 at 13th level, 3d6 at 17th)" }], plus a note flagging that the printed base die is missing from the source text ("it instead takes an additional damage").

refuted.name: damage-type-substitution
refuted.why:
The proposal's own one-sentence definition stacks four unrelated capabilities, and its two exemplar feats share no implementation at all.

(1) ELEMENTAL EVOLUTION IS NOT A REWRITE OF ANOTHER RECORD'S DAMAGE. The barbarian's Rage additional damage is computed by the app's own single table, RAGE_DAMAGE in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\derive.ts:2255-2298, and that table ALREADY substitutes the type: `if (inst.type) type = inst.type; // spirit / energy / poison override the weapon's own type`. Nothing reaches into a foreign record — the substitution slot exists and is exercised by six instincts. What Elemental Evolution needs is for that slot to read the pick the record already stores (`choice.flag: 'damage'`, 7 options, on the feat in public/core.json) instead of a constant. Precedent for consuming a feat's choice.value inside the strike pipeline exists twice already: `strikeDamageRiders`' `fromChoiceFlag` (derive.ts:2461, live on gird-champion) and `critSpecSources`' `{actor|flags.…}` placeholder resolution (derive.ts:2325-2345). This is wiring inside the existing `choice` + `weaponRider` lanes, not a missing system — and it is the SAME wiring the app already needs independently, because elemental-instinct is hardcoded to `type: 'energy'` and so the app currently mis-prints '4 energy' for a water-cold barbarian even before the feat is taken.

(2) THE ACCUMULATING MENU IS ALREADY BUILT, BY NAME. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\build.ts:2667 carries the comment 'NOT added to takenFeats — Energized Spark is repeatable, so the player may still pick it again manually for another type', plus a restricted sub-choice path for the Dominion Epithet grant (build.ts:2674-2685). `maxTakable: null` → `maxTakes()` = Infinity (featGrants.ts:330), featSlots.ts:36 counts takes against the cap, each take stores its own `choice {value,label}`, and FeatsTab.tsx:85 renders 'Energized Spark (Fire)' per take — three takes are three rows, i.e. the menu, already visible. The only residue is excluding already-picked options in later takes: a filter in an existing picker, the same shape as the cap counting next to it.

(3) THE PER-ACTIVATION ELECTION IS THE EXISTING `mode` LANE. 'Re-chosen each time a mode is entered, persisting only for that activation' is precisely `exclusiveGroup`: one member of a group on at a time, chosen when switched on, gone when switched off. modes.ts:138-142 already ships four variant rage states in group 'barbarian-rage' (Rage, Rage (legacy), Rotting Rage, Wooden Rage); oracle-cursebound has 4 stages, solarian-attunement 5. The claim that 'a mode can flip a flag on and off' understates it — a mode also carries resistances, senses, speeds, grantedStrikes, strikeDamage and spellSlotBonus (types.ts:2492-2522).

(4) ONLY THE SOURCE-SCOPED REWRITE IS FIELDLESS, and it changes no number on this character's sheet. Energized Spark's targets in this app are three computed spirit terms (spirit-striking, greater-spirit-striking, gird-champion) plus the Invoke Offense mode strike; retyping them alters neither dice nor flat value, only the label and an added trait, and only for instances the player elects. Its entire consequence lands on the TARGET's resistances/immunities — the lanes doc's explicit non-lane ('Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet'). The app moreover has a settled, deliberate treatment of exactly this shape: glossary.ts:85, `versatile: 'each Strike can instead deal the listed damage type … of your choice'` — printed on the strike and explained, never computed, across hundreds of weapons. Energized Spark is versatile-for-spirit-damage.

I confirm the reviewer's negative claims about the lanes they named: WeaponRider and UnarmedRider (types.ts:325, :362) carry add/remove/stepDie/setDie/range and no damage type, strikeDamageRiders only ever appends terms, and GrantModification (types.ts:754) has only innateUsesPerDay / actionRider / deityDomainsFromChoice. But a cluster of 4 whose two exemplars need (a) nothing new whatsoever and (b) a display-only relabel whose effect is target-side, held together by three capabilities the app already ships, is not one missing system. It is one wiring defect in the rage-damage type slot, one picker filter, and one clause the app is already right to print rather than compute.

refuted.name: material-on-unarmed-strikes
refuted.why: The `situational` lane already carries this exact capability, and the app ships a live precedent for it. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2780 holds `"adamantine-strikes": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'strikeDamage' }], when: "with your unarmed attacks", bonus: "they are treated as adamantine (bypassing adamantine-gated resistances and Hardness)" }]`. That record is the monk class feature whose printed text (public/core-descriptions.json) is "Your unarmed attacks are treated as adamantine" — the same clause as Precious Alloys, on the same subject (melee unarmed attacks), naming the same downstream rules (resistance bypass + Hardness). It reaches the sheet: `classFeatures` is in SITUATIONAL_COLLECTIONS (src/rules/explain.ts:341), `statHasSituational` stars the strike in src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:407, and StrikeDetailModal.tsx:77 opens the {kind:'strikeDamage'} popup that prints the prose. A second route exists too: `UnarmedRider.add` (src/rules/types.ts:338) merges arbitrary tags into an unarmed Strike's trait list via applyUnarmedRiders (src/rules/derive.ts:3017-3040), so 'cold-iron'/'silver'/'adamantine' can sit on the strike exactly where a weapon's own traits sit. The metal pick is ALREADY stored: public/core.json's precious-alloys carries choice{flag:'material', kind:'array', options adamantine/cold-iron/silver} with maxTakable:3, so two takings holding two metals at once is a solved shape, not a blocker. The reviewer's core premise — that item `material` feeds resistance/weakness/hardness rules an unarmed strike is cut off from — is factually false in this codebase. `item.material` is read in exactly four places, all display: src/sheet/filterSpecs.ts:137 (a filter category), src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx:285 (an inventory subtitle), src/sheet/ItemDetail.tsx:119-121 (a 'Material' stat row), and ItemEditorModal (which writes it). Nothing in derive.ts reads `.material` at all — a cold-iron longsword's material never reaches its Strike, its damage, or any computation; grep for bypass/adamantine/cold-iron across src turns up no IWR-bypass engine. There is nothing to feed, because the consumer the reviewer imagines does not exist for items either: bypassing a resistance or triggering a weakness requires the TARGET's stat block, which lives on the enemy's side (the lane doc's NOT-lanes explicitly excludes 'Effects on enemies … rather than on your own sheet', and the tracker's monster IWR is printed prose, not a damage calculator). With no computed consumer, the material-vs-trait distinction the reviewer leans on has no observable effect — both are strike-side display, which is precisely what the situational and unarmedTraits lanes deliver. What is actually true is smaller: precious-alloys has no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry (grep finds it nowhere in src/rules/*.ts) and no unarmedTraits rider, so it is a promised-but-empty defect in an existing lane — one registry line, the same line adamantine-strikes already has — not an absent system. The audit's own gold-candidates.json entry agrees, recording ourFields:['choice'] with needsMissingSystem:false. (Note: the other three precious-alloys freetext entries — repeatable-with-distinct-pick and the level-gated option list — are different proposals and were not assessed here.)

refuted.name: subsystem-retagging-of-a-grant
refuted.why:
Refuted twice over — once by a shipped precedent of the identical shape, once by the fact that the consumer the reviewer invokes does not exist.

1) The identical re-tag is ALREADY BUILT. `diverse-mystery` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json, seeded from scripts/data/effect-backfill.json) grants a focus spell from another mystery and states the re-tag in the effectChoice itself: prompt = "Revelation spell from a mystery OTHER than your own (it gains the cursebound trait, and casting it also inflicts that mystery's Cursebound 1)", with each option carrying `grant.focusSpells`. `paradoxical-mystery` goes further and explicitly mixes the two subsystems in one picker (`from.anyTraits: ['cleric','oracle']`, note "Domain spells and revelation spells are both listed…"). So the lane pair `choice` + `effectGrant` (EffectChoice.options[].grant + prompt/`note`, types.ts:1029-1040) demonstrably carries "this granted focus spell belongs to the revelation/cursebound subsystem". Domain Fluency is stored the same way (effectChoices → grant.focusSpells, plus focusPoolBonus 1) and simply has not had the clause written into its prompt/note. That is an unfilled instance of a lane in active use, not an absent system.

2) The premise "curse escalation fires when a revelation spell is cast" is false for this app. `CLASS_RESOURCES.oracle.cursebound` (src/rules/classResources.ts:110-123) is a MANUAL meter — kind 'counter', meter: true, refresh 'rest', note "Rises when you use cursebound abilities; drops by 1 when you Refocus" — rendered as +/- buttons in src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:830-874. Nothing auto-increments it for ANY cursebound ability, including the oracle's own revelation spells (the 5 spells that carry the `cursebound` trait in core.json). The only `onCast` handler in src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:1444-1460 spends ITEM charges. So a machine-readable `category: 'revelation'` on focusSpells would be a write-only field with no reader — the exact failure this project already ruled against.

3) Two further shipped routes reach the real player-facing consequence, both source-gated so they only appear for a character who has the feat: SPELL_MARKERS / `spellMarkersFor` (situationalBonuses.ts:3325-3343 → explain.ts:314 → SpellsTab marksFor → the star on that spell's own card, ruling G's "the spell is where the player meets it"), and RECORD_MARKERS with `on:'condition', id:'cursebound'` → recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'condition', c.id) at VitalsRail.tsx:1026 — `cursebound` is a real condition in core.json, and the 10 `curse-of-*` records plus `water-walker` and `lighter-than-air` already express cursebound-keyed behaviour through exactly these two lanes.

Two of the reviewer's supporting claims are also inaccurate: focusSpells is not opaque provenance — buildCharacter emits `spellSources` (spell id → granting record name, build.ts:1907/2486, types.ts:3100), so the app does record which feat granted each focus spell. And the "cluster of 2 of 183" is one feat and one byte-identical clause counted under two lenses ('numbers' and 'unmodellable'); Domain Acumen, which prints the same clause, is not even in the cluster.

refuted.name: outcome-driven-inventory-state
refuted.why:
REFUTED as out-of-scope, on the trigger and on the effect, plus the cluster is n=1.

1) The cluster is one sentence in one feat. The "2 of 183" entries are the SAME clause of the SAME feat (twirling-throw, "The weapon returns to your hand after the attack unless you critically failed on the attack roll") duplicated across two lenses (`resources` and `unmodellable`) in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/audit/gold-freetext.json. No second feat is involved. I grepped all 183 entries for throw/hand/held/wield/return/drop/stow/draw: 23 hits, and the only held-state ones are those two. This is not a lane; it is a swashbuckler finisher's closing sentence.

2) The TRIGGER is off-sheet by construction. "Critically failed on the attack roll" means failed by 10+ against the target's AC. The app never has a target and never computes a degree of success. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/dice.ts is the whole roller: `roll()` returns `{dice, modifier, total}` and a `d20: {natural, outcome?: 'crit'|'fumble'}` where outcome is set ONLY on a natural 20 or natural 1 — no DC parameter exists anywhere in the module, and DiceDrawer.tsx renders only the "nat 20"/"nat 1" flags. Degree of success appears nowhere in src/ except as prose inside situationalBonuses.ts strings. Whether this attack critically failed is a fact about another creature's AC, supplied at the table. That is the lanes doc's own exclusion: "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet." Note the feat's OTHER clause (ignore the 2nd/3rd range-increment penalty) needs distance-to-target — the same off-sheet geometry. The whole feat lives outside the sheet's coordinate system.

3) The EFFECT on the branch that matters is battlefield/VTT bookkeeping. `equipped` in src/rules/types.ts:2979 is documented "Held/wielded" and is a persistent loadout declaration, not moment-to-moment hand occupancy. I traced every write: builder/shared.tsx:539 (player toggle), InventoryTab.tsx:715-728 and ItemDetail.tsx:538 (player drags to a location), play.ts:1142 (affixing a talisman), transfer.ts (import), seed.ts (fixture). The rules engine NEVER writes it. There is no free-hands count (`hands` is a static item property in seed.ts, purely displayed), no reload state, and no ammunition consumption — every quantity decrement in the codebase is a player click (InventoryTab.tsx:354, ItemDetail.tsx:501, play.ts:1190). There is no "an attack happened" event in the app at all. So the app never models the BASELINE (a thrown dagger leaving your hand); its default state is "still equipped". Twirling Throw's normal case therefore produces exactly the state the sheet already shows — zero delta. The only branch with content is the critical failure, where the weapon is now lying at some map coordinate, retrieved with an Interact the GM adjudicates. Building this would add a state the app can only ever set from information it does not have, to undo a state it does not model.

4) And the expressible half is already expressible. The app's established route for a degree-of-success rider on a strike is the `situational` lane (J), whose contract in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts explicitly says `bonus` may be "a short effect phrase" and is "DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number". `doom-switch` (line 2644) already carries three separate degree-of-success branches keyed to `kind: 'strikeAttack'`; ~30 further entries carry "success becomes a critical success" / "critical failure becomes a failure" the same way. A `strikeAttack` entry with when "after a Twirling Throw" and bonus "the weapon returns to your hand unless you critically failed" is the identical shape, and the feat is a granted 1-action activity (`grantsAction`) whose printed text already states it verbatim — which is precisely the lanes doc's rule that "the internal steps of an activity — 'make a Strike', 'you may Step' — the app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane." Where the dagger is between step 2 and step 3 of an activity is such an internal step.

The reviewer's strongest observation is true and is the refutation, not the case: "a thrown weapon's location is never tracked at all." Correct — and neither is any other transient physical fact (hands, ammo, reload, position, target AC). This app is a build-and-loadout engine, not a combat-resolution engine; per-action object possession is a VTT/table concern.

refuted.name: availability-gated-on-live-condition-state
refuted.why: Two shipped lanes already express "available only while a condition is on me"; the reviewer benchmarked against the wrong one. (1) The `situational` lane (lanes doc §J, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts) is routinely keyed on the character's own live condition state: `lifebloods-call` when="on melee Strikes while you have the wounded and/or doomed condition"; `let-death-be-my-weapon` "while you have the doomed, dying, or wounded condition"; `wild-haired-fury`, `deathless-servant`, `numb-to-death` ("while you are dying"), `ankle-biter` ("while prone"), `bloodsoaked-dash` ("while you are at or below half your maximum Hit Points"). Decisive precedent: `lighter-than-air` — when="to your fly Speed while you are cursebound 3 or greater (the Fly effect itself requires the cursebound condition)" — i.e. an effect whose AVAILABILITY requires a condition on the character, carried as a star plus printed precondition. (2) The `mode` lane is the app's designated route for a temporary state it cannot compute: ModeDef carries `duration` ("until the end of your turn"), `strikeDamage?: StrikeDamageRider[]` (exactly Blood and Spirit's +1d6 spirit rider), `exclusiveGroup` (holy/unholy) and `note`. Live condition-gated modes already ship: `curse-of-engulfing-flames` ("While cursebound: …"), `flamboyant-athlete` ("While you have panache: …"), `shadow-master`, `item-living-statue`. ModeDef.duration's own comment states the policy: the app has no clock, the note tells the player what they are tracking, they toggle it off. The same policy is stated for printed Requirements lines at src/rules/derive.ts:699 `stanceRequirementIssue` — "Only mechanically checkable requirements can fail here; the rest are shown as a reminder" — and the lanes doc's NOT-lanes list excludes prerequisites/access clauses and an activity's internal steps. actionGates.ts is a 56-line display helper that stamps a "Needs Rage/Panache" badge off `character.classResources`; it is not the conditional-availability system, `situational` and `mode` are. A computed gate is impossible here anyway: ActiveCondition is `{id, value}` (types.ts:2767) with no damage type, so persistent BLEED is not distinguishable from persistent fire even in principle. What is actually wrong is one record: `blood-and-spirit` in public/core.json carries only its holy/unholy `choice`, with no entry in situationalBonuses.ts and none in toggle-modes.json — a promised-but-empty defect in 1 of 183 entries, fixable by authoring a mode (duration "until the end of your turn", strikeDamage 1d6 spirit, note carrying both routes) or a strikeDamage situational star whose `when` states the bleed requirement. Secondary: the proposal also fuses condition-reading with "a second, mutually exclusive route" (HP-as-cost, unresistable damage), which the same gold-freetext file files as separate needs under different lenses, so it is not one system either.

refuted.name: lane-miss-situational-prose
refuted.why:
The situational lane covers all 35 entries, and the app has no other possible fidelity for them. Verified in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts: SituationalBonus.bonus is a free-prose string rendered verbatim by explain.ts:405 as `${l.bonus} from ${l.source} — ${l.when}`, starred on the stat and clickable to the source record. Of 4,097 authored bonus fields, 382 are not a plain +/-N modifier; the file contains 120 degree-of-success remap phrases, 56 fortune/reroll, 63 ally-scoped and 18 suppression clauses, plus a second registry (RECORD_MARKERS, 112 entries over 19 action/condition surfaces) for effects that touch an action or condition instead of a stat. Neither is described in mechanic-lanes.md — line 123 calls situational 'a bonus' and RECORD_MARKERS has no row at all, which is why the readers missed it.

All four 'authored verbatim' claims confirmed: :2655 hydraulic-maneuvers carries all three of its 'unmodellable' clauses in one field ('range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure'); :606 ascended-celestial-dedication carries 'roll twice and use the higher result (fortune)' AND a second target 'ALLIES inside your active nimbus — on saves against fear', refuting the ally-scope need too; :768 on-my-best-day carries '+1 to +3 status (by degree of success; on a critical failure it applies only to the next attack against you)', covering both by-degree packages and one-shot consumed-on-use lifetimes; :2219 robust-recovery carries '+4 circumstance (instead of the usual +2)'.

Every unauthored need has a live precedent, including two the reviewer did not cite: :2703 cindersoul is authored as kind 'hp' with when 'on the flat check to recover from persistent acid, bleed, or poison damage' and bonus 'DC 10 instead of 15' — exactly divine-health's supposedly lane-less flat-check clause, and 12 further flat-check entries exist; and :3230 experienced-professional, one of the 37 audited feats itself, is already authored as {on:'action', id:'earn-income', value:'crit fail -> fail'}. Others: :2688 agent-of-all-holds and :3248 sure-feet for crit-fail->fail and success->crit-success; :2610 shootists-edge and :2130 masterful-hunter for 'ignore the range increment penalty' (twirling-throw); :783 turn-back-the-clock for 'you must use the new result even if it's worse' (minor-omen); :3222 defy-death for an 'if you have <other feat>' conditional (divine-health); ever-dreaming, evade-doom, uncanny-dodge and eagle-eyes for per-character rewrites of unconscious/doomed/off-guard (ascended's confused clause).

The load-bearing fact: src/rules/dice.ts:74 is rollCheck(label: string, modifier: number) — no DC parameter, sole caller CharacterSheet.tsx:361, and roll() flags only a natural 20/1. The app never resolves a check against a DC and never computes a degree of success for any roll, so there is no outcome tier for a 'degree-of-success remap lane' to rewrite. Player-applied prose is not a workaround; it is this app's fidelity for outcome-tier, reroll and suppression rules by design, and building an engine for them would mean building DC resolution first — a different and far larger claim than this cluster makes.

Two of the eight examples (adhyabhau :100 '+1 circumstance against emotion effects', divine-health :180 '+2 status on saves against diseases and poisons') are authored with only their numeric half, the remap clause absent from the bonus string. That is the manual's own 'promised but empty' bucket — an unwritten entry in an existing lane, not a missing lane. The fix is authoring work plus a mechanic-lanes.md correction (widen the situational row past 'a bonus' and add a RECORD_MARKERS row), not a new system.

refuted.why: The lane is RECORD_MARKERS in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3181 (type RecordMarker at :3167 = exactly the proposed {on:'action'|'condition', id, value?, note}), with a data-field twin at src/rules/build.ts:3277-3290 (modifiesGrant.actionRider -> grantMarkers, typed at src/rules/types.ts:3466). Not a write-only field. Pinning is by kebab-cased ROW NAME (MainTab.tsx:183, StatDetailModal.tsx:12), not core.json membership, so a feat's own granted action takes marks too (precedents: elemental-blast, amulets-abeyance, mirrors-reflection, destructive-vengeance, fling-magic), which covers march-of-law's own row. I confirmed in public/core.json that every condition the cluster needs exists (confused, slowed, clumsy, fatigued, unconscious, persistent-damage, deafened, dying, doomed) and every action row too (pick-a-lock, earn-income, aid, stride, swim, step, sneak, balance, climb); the single exception is recognize-a-spell, absent as an action record - a one-row DATA gap with an established route (scripts/data/actions-additions.json, 100 such additions), not a missing capability. WHY THE CLUSTER FIRED ANYWAY (the actionable finding): docs/mechanic-lanes.md never documents RECORD_MARKERS or actionRider - its nearest row is `note` at line 127, 'a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable', which reads as unpinned prose with no action/condition target and no inline value. A classifier told to judge only from that manual must emit 'no lane at all' for every mark-shaped clause, which is precisely what these 35 entries are. The fix is a row in section J of mechanic-lanes.md, not a new system. ONE BOUNDARY WARNING: other entries in the same nine gold-freetext feats are genuinely NOT mark-shaped and must not be folded in here or the group becomes not-one-system - zombie-dedication's creature traits on the character and its void/vitality healing inversion, ascended-celestial-dedication's fortune reroll and 30-foot light emanation, and divine-health's ally-facing +1 sized by the champion's aura radius. refuted.name: lane-miss-existing-fields
refuted.why: Verified in the codebase, and the reviewer is substantively right — these are reader errors, not a hole. (1) quick-recognition #138 ('once per round' needs a round-based reset, not a daily one): C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\types.ts:1183 declares LimitedUses.per as 'round'|'turn'|'minute'|'hour'|'day'|'week'|'month'; src\rules\featUses.ts defines SUB_DAILY = ['round','turn','minute','hour'] and resetEncounterUses(), whose comment names this precise case ('a once per round feat that only came back at daily preparations would be usable once per DAY — the tracker would be lying in the restrictive direction'); src\sheet\FeatsTab.tsx:431 renders the reset control gated on isSubDaily(use.per), titled 'New encounter — refill every per-round/turn/minute/hour use'. Decisively, the shipped record ALREADY carries it: public/core.json quick-recognition has limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}. The reader claimed 'no lane' for a lane the record itself populates. (2) divine-access #108/#110/#112 ('must feed spell SELECTION, not merely casting; including level-up swaps'): src\sheet\SpellsTab.tsx:270-319 computes the picker's eligibility as onList(s) || added.has(s.id) || opened, where added = spellListAdditions['*'] ∪ spellListAdditions[entry.id]; that memo feeds optionsFor(rank), which IS the repertoire Add picker (the modal's swap is Remove + Add per rank). src\builder\Builder.tsx:434-470 does the same for build-time/level-up repertoire, with a comment saying it was added because the builder 'filtered on tradition alone, so a caster building a repertoire here could never pick the spells their own feat had just granted them.' SpellAccessGrant (types.ts:2945) even carries max (the 'up to three') and from:'deity', and build.ts:3325 resolves from:'deity' against content.deities[deityId].spells — Blessed Blood is the cited precedent and is the identical clause shape. 472 of 485 deities carry spells, so the record's own inert note ('deity data doesn't record which cleric spells a deity grants') is STALE: this is one stale field on a fully wired lane. (3) devout-blessing #133 ('or any other to which you have access'): the manual's own NOT-lanes list excludes 'access clauses' outright, so this should never have been emitted. Insofar as it is mechanical, FeatChoiceDef.note (types.ts:1385-1392, rendered shared.tsx:2535 and Builder.tsx:348) is the app's documented device for a printed restriction it cannot enforce (Splinter Faith's 'up to one domain that isn't on either list'), and choiceOptionAdditions (types.ts:571) is the built route for an owned record widening another record's menu — both live uses target armament/blessing choices. Note the reviewer's field name is WRONG here: devout-blessing picks a BLESSING (classFeatures blessed-armament/shield/swiftness), not a domain, so domainPool:'all' is irrelevant. (4) precious-alloys #146 (adamantine at 13th) is the cluster's weakest member and the reviewer's mapping is also wrong: requiresSkillRank gates on SKILL RANK via qualifiesForOption (derive.ts:1024) and there is no level gate on FeatChoiceDef.options[] or EffectChoice.options[]. But this is one optional property on an existing lane's option object, not a capability: level predicates are pervasive (whileActive[].minLevel, SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel, FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS_LEVELED[].minLevel, OpenChoiceFrom.maxLevel), qualifiesForOption is already the hook, 'legal values recomputed as the character advances' is exactly what kind:'skills' and kind:'open' choices already do (Assurance is the documented canonical case), and the note lane covers the residue. The record already carries the choice with all three metals; the defect is an under-enforced gate — a VALUE defect, which the manual itself says this method cannot catch ('It compares presence, not value'). Net: 5 of 6 entries are covered by shipped, end-to-end-wired lanes (limitedUses per:'round'; spellListAdd feeding the picker's eligibility; note/choiceOptionAdditions for the open access clause), and the 6th reduces to adding one optional minLevel property beside requiresSkillRank. Nothing here is a system. Secondary note for the parent: the cluster is also held together only by a meta-claim ('the reader didn't check the fields'), not by any shared capability — a per-round use pool, a repertoire-picker widening, an access-driven open menu and a level-gated option are four unrelated things — so not-one-system would refute it too; already-expressible is the stronger and more actionable verdict.

refuted.name: degree-of-success-remap
refuted.why: REFUTED by the `situational` lane itself plus its sibling action/condition-marker lane, both in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts. The reviewer's stated reason for rejecting `situational` is a misreading of the lane: it is not "a typed bonus to a roll's total". Its header says it is DISPLAY-ONLY ("nothing here changes a computed number"), `SituationalBonus.bonus` is documented at line ~74 as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE", and `parseBonus` (line ~3384) is written to return null for a non-numeric phrase precisely so prose entries skip the stacking arithmetic and render as a starred line the player reads. Counting live phrasings in that one file: 29 "success becomes a critical success", 14 "critical failure becomes a failure", 7 "one degree of success better", plus 13 arrow forms — 64 remaps already authored and rendering. Every sub-requirement the reviewer calls shapeless is already carried: (1) THE SHIFT ITSELF — magical-shorthand ("a success becomes a critical success (untyped)"), intuitive-crafting, nocturnal-navigator (both directions in one entry), iron-lung and unwavering-mien ("treat your result as one degree of success better"), runic-skullcap, travelers-fulu, hydra-mutagen, cloak-of-repute-major ("success becomes a critical success; critical failure becomes a failure"). (2) DIRECTION — both up and down are live, separately and together. (3) SCOPE = ONE NAMED SKILL ACTION — steadying-stone line 609: targets [{skill: acrobatics}], when "on Acrobatics checks to Balance on uneven ground made of earth or rock", bonus "success becomes a critical success". That is byte-for-byte the adroit-manipulation shape (Thievery/Pick a Lock). The stronger route is the RecordMarker lane (RECORD_MARKERS, line 3181), whose declared purpose is "a mark on an ACTION or a CONDITION rather than on a stat" with `value` = "the CHANGED value, shown inline in parentheses on that row": sure-feet is [{on:'action',id:'balance',value:'success -> crit success'},{on:'action',id:'climb',...}], fishseeker-shoony carries 'success → crit success; crit fail → fail' on grab-an-edge, sturdy-bindings 'crit fail -> fail' on grapple, the-publican on aid, student-of-the-canon on recall-knowledge and decipher-writing, caveclimber-kobold / cliffscale-lizardfolk / paddler-shoony on climb and swim. `pick-a-lock` already exists as a marker id (quick-unlock uses it), so adroit-manipulation has a ready slot. (4) SCOPE = A DOWNTIME ACTIVITY — experienced-professional, one of the reviewer's own six examples, IS ALREADY AUTHORED at line 3230: {on:'action', id:'earn-income', value:'crit fail -> fail', note:'...'}. (5) SCOPE = A SKILL CATEGORY (any Lore) — unmistakable-lore line 2618: targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'lore:*'}], when "to Recall Knowledge with a Lore subcategory you are trained in", bonus "critical failure becomes failure". `SituationalTarget.detail` is documented to accept a skill key, a `lore:*` key, or `all`. This is the exact any-Lore + named-activity + crit-fail→fail shape claimed to be missing. (6) SCOPE = A TRAIT-FILTERED SAVE, WIDER THAN THE BONUS BESIDE IT — iron-lung: {save:'all'}, "against an inhaled poison"; unwavering-mien: {save:'all'}, "against an effect that would make you fall asleep"; bravery's marker note carries the fear-save remap. adhyabhau's objection ("the bonus is Will-only, the upgrade is all saves, so the two clauses cannot share one filter") dissolves because the value is an ARRAY of entries each with its own `targets` and `when` — warpipes already ships three entries with three different targets and three different triggers. adhyabhau is simply [{save will, 'against emotion effects', '+1 circumstance'}, {save all, 'against emotion effects', 'success becomes a critical success'}]; its current single-entry record at line 100 is a promised-but-empty defect in a lane that holds the shape, not a missing lane. (7) SELF-ONLY vs ALLY-SHARED — same answer: separate array elements, and ally reach is expressed per-entry inside `when` by established convention (ghosts-in-the-storm "also applies to allies in your kinetic aura", warpipes "you and allies who can hear", devrins-cunning-stance, pennant-of-victory; aon-vulture even scopes a remap to another creature's saves in the `when`). divine-health becomes [{save all, 'saves against diseases and poisons — allies in your champion's aura get +1', '+2 status'}, {save all, 'your own saves against a disease or poison', 'success becomes a critical success'}]. The RECORD_MARKERS comment on aura-of-courage states the standing ruling outright: "Only the PLAYER half is modelled … an ally's conditions are not this sheet." So the shift being self-only needs no new scope primitive — the ally half is prose on this sheet either way. (8) THE GATE ON OWNING ANOTHER RECORD — two routes, both live. Free-text: 22 `when` strings already gate on ownership or rank ("only if you have the Bardic Lore class feat", "if you have that feat and expert proficiency in the skill used"). Structured: `modifiesGrant.actionRider` in src\rules\build.ts (~3265-3290) evaluates `ownedIds.has(mod.from)` and emits a RecordMarker with value+note into `Character.grantMarkers` (typed at src\rules\types.ts:3467, described as "gated: they are only here because the character has the record being modified"), which merges into the same display path via `markersFor`'s `extra` channel. That is exactly divine-health's Sacred Body clause: crit-fail→fail present only if the named class feature is owned. And the display is real, not a write-only field: markersFor → recordMarkersFor (src\rules\explain.ts:297-307) → rendered on action rows in src\sheet\MainTab.tsx:502 and src\sheet\StatDetailModal.tsx:183, and on condition rows in src\sheet\VitalsRail.tsx:1026, with the changed value inline in parentheses and a `*` back to the source. Two of the six example feats are ALREADY CARRIED (experienced-professional as a marker; hydraulic-maneuvers at line 2655 already reads "a critical failure becomes a failure" scoped to "the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers"), and robust-recovery and divine-health already have entries missing only a second array element. What is genuinely absent is not a lane but a dice engine: grepping src/ and tracker/src for degreeOfSuccess/criticalSuccess resolution logic returns only glossary.ts and situationalBonuses.ts — this app computes and displays modifiers, it never rolls a d20 or resolves an outcome tier, so there is no roll result for a remap to rewrite. Auto-applying the shift is a VTT/resolution-time concern, and the mechanic-lanes doc's NOT-lanes list already puts the internal steps of an activity outside scope. The capability the reviewer describes — record a tier shift, with a direction, scoped to a named action, an activity, a skill category, or a trait-filtered save, optionally gated on another owned record, and surface it where the player looks — exists, is used 64 times, and is wired to three UI surfaces. The four unauthored records are lane-population defects for the promised-but-empty bucket, not a missing system.

refuted.name: standard-action-record-patching
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The premise ("actions the app does not own as records") is false, and the lane the reviewer says is a near miss is in fact the shipped lane, already carrying ~61 of exactly these patches.

1) The app DOES own them as records, with the disputed fields as first-class fields.
- C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/actions.ts — `ACTIVITIES: ActivityDef[]` with `{name, mode, cost, skill, traits, desc}`. It contains Aid (cost REACT), Disarm / Shove / Trip / Grapple / Reposition (cost A1, skill Athletics), Treat Poison, Stand, Step, Leap, Pick a Lock, Treat Wounds, Repair, Earn Income, Gather Information.
- C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/skillActions.ts — `SKILL_ACTIONS` per skill, each entry `{name, costText, minRank, feat, featName, desc, tiers}`. That is the action cost, the entry requirement, AND the proficiency-rank gate, as declared fields. `skillActionsFor(skill, rank, hasFeat)` filters them at open time against the character's LIVE per-skill rank and feat set — precisely the "evaluate the gate per-skill at the moment of use" the gold entry for quick-recognition calls impossible.
- C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json `actions` (865 records) has `aid`, `disarm`, `shove`, `trip`, `treat-disease`, `treat-poison`, `stand`, `pick-a-lock`, each with an `actionCost` field. MainTab.tsx `enrichActivity` joins ACTIVITIES to these by kebab id.

2) The patch lane exists and is `modifiesGrant` -> `actionRider` (mechanic-lanes.md line 88), plus its registry twin `RECORD_MARKERS` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3181), resolved by `markersFor()` / `recordMarkersFor()` and rendered on BOTH action surfaces — MainTab.tsx:502 for universal/basic actions and StatDetailModal.tsx:183 for per-skill actions, the latter keyed by `actionSlug(a.name)`. Shape: `{on:'action', id:<action id>, value:<the CHANGED value, shown inline in parentheses>, note}`. The target is a BARE ACTION ID STRING — no grant is required. The reviewer's blocker ("a universal basic action was never granted, so there is no grant to point at") is contradicted by types.ts:761 in the field's own doc comment: "A rider on the action `from` grants — or IS, when `from` is itself an action record".

3) Every one of the five fields the reviewer says "no lane touches" is already carried against these exact actions:
- action cost: `quick-unlock` -> `{on:'action', id:'pick-a-lock', value:"1 action", note:"You Pick a Lock using 1 action instead of 2."}`. That IS quick-recognition's shape, already shipped. Also Kip Up (Stand as a free action, minRank master), Quick Repair, Quick Identification, Battle Cry (Demoralize as a free action), Hobnobber, Tame Animal — all cost rewrites of pre-existing actions, carried in skillActions.ts via costText + minRank + tiers.
- entry requirement: `feather-step` -> step ("you can Step into difficult terrain"); `stitch-flesh` -> treat-wounds (usable on undead); `fancy-moves` -> demoralize (roll Performance instead); `streetwise` -> gather-information; plus Titan Wrestler (patches the size requirement of Disarm/Grapple/Reposition/Shove/Trip, and scales it at legendary), Pickpocket, Experienced Tracker in skillActions.ts.
- proficiency-rank gate: `minRank` + `tiers` on every skill action; the untrained side has its own field — effect-backfill.json carries `untrained-improvisation` -> `untrainedProficiency: {levelMinus: 2}` (read at derive.ts:326), and `clever-improviser` already grants it (featFeatGrants.ts:42).
- range on an Athletics maneuver: distance values on action rows are routine — `black-powder-boost` -> leap `"+10 feet"`; `dancing-leaf` -> leap/high-jump/long-jump `"+5 feet"`; `fantastic-leaps` -> leap `"+10 ft / +5 ft up"`; `armbands-of-athleticism-greater` -> climb/swim `"+10 feet"`. hydraulic-maneuvers' "range 15 feet" is the same field on disarm/shove/trip, and is ALREADY written today at situationalBonuses.ts:2655.
- the value the action confers on its patient: `magic-hands` -> treat-wounds `value:"d10"` (the d8s->d10s land on the PATIENT, not the actor, and the feat gives no bonus to the Medicine check — the marker lane was built for exactly this); `crafters-eyepiece` -> repair; `the-harder-they-fall-ranger` -> trip `"+1d8 bludgeoning"`.
- the actions named as unreachable are already marked: `the-publican` -> `{on:'action', id:'aid', value:"crit fail -> fail"}` (Aid, patched by a record, by id) and `sturdy-bindings` -> grapple. Even the degree-of-success shifts the reviewer excluded are carried: `sure-feet` -> balance/climb "success -> crit success", `student-of-the-canon`, `experienced-professional` -> earn-income "crit fail -> fail".

4) Two of the five examples are ALREADY BUILT, and one more is half-built:
- robust-recovery — situationalBonuses.ts:2219, save entry, bonus "+4 circumstance (instead of the usual +2)", when "on your save against a disease or poison after ANYONE uses Treat a Disease or Treat a Poison". "Anyone" is the inbound/patient case the reviewer says has no route, and it is filed on the sheet where the number is actually rolled.
- hydraulic-maneuvers — situationalBonuses.ts:2655, carrying the 15-foot range, the bonus suppression, and the crit-fail->fail in one entry.
- clever-improviser — featFeatGrants.ts:42 -> untrained-improvisation.
- quick-recognition — already carries `limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'}` in effect-backfill.json, refuting the "needs a round-based reset tracker" claim; and its core.json prerequisites are ["Master in Arcana, Nature, Occultism or Religion", "Recognize Spell"], while Recognize Spell is itself a FEAT record (`feats/recognize-spell`, actionCost reaction). So `modifiesGrant: [{from:'recognize-spell', actionRider:{value:'free action', note:...}}]` works unchanged today — build.ts:3261 gates on `ownedIds.has(mod.from)`, which the prerequisite guarantees, and actionRider.actionId defaults to `from`, landing the mark on the row Recognize Spell already occupies in both MainTab and the Arcana skill popup.

What survives is authoring, not architecture: ~13 records need RECORD_MARKERS / modifiesGrant.actionRider entries in a table that already holds 61 of them against Aid, Trip, Grapple, Leap, Step, Balance, Climb, Swim, Pick a Lock, Treat Wounds, Repair, Earn Income, Gather Information, Recall Knowledge, Decipher Writing, Demoralize, Hide and Sneak. Missing rows in a shipped registry are the "promised but empty" bucket of mechanic-lanes.md, explicitly NOT the "no lane at all" bucket. (Secondary: the cluster also conflates — a printed-field patch on an action record vs. mid-roll degree-of-success remapping vs. type-and-source-aware bonus SUPPRESSION are three different capabilities — but already-expressible sticks first and covers all of the fields the reviewer actually enumerated.)

refuted.name: effect-lifetimes-beyond-on-off
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The reviewer named the wrong nearest lane. They compared against `mode` + `limitedUses` and never checked `situational` (lane J, C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts), whose entire purpose is a bonus scoped to a circumstance, with the LIFETIME carried in the `when`/`bonus` prose and rendered on the affected stat's popup under "Situational (apply when it fits)" (StatDetailModal.tsx:106-130, fed via FEAT_SITUATIONAL keyed by feat id).

Decisive: two of the three example feats ALREADY carry entries encoding the exact lifetimes claimed to have no route.
- situationalBonuses.ts:768 — "on-my-best-day": targets AC, when "until the end of your next turn after an Incarnation Lore check with On My Best Day…", bonus "+1 to +3 status (by degree of success; on a critical failure it applies only to the next attack against you)". That is sub-claim 5 (a bonus consumed by the first matching incoming attack), shipped.
- situationalBonuses.ts:2655 — "hydraulic-maneuvers": targets athletics, when "on the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers", bonus "range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure". That is sub-claim 6 (a one-shot rider on your very next action, gated to three named actions), shipped — along with the 15-ft range, the bonus-type suppression and the crit-failure step.

Not one-offs. The lane ships dozens of the same lifetime shapes: destined-victory:169 "against an enemy's next attack after it hits you"; scour-the-library:774 "against that creature's next attack against you"; esoteric-warden:776; monster-warden:515; knowledge-is-power:2221 "(ends after 1 minute if unused)"; swordmaster-dedication:2224 "the first attack roll after…"; dragon-roar:2232 "your first attack that hits…"; you-seem-somewhat-familiar:427 "your next attack, damage, or save after…". And a Sustain-with-a-hard-cap (sub-claim 4) at tidal-shield:490: when "once per day, after using Tidal Shield, until the end of your next turn (Sustain up to 5 rounds)".

The clock half is routed too:
- `mode.duration` (types.ts:2538) IS the maximum-duration field. 191 of the 203 authored feat modes in scripts\data\toggle-modes.json carry it; it renders on the pill (VitalsRail.tsx:1071) and as "Lasts X." (VitalsRail.tsx:1168). A Sustain-capped duration already ships in that same field: item-grim-specter, duration "up to 1 minute (Sustained)".
- The 1-hour lockout is already on the record: scripts\data\effect-backfill.json gives critter-shape `limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'}`. The reviewer's argument that per-hour uses are not a cooldown-from-end is technically true but has no consequence in the one case chosen to prove it — Critter Shape's own printed text states the same constraint twice: "Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape" AND "can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour". The two coincide, so nothing diverges.
- Auto-transition into a different named state (sub-claim 2) is an exchange between two toggles the app already has — the exclusive form/stance manager (Character.activeStance, StanceDef.form) plus `mode.note`; greater-transformation's note already words exactly this kind of form/duration relationship.

What is genuinely missing is not a lane but a documented, app-wide design choice, stated in the code at types.ts:2536: "The app has no clock — this tells the player what they are tracking; they switch it off" (repeated at types.ts:521). No lifetime anywhere in this app counts down — not potions, mutagens, elixirs, stances, nor any of the 191 shipped mode durations. So the proposal reduces to "make the existing route automatic", which is a play-state/timer feature request, not a capability with no route. Its harder half would additionally require the sheet to observe round order and incoming enemy attacks resolving, which is encounter state living in the separate Heroes Heaven Tracker, not on the character sheet.

Actionable residue (content defects in existing fields, NOT a new lane): (a) the on-my-best-day situational entry omits the "Sustain this effect for up to 1 minute" cap — tidal-shield:490 shows the wording to copy; (b) critter-shape has no toggle-modes.json entry, so it gets no `duration: "10 minutes"` pill and no `note` naming the revert-to-hybrid-shape target. Both are edits to fields that already exist and already display.

refuted.name: partial-and-overridden-inheritance
refuted.why: REFUTED on three independent grounds. (1) The flagship example is already shipped, verbatim. hybrid-study-spell in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json carries effectChoices[0] with eight options, each whose grant is exactly {focusSpells:[<that study's conflux spell>]}, plus focusPoolBonus:1 — authored in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. That is the effectGrant lane (G, effectChoices[].grant). The clause the reviewer treats as the hard part, 'You don't gain any of the hybrid study's other benefits', required ZERO machinery: this app's grants are ENUMERATED, never inherited. A record names the pieces it hands over; it does not import a bundle and then trim it. So 'import a named subset' is not a missing capability, it is the app's only behaviour, and 'DENY what the reference would otherwise hand over' is the null case — you simply do not list it. The reviewer's premise ('every choice/effectGrant lane hands over whole options') is backwards; there are no whole options to hand over. (2) Where the app DOES have a real inherit-a-bundle relationship, all four demanded operations already exist in one live lane: classArchetype (lane K), src/rules/types.ts:770-822, applied at src/rules/build.ts:3084-3130. suppressFeatures = explicit denial of what the referenced class hands over, enforced by real subtraction at build.ts:3135 (`for (const id of archSuppressed) ownedFeatureIds.delete(id)` — it deletes from the engine's master reachability set). armorCap/weaponCap = per-instance override of the referenced thing's printed proficiency, with the type comment stating outright that 'armor/weapon above only ever raise a rank, so a removal needs its own lane' — the lane was built. slotCap and negative cantripDelta = subtract from what the class table grants. spellListReplacement = per-instance override of a printed parameter (the tradition's spell pool) for this instance only. 14 records carry classArchetype; 6 use suppressFeatures (avenger-, runelord-, battle-harbinger-, palatine-detective-, warrior-of-legend-dedication...), 2 use caps, 2 use negative cantripDelta. Partial-and-overridden inheritance is not absent; it is populated and load-bearing. The reviewer benchmarked against the wrong neighbour — modifiesGrant is the additive-rider lane, classArchetype is the subtractive one. (3) The other two examples need no override because their referenced records hold nothing to override. Measured: 0 of 1,832 spell records in core.json carry ANY sheet-applying field (speeds, senses, passiveEffects, acBonus, resistances, immunities, proficiencies, maxHpBonus, grantedStrikes, abilityBoosts). The complete spell field list is area/baseArea/baseDamage/cast/damageKind/defense/description/duration/edition/heightening/id/name/range/rank/rarity/ritual/ritualPrimary/save/source/spellLists/targets/traditions/traits. So: critter-shape's 'you still don't gain a fly Speed' denies a Speed that nothing grants — pest-form's record has no speeds field, no polymorph statistics, nothing; the same is true of its 'restriction' that supposedly must be lifted. Both halves are constraints on which animal the player narrates, i.e. the NOT-lanes entries 'the internal steps of an activity' and GM adjudication, with `note` as the only display need. And eternal-blessing's 'pinned at 15 feet' is not an override at all: bless already carries baseArea {value:15, kind:'emanation'} — 15 feet IS its printed base. The clause restates the default. Its Sustain-to-expand rule cannot be 'killed' because it is never run: grep of src/rules/ finds Sustain only as a listed action row in actions.ts:47/102, with no aura simulation, no radius state, and baseArea read only by heightening.ts:132 and SpellsTab.tsx:180 to PRINT an upcast area. A per-instance override of a parameter no engine consumes is a no-op. Fallback verdict if the above is contested: not-one-system. The 8 entries (indices 42, 44, 46, 122, 124, 150, 151, 152 of gold-freetext.json) are three unrelated things bolted together — an enumerated partial grant that already ships, a restatement of a spell's own printed area plus suppression of an unsimulated sub-rule, and prose limits on a polymorph the app never applies. The cluster is also built by cherry-picking: it takes eternal-blessing 42/44/46 and critter-shape 122/124 while dropping their siblings 40/41/43/45 (always-on hosted spell at a level-derived rank; ally-facing attack bonus) and 120/121/123 (mode with a duration, auto-revert target, and cooldown) — which are where those feats' actual mechanical weight sits, and which belong to different proposals. Side note on reviewer reliability: entry 41 asserts 'The vocabulary has no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all'; SituationalTarget in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:24-42 has both `attack` and `strikeAttack` kinds, and situationalBonuses.ts already expresses radius-scoped ally emanations as printed `when` text (see viridian-crown line 2104, leshy-familiar-secrets line 2213).

refuted.name: terrain-and-movement-cost-rules
refuted.why:
Covered by the `situational` lane, whose "satisfied by" in mechanic-lanes.md is `situationalBonuses.ts` — the file that holds RECORD_MARKERS (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3181), the action/condition marker surface built for Ruling D. Its own doc comment states the purpose precisely: "Some things change no number the sheet holds... None of those has a stat row, and starring the nearest roll would be a lie." So the reviewer's rebuttal ("situational is wrong because no roll is involved") is a misreading of the lane: the roll-bonus half is FEAT_SITUATIONAL; the no-roll, no-number half is RECORD_MARKERS in the same lane, and it is exactly where movement-rule changes go. Their "nearest lane considered" (speed/speedBonus) was never the right neighbour.

The shape is not merely expressible, it is already built seven times over, all on movement actions: 'water-dancer' (line 3254), 'unimpeded-journey' (3292), 'rite-of-passage' (3285), 'stonestep-shisk' (3287), 'tunnel-rat' (3291), 'wildwood-halfling' (3295), 'feather-step' (3233) — plus the mode 'item-sure-step-potion' in core.json carrying "You can Step into difficult terrain" as a mode note.

The cluster's own two records are the tell. Both are 2 records / 3 clauses (8 gold entries = 2 clauses x 3 lenses for fishblooded, plus march-of-law's terrain clause x 2 lenses), and each clause has an exact built twin:
- fishblooded's two clauses ARE water-dancer's two marks, near-verbatim: {on:'action', id:'stride', note:"In an aquatic or swamp environment you ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain."} and {on:'action', id:'swim', note:"Swimming up or down isn't difficult terrain for you."}
- march-of-law's "ignoring difficult terrain" is unimpeded-journey's stride mark ("you ignore the effects of difficult terrain, and treat greater difficult terrain as difficult terrain").
fishblooded and march-of-law simply have no registry entry yet (verified: both exist in public/core.json feats but carry no marks). That is a promised-but-empty record fill in an existing lane — the cheap defect class — not a missing system.

Both ride-along gaps also collapse:
1. "aquatic environment as a state the sheet must represent" — the app deliberately does NOT model where the character is standing; Ruling M (the singing-shortbow comment at situationalBonuses.ts:~88) settled that a condition the app can never know goes in the trigger TEXT with a permanent star. Environment-gated entries are an established convention throughout: 'tactile-azarketi' ("in aquatic environments"), 'aquatic-pirouette' ("while underwater"), 'endemic-herbs' (five different terrains), the four grades of item-elixir-of-the-peaks ("Only functions while in mountainous terrain"), and water-dancer itself. No new state is needed, and inventing one would contradict a standing owner ruling.
2. "the two fishblooded clauses are different rules" — true, and the existing route already separates them by construction: they attach to different action ids (stride vs swim), so ignoring existing difficult terrain and de-classifying a direction land on different rows. The "X isn't difficult terrain for you" variant is independently built too ('tunnel-rat').

The marks reach the player: markersFor (line 3366) -> recordMarkersFor (src/rules/explain.ts:297) -> MainTab.tsx:502, StatDetailModal.tsx:183, VitalsRail.tsx:1026, rendering an inline (value) plus a star linking back to the source on the Stride/Swim/Step rows. There is even a second, play-time route: setTempSpeed (src/rules/play.ts:595) and the Speed control at CharacterSheet.tsx:956 are labelled for exactly this ("Hasted, Slowed, difficult terrain…"). Finally, there is nothing numeric to exempt: this app models no grid and no per-square movement cost, so a "multiplier on the cost of each square" has no computed value anywhere to switch off — a genuine cost engine would be a VTT/battle-map concern, and the sheet's job here is to state the changed rule on the action, which it does.

refuted.name: sheet-derived-values-and-option-sets
refuted.why:
The 8 entries glue together four unrelated capabilities, three of which already have lanes and live data precedents, and one of which is an explicit NOT-lane. They share only the phrase "depends on the character."

(1) lore-seeker's inherited tradition is NOT an option set at all — nobody picks a tradition; it is resolution of a field VALUE. And the resolution site already exists and already implements the printed rule. src/rules/build.ts:3898 defines `const caster = spellcasting.find((e) => e.type === 'prepared' || e.type === 'spontaneous')` ("whatever casting the character already has"), and build.ts:4065 computes the innate entry's tradition as `... ?? caster?.tradition ?? 'arcane'` — lore-seeker's clause verbatim, recomputed on every build. build.ts:4074 does the same for the second clause: `keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility ?? profile?.keyAbility ?? 'cha'`, so the feat's own spellcastingGrant profile (Intelligence) applies ONLY in the no-existing-caster branch — the exact conditional the reviewer says is inexpressible. `InnateSpellGrant.tradition` is optional (types.ts:1194); the record opts out by storing "tradition":"arcane" three times in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:186. `entryRetune` (types.ts:543) already retunes an existing entry's tradition and keyAbility, and its `keyAbilityFromClass` (applied at build.ts:4125) is this app's established precedent for a derived reference to another entry instead of a stored literal. So "a stored tradition string is the wrong data type" is false — the field is already optional-with-derived-fallback.

(2) precious-alloys' 13th-level option is per-OPTION gating inside a picker that is already built: public/core.json carries choice {flag:'material', kind:'array', options:[adamantine, cold-iron, silver]} plus maxTakable:3 (repeatable-with-distinct-choice, read via maxTakes(), types.ts:1442). The live gate slot is FeatChoiceDef.options[].requiresSkillRank (types.ts:1372), enforced by qualifiesForOption (derive.ts:1024) at both the build site (derive.ts:1068) and the daily site (dailyChoices.ts:51) — 32 uses in data. Haunting Memories is the structural twin: one list whose membership is a live predicate over the character, recomputed as the build grows, pick stored and re-openable, and an answer whose gate stops holding silently stops granting. `self:level >= N` is already implemented three times (whileActive[].minLevel at derive.ts:729, SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel at types.ts:1107, critSpecLevel at types.ts:694). This is one missing sibling field on an existing gate object.
