(3) devout-blessing's "or any other to which you have access" is choiceOptionAdditions (types.ts:571), whose doc comment states the purpose exactly: "A record whose entire content is widening a menu another record owns." effectiveChoiceOptions (derive.ts:984) walks the character's owned feats, features and heritages and appends their additions to the target record's list, keyed by target+flag, including addIfSanctified — additions gated on a character property. Live twice (radiant-armament to blessed-armament; greater-armament to harbingers-armament). In PF2e access comes FROM a record, so "printed list PLUS what you have access to" is precisely this lane; the residue is an access clause, which mechanic-lanes.md lists under NOT lanes.

(4) march-of-law's movement variants store nothing and move no sheet number — mechanic-lanes.md excludes them twice: "The internal steps of an activity ... The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane (grantsAction)", and "Prerequisites, access clauses". The Speeds to filter against are already displayed in the Speeds block, and the feat's one computable clause is already built (limitedUses {max:1, per:'round'} in effect-backfill.json).

Broader refutation of the unifying claim: character-derived option sets that are recomputed as the build changes are a mature, documented capability here — FeatChoiceDef.kind:'skills' is documented as "resolved from the CHARACTER at build time ... which ones qualify depends on the build and changes as it grows" (types.ts:1336), and kind:'open' with from.type of own-spell/own-feat/own-item/own-companion resolves the pool from the character at render time (src/rules/openChoice.ts:108-184). A value-resolution fallback, a per-option predicate, a cross-record menu addition, and a use-time narration are four separate capabilities, not one system; the proposed unification buys nothing.

refuted.name: repeatable-record-with-per-instance-choices
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The lane is `choice`/`effectChoices` riding on the feat-slot machinery, and all three sub-claims already run today. I proved it by executing buildCharacter, not by reading fields.

1) "One record holds one answer set." False. Answers are keyed by SLOT, not record id. src/rules/build.ts:2718-2721 pushes `{ featId, level, category, choice: featChoiceById[slotKey], slotKey }`, and the comment there is the fix for exactly this bug: "The slot key travels with the feat so a REPEATABLE feat's per-taking answers can be told apart. Keyed by feat id alone, take 2 and take 3 shared one answer." `choiceKeys()` (build.ts:437) fans a multi-pick take out to `<slotKey>#<i>`. `maxTakes()` (src/rules/featGrants.ts:330) reads Foundry's `maxTakable` (null = unlimited), and `eligibleFeatsForSlot` (src/rules/featSlots.ts:36-48) counts takes in OTHER slots against that cap. An existing suite, C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/test/repeatable-feat-picks.test.ts, asserts per-take independence, per-take tagging (grantedBy/grantedBySlot/slotKey), legacy-save fallback, and round-trip survival.

2) "The accumulation is unmodelled." False. `character.feats` is a MULTISET and every grant pass iterates it, so each copy contributes its own answer's effects. My probe through buildCharacter with the real content db: Domain Initiate taken twice on a Sarenrae cleric yielded [{slot:'2:class:0',choice:{value:'fire'}},{slot:'4:class:0',choice:{value:'healing'}}] AND a focus pool of {current:2,max:2} — two independent answers, both results coexisting as an accumulated set. Precious Alloys x2 yielded cold-iron + silver side by side; Energized Spark x3 yielded fire+cold+sonic, three distinct values coexisting. Corroboration: src/rules/counterMods.ts:27-60 carries an explicit `repeatable` flag so take-count multiplies, and build.ts:956/1009 deliberately does NOT dedupe languages because "Multilingual is repeatable and taking it twice grants twice as many languages". 35 records in public/core.json already ship repeatable+choice together (139 repeatable feats total) — a populated lane, not an unbuilt one.

3) "Nothing validates a pick against picks made by other copies." The only true residue, and it is one predicate inside the existing lane, not a system. `choiceOptionsFor(options, def, answers, idx)` (build.ts:442-452) ALREADY takes an answers array and filters it when `def.distinct` is set; the open-choice branch does the same inline (src/builder/Builder.tsx:304-306). The array handed in is just the current slot's choiceKeys fan-out, so widening it to sibling slots holding the same featId is a ~3-line change at one call site. The app already does this cross-slot shape elsewhere: Gradual Attribute Boosts computes `setExclude` from OTHER LEVELS' answers and passes it as `exclude` to the same PopupSelect control (Builder.tsx:1798-1806, src/builder/shared.tsx:585-605), and `domainPoolForChoice` (src/rules/derive.ts:867-878) reshapes one record's option pool from ANOTHER record's stored answers. Cross-instance exclusion also moves nothing on the sheet, which is the lane doc's own definition of a lane (docs/mechanic-lanes.md:3-5); and the choice lane already has a first-class slot for un-enforceable printed restrictions — `def.note`, "name the part that is on the player, instead of silently offering a wider list than the rules allow" (src/rules/types.ts:1374-1386, rendered Builder.tsx:344-350).

The cluster also conflates. Each of the 7 entries bundles the repeatability wording with an unrelated per-feat gap that has its own name: precious-alloys wants a precious MATERIAL on an unarmed strike (the `material` lane is item-only) plus a level-gated option list; energized-spark wants a source-scoped, per-use elective damage-type SUBSTITUTION. Neither is about repeatability, and stripping them leaves nothing the machinery above doesn't already do.

divine-access collapses hardest. Its claimed cross-instance exclusion is over SPELLS, and the record collects no spells: public/core.json gives it choice.kind:'text', flag:'divineAccessDeity', marked `inert` with "Heroes Heaven's deity data doesn't record which cleric spells a deity grants". That note is STALE — 472 of 485 deities in public/core.json now carry a `spells` array (Sarenrae: breathe-fire, fireball, wall-of-fire), and the consuming lane exists: `spellListAdditions` with from:'deity', as:'list'|'repertoire'|'font' and `max` (build.ts:3298-3336) feeds BOTH the sheet's Manage-Spells picker and the builder's repertoire picker (Builder.tsx:437-460: "Add up to three of your deity's spells to your spell list — resolved from the build's own deity"). So "widening a later picker's option set, which no lane names" IS named: `spellListAdd`. Divine Access is a data-authoring miss in a built lane (author it as kind:'open', from:{type:'spell'}, picks:3, distinct:true plus a `note`, or extend `from` to resolve the feat's chosen deity rather than the character's), plus one stale `inert` string — a defect worth filing, not evidence of an absent system.

refuted.name: ability-costs-against-resource-pools
refuted.why: Every load-bearing premise is factually wrong against the code. (1) The Mythic Point pool is not brand-new — src/rules/play.ts carries `mythicPoints`, `MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS = 3`, `setMythicPoints()`, seeding in `initialPlay`, and refill at `rest()` (with a comment citing War of Immortals p.76 that it is a session, not daily, resource); VitalsRail.tsx renders a 'Mythic' rail card with three clickable pips, Calling/Destiny chips, a link into MythicRules.tsx, and a note printing the real regain rules. It displays, decrements and restores today. (2) 'limitedUses is a counter belonging to the record itself, not a shared pool an unrelated action can bill' is refuted twice: MainTab.tsx:438 `ActionUses` bills `a.usesFrom` — the GRANTER's counter, keyed by the granter's id in PlayState.featUses — with `disabled={use.current <= 0}`, which is also the blocking-when-empty the reviewer says is missing; and src/rules/classResources.ts is a general shared-pool registry (per-character maxima, refresh rules, meter-vs-pool, +/- steppers on the rail, `resourceFloors`) that records reference by id via the feat field `resourceMaxSet` (types.ts:1518). Its Sanguimancy HP entry is documented verbatim as a pool 'you can also SPEND to power sanguimancy feats' — an unrelated record billing a shared pool. (3) 'spellSlot only grants slots — nothing consumes one' is false: `toggleExpended(play, key)` with key `entryId:rank:slotIndex` is slot consumption, decoupled from casting anything, and `setSlotsUsed` does the spontaneous per-rank pool; SpellsTab.tsx:1063 and :1153 render both as pips with live used/max per rank. The 'prepared slots are index-addressed' objection names the app's own key format — that addressing IS the implementation. (4) 'Two independent costs for one activation has no expression at all' — guarded-domain already carries `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}`, deliberately authored into scripts/data/effect-backfill.json so it survives `npm run data`, drawing battery pips in FeatsTab.tsx; the mythic pips are a second independent tracker on the same sheet. Both of this feat's costs are tracked now. (5) The 'rank chosen feeds the effect's size' half is the shipped `mode` lane: toggle-modes.json `deitys-protection` is the structural twin — 'Turn this on after you cast a domain spell. The resistance equals the rank of the domain spell you cast', duration 'until the start of your next turn', resistance as a formula — and `item-warcallers-chime-of-resistance` already carries resistances `[{type:'chosen damage type (acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic)', value:5}]`, literally energetic-resonance's five types as a player-chosen type; `geomancer-dedication` is a mode explicitly gated on 'after expending a slot'. (6) A rank-scaled cost with true gating already exists in itemUses.ts: `chargeCostToCast(item, rank)` + `canCastFromItem`. The only genuinely absent thing is AUTO-billing (a cost field that decrements the pool for you), and that is uniform deliberate design, not a hole: focus points — the paradigm — are manual pips too (SpellsTab.tsx:1367) and casting a focus spell is never gated on the pool, and docs/mechanic-lanes.md rules it out by name in its NOT-lanes list ('The internal steps of an activity… The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane'). Paying a cost is an internal step. Residual: energetic-resonance has no mode row in toggle-modes.json or effect-backfill.json — a promised-but-empty defect in the existing `mode`/`note` lane, fixable with one authored row modelled on deitys-protection. Secondary refutation if that one were rejected: the cluster is also not-one-system — building the proposed cost machinery perfectly would leave energetic-resonance broken, because its real ask is a momentary chosen-type resistance sized 2x the rank (the mode lane), while guarded-domain's ask is a flat annotation on a pool that already exists and has no numeric consequence.

refuted.name: ally-facing-aura-benefits
refuted.why:
REFUTED on three counts.

1) The load-bearing sub-claim is factually false. The reviewer says "there is no bonus target for ATTACK ROLLS at all". There are two. `ModeTargetKind` in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\types.ts:2431-2440 includes 'attack' (also 'damage', 'spell-attack', 'spell-dc', 'class-dc'), and `SituationalTarget.kind` in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts:24-42 includes 'attack' plus 'strikeAttack' ("`attack` is the legacy spelling of `strikeAttack`; both match a strike's attack roll"). Both are live, not decorative: mode attack mods are pooled into the real strike number at src\rules\derive.ts:2653, :2810, :2921 (and companions.ts:419, :821) and itemised in the breakdown at src\rules\explain.ts:944 via `modeAdjust(c, { kind: 'attack' }, parts)`. The lanes doc simply doesn't tabulate every ModeTargetKind under the `mode` row — the reviewer read the doc's table as the vocabulary.

2) The cited example is already built, using that target. scripts\data\toggle-modes.json carries `feat-eternal-blessing`: `modifiers: [{ target: 'attack', type: 'status', value: 1 }]`, duration "permanent - you may Dismiss it...", note "...radius 15 feet (it cannot be increased): you and allies inside gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls." So the holder's +1 to attack rolls moves, the fixed-and-uncappable 15 ft is recorded, and the ally clause is stated. Same for the rest of the cluster: `thermal-nimbus` holds the holder's own level-scaling resistance as an `effectChoices` cold/fire pick granting `resistances: [{ value: '@actor.level' }]` (scripts\data\effect-backfill.json) with the aura in scripts\data\stances.json; `divine-health` holds +2 status vs disease/poison (situationalBonuses.ts:180); and `ascended-celestial-dedication` already carries the ALLY half explicitly (situationalBonuses.ts:606: `when: "ALLIES inside your active nimbus - on saves against fear"`, bonus "+1 status"). The champion's-aura shape the reviewer calls unmodellable is a populated idiom, not a gap: aura-of-determination and aura-of-life (:711-712, "you and allies inside your champion's aura"), aura-of-confidence (:692), aura-of-preservation (:640), enlightened-presence (:554), initiate-benefit-regalia (:894), exalted-greatness (:196), aura-of-courage as a condition marker (:3196). 224 situational `when` phrases in that file name an ally or an aura. A borrowed, level-growing radius is expressed by naming its owner ("your champion's aura") rather than by a number the app would then have to keep in sync.

3) The irreducible residue - the outbound cross-sheet write - is out of scope by explicit owner ruling and by the lanes doc's own boundary. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\work\rulings\DECISIONS.md, Ruling F ("Bonuses that land on someone else"), decided verbatim: "if its an effect the effects a teamate and not you then dont do anything, if its active to a limited to an amount of time then add mode to the user that activated the thing... but it wint actually do anything" -> (1) bonus goes to a teammate, not you => NOTHING on your sheet, the record's description already says what the ally gets; (2) if timed, the activator gets a display-only mode. Ruling M (DECISIONS-round2, quoted in situationalBonuses.ts:85-90) settles the radius half: for an aura "whether it includes you depends on where you stand, which the app can never know" - so membership is a table/VTT fact, and the app has no positional model to gate on. The stance is even encoded in the data: toggle-modes.json `item-forge-warden` reads "Adjacent allies gain the same fire resistance 5, but that belongs on their sheets."

And the receiving end already exists, which is why no emitter->receiver channel is needed: the beneficiary declares membership on their own sheet. src\rules\modes.ts ships `cat-bless` (m(1,'status','attack'), note "Allies in the aura gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls"), `cat-heroism`, `cat-inspire-courage`, `cat-rallying-anthem`, `cat-song-of-strength`, `cat-triple-time`, `cat-aid` - the ally toggles the aura they are standing in and their own numbers move, at the ally's magnitude. That is where a differing ally value lives: the emitter's record stores the holder's number, the recipient's toggle stores the ally's number. Two sheets, two storage sites, no cross-sheet write - by design, and the design was chosen deliberately, not overlooked. (Even the party feature can't supply the channel: teammate sheets are read-only, and the only cross-sheet write in the app is the GM's, per Ruling L.)

Secondary note: the cluster also smuggles in three things that are not this system at all - thermal-nimbus's aura DAMAGE to creatures entering it (the lanes doc's NOT-a-lane list, "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield"), the per-source resistance stacking exception, and "a spell permanently active at a level-derived rank". Those are separate proposals and should not be scored on this one's evidence.

refuted.name: modifier-suppression
refuted.why:
REFUTED by the `situational` lane (lane J), and the strongest single piece of evidence is that the reviewer's own headline feat is ALREADY AUTHORED IN IT. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2655 ships: "hydraulic-maneuvers": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'athletics' }], when: "on the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers", bonus: "range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure" }]. Line 2655 sits inside FEAT_SITUATIONAL (declared line 84, next top-level table at 3181), so it is live: featSituationalFor -> featSituationalLines -> situationalList -> a star beside Athletics with that text in the Athletics popup.

The proposal rests on a false premise about the lane's mechanism. The file header states it outright (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:11-12): "It is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number." The `bonus` field is documented as "The modifier, e.g. \"+1 circumstance\", or a short effect phrase", and explain.ts:situationalList renders it as literal prose: `${l.bonus} from ${l.source} - ${l.when}`. The lane does not ADD anything, so "situational only ADDS a conditional bonus" is wrong. Withholding is exactly as expressible as granting, because neither is arithmetic. Measured over the file: of 4,097 `bonus` strings, 382 are non-numeric effect phrases and 88 use negation/suppression phrasing. Existing shipped suppressions of whole modifier classes: "armor check penalty does not apply" (x2), "the -2 item penalty does not apply" (x2), "-2 item (the chain's Diplomacy bonus does not apply)", "ignore the volley trait's attack penalty", "ignores the -4 circumstance penalty for not sharing a language", "you ignore the concealed condition (no flat check)".

The range-increment half is refuted three separate ways. (1) The phrase the reviewer says has no route is in the file verbatim, twice: `bonus: "ignore the range increment penalty"` on masterful-hunter (line 2130) and shootists-edge (line 2610). (2) The specific objection - "the offset differs per increment and must not apply past the third" - is already carried as a per-band table by triangulate (line 2769): "no range penalty (cancels the usual -2)" for the 2nd increment plus "-3 at the 3rd increment, then -2 more per further increment (-5/-7/-9)". Also far-throw (2719) "-1 instead of -2 range penalty" and distant-archer (2710) "penalty reduction, min 0". (3) The premise that this is "an engine-computed penalty" is factually FALSE: grep across src/rules finds zero computation of a range-increment penalty anywhere. The sheet has no target and no distance to one, so there is no number in any breakdown to suppress. Per the manual's NOT-lanes list, effects depending on the battlefield rather than your own sheet are not lanes at all.

The claim that "engine-derived penalties modelled as overridable bands" is absent architecture is also false - that exact shape is shipped. derive.ts:1074-1092 `mapStepFor` computes the multiple attack penalty (5, or 4 agile) and any feat can override it per band via the documented `mapReduction` field (types.ts:439-447: `step`, `agileStep`, `whileState`, `note`), state-gated at runtime and surfaced in the strike breakdown. Its doc comment records why: Agile Grace and the ranger's Flurry "printed a number the sheet never showed." Range increment itself is modelled too - `weaponRider.range = { set?, add? }` (types.ts:400, "There is no other range lane").

The type-tagging requirement is likewise already met at the display layer where the lane operates. explain.ts pushes item bonuses as their own tagged line - `parts.push({ label, note: 'item bonus', value: skillItem })` - and mode-derived parts carry `note: `${type} ${sign}``. Because item bonuses do not stack (deriveSkill takes the max), a skill has exactly ONE item-bonus line, so "you lose all item bonuses" points at a single visible row. explain.ts even ships a withhold-a-contributing-modifier-with-a-reason mechanic already: `{ label: u.mode, note: `${u.type} ${sign} - doesn't stack`, value: 0 }`, plus SITUATIONAL_SUPERSEDES (line 3353) which suppresses superseded star lines.

Finally, twirling-throw's real lane is `grantsAction`, and it already reaches the sheet: its record carries actionCost {type:'actions', value:1}, and MainTab.tsx:237-247 lists every owned feat with a real action cost in `featActions` with its full description, so "ignoring the penalty for making ranged attacks within the second and third range increment" is printed where the player uses it. The manual's NOT-lanes section rules exactly this: "The internal steps of an activity ... The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane (grantsAction)."

Secondary ground, had already-expressible failed: not-one-system. The cluster is only 6 of 183 entries because it is 2 records x 3 lenses, and the two records need unrelated capabilities - a semantic bonus-class exclusion on a skill check you roll, versus a distance-banded penalty waiver on a Strike against a target the sheet cannot see. No single system covers both.

refuted.name: character-creature-traits
refuted.why:
The premise ("the only trait stores in the vocabulary hang off attacks") is false, and every consumer the cluster names already has a lane.

1) A character-creature-trait STORE with a live READER already exists. src/sheet/DetailsTab.tsx:407-416 renders a "Traits & size" card whose Traits row is the character's own creature traits, each pill an InfoTerm popup resolved by traitDesc() -> CREATURE_TRAIT_GLOSSARY (src/rules/glossary.ts:50, 267). It is populated: public/core.json ancestries carry skeleton = ["skeleton","undead"], leshy = ["leshy","plant"], dwarf = ["dwarf","humanoid"]; heritages carry dhampir = ["dhampir"], beastkin = ["beastkin"]; and core.trait holds full records for undead, zombie, mindless and skeleton. A Skeleton PC's sheet already says the character IS undead. The same capability exists a second time for companions: animalCompanions/specificFamiliars carry creature traits (effect-backfill.json sets aon-zombie traits = ["mindless","minion","undead"]) rendered at src/sheet/CompanionsTab.tsx:553,566. So this is not an absent system; zombie-dedication is a record with no value in an existing store.

2) Healing legality / vitality-void inversion does NOT need traits and is already built: CharacterDefenses.negativeHealing (src/rules/derive.ts:1264) is aggregated at derive.ts:1756-1759 from heritage OR **feat** (db.feats[f.featId]?.negativeHealing) OR invested item, and rendered at DefensesPills.tsx:81 and VitalsRail.tsx:738. The feat reader is already wired and dhampir uses the field; the six undead dedications simply leave it unset — a textbook promised-but-empty defect, not a missing lane. The cluster also mis-attributes the rules: post-Remaster the inversion comes from the void healing ability inside "basic undead benefits", not from the undead trait, so it never belonged in a trait store.

3) The rest of "basic undead benefits" is already carried by the `immunity` lane: zombie/lich/ghoul/vampire/mummy/ghost dedications each hold immunities = [death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep]. The remainder (no air/food/drink/sleep) is the `note` lane; the water half even has breathesWater.

4) "So other records can key off it" is already served by `situational` with a printed when-clause — the app's established convention for self-trait conditions: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:816 aeon-stone-amber-sphere reads "if you are undead, to Deception checks to Impersonate yourself as a living creature". Nothing in this app computes off any creature trait, own or target's (see gold entry 96), so a machine-readable flag has no consumer to serve.

5) The two consumers left over are explicit NOT-lanes in the manual. "What can target or exclude them" is an incoming effect resolved on the other creature / by the GM. Trait-shaped prerequisites (skeleton-commander: "have the skeleton trait") are covered by "Prerequisites, access clauses" and by design are never enforced: checkPrerequisites (src/rules/build.ts:5296) enforces only proficiency ranks, ability modifiers and has-feat, documented as "under-enforcing never wrongly blocks a legal pick". So "nothing downstream can filter on it" describes a deliberate invariant, not a hole.

6) The negation (entry 17, "not mindless") has nothing to negate: no field or record ever asserts mindless on a character, so a deny-entry would subtract from an empty set. The entry itself concedes it is "only worth carrying as printed text" — and that text is already on the sheet, since the feat's full description renders in FeatDetail.

Residual, and it is a defect list rather than a system: (a) a feat cannot push into the existing Traits row, and heritage.traits is stored but not read by DetailsTab:410 (ancestry-only) — one aggregation line of exactly the shape breathesWater/negativeHealing already use; (b) six undead dedications are missing negativeHealing: true; (c) zombie-dedication also drops "Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet" (speedPenalty lane) and carries no `note` for the no-air/food/sleep clause. All three are promised-but-empty against lanes that exist.

refuted.name: always-on-hosted-spell-effects
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the lane they nominated already has both flags they say it lacks, and both example feats are already carried in live data.

1) `innateSpell` does NOT force uses. `InnateSpellGrant.atWill` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:1195) makes build.ts:4055 set `innateUses[spellId] = 0`, and SpellsTab.tsx:1481-1496 then renders the meta as `'at will'` and passes `pip={isInnate && uses !== 0 ? … : undefined}` — literally no pip, no counter, nothing to spend. Their premise 'it produces a castable entry with uses' is false for that flag.

2) The level-derived rank is the SAME formula, already implemented. `heightenHalfLevel` (types.ts:1206) resolves in build.ts:4029 as `Math.max(base, Math.ceil(level / 2))` — ceil(level/2), recomputed by buildCharacter on every level change. That is Eternal Blessing's 'half your level (rounded up)' verbatim. The combination atWill + heightenHalfLevel ships on 14 live grants today (wildborn-adept, warding-light, halo, patrons-glamour, suli-amir, …), so the exact shape 'named spell, no use counter, rank = ceil(level/2)' is not hypothetical — it is an exercised route.

3) The hosted spell's CONSEQUENCES are the `mode` lane (Section J) plus `speed` (Section D). `ModeTargetKind` includes `'attack'` (types.ts:2444) and 20 live modes carry an attack-roll modifier — refuting the gold entry's claim that 'the vocabulary has no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all'. `ModeDef.speeds` accepts an actor formula, and cyclonic-ascent already stores `{"fly":"max(30,@actor.speed.land)"}`, which IS the fly spell's own rule. `ModeDef.duration` is free text and 23 modes already use permanent/until-daily-preparations wording.

4) Both named examples are already populated, not absent:
   • constant-levitation → C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/effect-backfill.json entry 172: `{"category":"feats","id":"constant-levitation","field":"speeds","value":{"fly":40}}` — the fly Speed reaches the sheet — plus the second clause in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:775 ('+10 status to fly Speed while your Psyche is Unleashed').
   • eternal-blessing → live in public/core.json as `modes['feat-eternal-blessing']` (authored at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/toggle-modes.json:869): gated `feats:['eternal-blessing']`, `modifiers:[{target:'attack',type:'status',value:1}]`, `duration:'permanent — you may Dismiss it, and it returns automatically after 1 minute'`, and a note recording the ceil(level/2) rank and the fixed 15-foot radius.

The residual asks fail on their own terms. 'Exposed to counteract/dispel' is not a sheet capability the app withholds — no effect from any source in this app carries a counteract handle, because a dispel is the GM removing the effect, and the app's route for that already exists and is the correct one: the mode is dismissible, which is precisely what Eternal Blessing's own 'You can Dismiss the spell' clause and a successful dispel both do.

Secondary (would also stick, weaker): `not-one-system`. The two examples share only the prose framing 'you are constantly under spell X'; their actual payloads are unrelated capabilities running through different engines — a fly Speed through deriveSpeeds, and an ally-facing status bonus to attack rolls through the modes/ally-effects path. No shared machinery would be built by treating them as one system.

refuted.name: mythic-proficiency-tier
refuted.why:
The lane is `situational` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), and it is already carrying this exact capability on 23 live records. The reviewer compared against the wrong neighbour: rankUpgrade/proficiencies are indeed useless here, but mechanic-lanes.md's own NOT-lanes rule sends this text to situational — 'A bonus to one specific roll is `situational`, not a flat bonus.' Mythic proficiency (War of Immortals p.76, verified in the local AoN mirror at C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/rules/rules-3322.json) is a proficiency bonus of level+10 that 'you use only when an ability tells you to' and that normally costs a Mythic Point — i.e. an opt-in, point-costed substitution on one named check. That is the definition of the situational lane's remit.

Evidence it is already expressed, not merely expressible: 23 entries in FEAT_SITUATIONAL carry the literal phrase 'mythic proficiency', including all 18 mythic callings and five mythic feats — acrobats-calling, artisans-calling, bookkeepers-calling, caretakers-calling, demagogues-calling, doomsayers-calling, dreamers-calling, echoes-of-the-scrolls/-spells/-swords, handlers-calling, hunters-calling, runelords-calling, sagas-calling, sages-calling, thespians-calling, thiefs-calling, guardians-calling, plus avoid-fates-gaze, become-shadow, binds-that-tie, steadfast-grip, prescient-parry. Each names the exact skill(s) in `targets`, the exact check in `when` ('to Balance, Maneuver in Flight, or Tumble Through, spending a Mythic Point'), and 'attempt the check at mythic proficiency' in `bonus`. I confirmed all of those ids resolve in public/core.json (feats or classFeatures), and SITUATIONAL_COLLECTIONS in src/rules/explain.ts includes classFeatures, with derive.ts:2130 explicitly adding build.mythicCalling to ownedFeatureIds so the calling entries do reach the sheet. Same architecture handles the sibling case of a rule that changes HOW you roll rather than the number: starsong-nectar stores 'roll two d20s, take the higher (fortune)' as situational prose. guardians-calling is the closest analogue — same Beast Lord/mythic family, same clause shape, already filed.

The two claimed requirements both dissolve. (a) 'A tier beyond legendary in the ladder': PROFICIENCY_RANKS ends at legendary correctly. That array drives stepRank/maxRank/skillIncreaseCap and the builder's rank pill — it models ranks a character HAS in a statistic. The printed rule says mythic proficiency is unlike the other ranks precisely in that you never hold it; adding 'mythic' as a sixth rung would let skill increases and rank caps step into it, which would be a defect. The absence is a correct absence, not a hole. (b) 'A per-check override that never touches the skill': that is what situational is, by contract — it flags the stat with a star and prints the condition in the stat popup without moving the computed number.

The companion half is settled precedent, not an unbuilt system. Ruling N is recorded inline above artillerist-dedication: 'a bonus belonging to something that is not your sheet… the owner chose a single Crafting star whose note covers all four, over building a marker surface on the siege weapon's companion block.' mythic-allies does the same for a summoned creature's attack/AC/saves. A companion's skill list is a fixed UNIVERSAL_SKILLS + type.skills set (companions.ts ~line 472) that does not include Diplomacy at all, so Gather Information has no row there to override — and the owner has already ruled how such a bonus surfaces.

Two further weaknesses. The cluster is not 4 records: all four entries (indices 76, 77, 82, 85 of gold-freetext.json) are the SAME feat, guarded-domain, and three of the four are the same single sentence seen through the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses. One record, two clauses. And the sibling rows in that same cluster assert 'nothing expresses mythic points' (indices 78/83/86), which is demonstrably false — MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS and setMythicPoints live in src/rules/play.ts and render as clickable pips in src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:958, with src/rules/mythic.ts + src/sheet/MythicRules.tsx carrying destinies, slot rules and the reference page. The auditor was not reading the app.

What is actually true: guarded-domain has no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry (its only authored field is limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}, at scripts/data/effect-backfill.json index 1302). That is a promised-but-empty defect in an existing lane — a one-line entry in the shape of guardians-calling — not a missing system.

refuted.name: named-place-attunement
refuted.why:
Covered by the `mode` lane (section J) plus `note`, and the reviewer's three objections to `mode` are factually inverted by the code.

(1) "Not a pick from a printed enumeration — the value is typed in." User-created modes ARE player-authored: C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:277 is a free-text `Mode name` input ("Guarded Domain — Sandpoint, 5-mile radius"), scoped per character or device-wide via `charId` (src/rules/types.ts:2458 ModeDef). Longer authored prose has a second home: NotePage (src/rules/types.ts:3156) — titled, icon'd, rich-text, with a `private` flag so it can be shared with the party.

(2) "It expires on elapsed in-world time, not on rest and not on a click." This is backwards. src/rules/play.ts rest() filters activeModes to item-driven modes only, with the comment "Modes the player toggled themselves are left alone — those are theirs to manage", and activeModes survives playForRebuild (play.ts:1505). A user mode is exactly a state that does NOT expire nightly and persists until a human clears it — the only lane in the app with that lifetime. As for the calendar expiry itself: nothing in this app tracks in-world date, travel, or downtime weeks (grep `downtime` finds only the downtime-activity catalogue in src/rules/actions.ts and skillActions.ts — no clock). Whether you spent "more than 1 month outside your domain", whether you got "1 week of downtime" in the place, and whether a creature has been inside "for at least 1 hour" are facts held by the GM's campaign timeline. The lanes doc's NOT-lanes list explicitly excludes GM-adjudicated exploration outcomes, so that clause is `note` (rendered on feats since 2026-08-06), not a new engine.

(3) "Single-slot exclusivity resembles stances but stances carry no authored value." ModeDef.exclusiveGroup (types.ts:2467) is enforced in toggleMode (play.ts:1401-1403) and again on rebuild (play.ts:946-947): activating one member deactivates the others — literally "selecting a new guarded domain immediately ends your protection over the previous". And the mode carries the authored value: its own name. "Shared with the companion" is also already there — companion activeModes are keyed per companion id (play.ts:102), and a beast lord's united companion lives on the same character record anyway (CompanionsTab), so this is not a cross-sheet requirement.

The premise "which later clauses dereference" does not survive inspection of the record. public/core.json + core-descriptions.json for `guarded-domain` (level 14, beast-lord archetype, already carrying `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}`): the two downstream clauses are (a) Gather Information at mythic proficiency, gated on presence in the domain, and (b) a 1/day 3-action teleport within the domain costing a Mythic Point. The place's NAME and RADIUS feed no modifier, DC, roll, or resource anywhere — the numeric asks in those clauses are the separate mythic-proficiency and mythic-point proposals (gold-freetext entries 76-78, 82-83, 85-86), and the missing action is `grantsActions`, an existing lane sitting empty (a promised-but-empty defect). Per the lanes doc's own definition — a lane turns printed text into "something that moves on the character sheet" — a typed place name moves nothing, so it needs storage, not an engine, and it has two storage homes.

Supporting: the app already HAS a persistent single-slot designation that later clauses genuinely dereference — ItemDesignation ('innovation' | 'weapon-implement' | 'bonded' | 'ikon' | 'rune-source', types.ts:2933), built precisely because "your innovation…" clauses needed a pointer to a modelled entity. It exists for inventory items because items are entities the calc layer reads. core.json has no settlement/location entity and no clause would compute from one.

Finally, the cluster is overstated: gold-freetext entries 79, 80, 81 and 84 are all the SAME feat, guarded-domain, seen through two lenses (resources x3, unmodellable x1). "4 of 183" is one record. A dataset-wide scan for place-attunement text (5-mile radius / guarded domain / re-attune) returns only guarded-domain and the Doomsday Door item, whose attunement destroys a location — an off-sheet world effect, i.e. GM material.

refuted.name: roll-outcome-driven-state
refuted.why:
The 4 entries are 2 feats (gold-freetext.json #49/#51 twirling-throw, #172/#173 inspire-imitation), and they demand two machines with zero overlap. Half A needs a rider on a general action's entry conditions, keyed by skill. Half B needs encounter-time physical location of one inventory object. Building either buys nothing toward the other; the only shared thing is the word 'critically' in the prose. Each half also fails on its own.

HALF A (inspire-imitation) is ALREADY EXPRESSIBLE, via a route the reviewer's survey missed: RECORD_MARKERS in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3167-3211 — declared for exactly this case ('Some things change no number the sheet holds'), keyed by owned-record id like FEAT_SITUATIONAL, and rendered live at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:502 (inline '(value)' + star + the note in the tooltip), src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:183, src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1026. Two precedents sit in it already: 'the-publican' carries {on:'action', id:'aid', value:'crit fail -> fail'} — a degree-of-success rider on the very same Aid row — and 'quick-unlock' rewrites an action's cost ('You Pick a Lock using 1 action instead of 2'), i.e. altering another action's usage terms is a built lane, not a missing one. And Aid is a curated row on every sheet (src/rules/actions.ts:42) whose own printed text states the prerequisite this feat waives: 'After preparing on a prior turn, attempt a DC 15 check...'. So Inspire Imitation is {on:'action', id:'aid', value:'no Prepare needed', note:'...with the skill you just critically succeeded at'} — landing on an existing row, clickable back to the feat.

The cluster's stated premise is also factually wrong. 'situational is a modifier the character brings TO a roll... No lane produces state from a result' is refuted by dozens of live FEAT_SITUATIONAL entries whose `when` IS a resolved roll's outcome that persists and is matched later, keyed by skill/target/duration: resounding-bravery ('for 1 minute after you critically succeed at a Will save'), monster-hunter ('prey you critically identified with Recall Knowledge, once per day per creature'), phenoms-verve, bestiary-scholar, daredevils-gambit, combat-assessment ('right after a critical hit'), unending-subsistence ('for 24 hours after you critically succeed at Subsist'), equitable-defense ('the creature that critically hit you' — someone else's roll), relentless-disarm (keyed to succeeded-but-not-critically, per creature), firebrand-braggart-dedication (a bonus branch after a successful boast AND a penalty branch after a failed one). Plus src/rules/modes.ts:134 'appliesWhen: an ally successfully Aids this check'. The lane never COMPUTES the trigger — its header states it is display-only by design — it stars the affected surface and prints the resolved-roll trigger where the player reads it. That is a design position, not an absent capability. And a stored per-skill crit flag would have exactly one consumer, the sentence itself: the waived step is gated nowhere (core.json's `aid` record carries no requirements field), so the flag would move no number.

HALF B (twirling-throw's 'returns to your hand unless you critically failed') is out of scope. Held/wielded state is one player-toggled boolean, inv.equipped (src/rules/types.ts:2979), which wielding derives from (src/rules/derive.ts:1930); nothing in the app ever takes a weapon out of your hands — no throw unequips anything, and no ammunition is consumed per shot anywhere. So on a success (the normal case) the clause asks for the state the sheet ALREADY shows. On a critical failure the ask is 'the dagger is on the floor 30 feet away' — mid-encounter object position, which is the baseline rule for every thrown weapon in the game and is tracked for none of them. That is the manual's own excluded category (battlefield state; 'the app lists the action, the player performs it') and a VTT/encounter-map concern, not a sheet capability this feat uniquely needs.

refuted.name: crit-threshold-widening
refuted.why: The `situational` lane with `targets: [{kind: 'strikeAttack'}]` already carries this exact mechanic, and it is already shipped for two other records with the same wording INCLUDING the success-qualifier the reviewer says nothing can express. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2755 — "savage-critical": strikeAttack, when "with a weapon or unarmed attack you have legendary proficiency in", bonus "a natural 19 that would be a success is a critical success instead". src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2853 — "keen-flair": strikeAttack, bonus "a 19 on the die that succeeds becomes a critical success". The reviewer's three stated objections all fail against the code. (1) "It is not a bonus, so situational is the wrong home" — the lane's own type doc, situationalBonuses.ts:73-74, defines `bonus` as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', or a short effect phrase", and the lane is documented as DISPLAY-ONLY ("nothing here changes a computed number", lines 10-12). Non-numeric rule text is the lane's designed payload: compliant-gold (line 2706) is a strikeAttack entry whose whole content is a trait grant, ceremony-of-strengthened-hand (2702) grants shove/trip, leap-the-falls (2746) grants two skill feats. (2) "Nothing in the vocabulary expresses a result-step shift" — 88 lines in that same file already do, e.g. nocturnal-navigator (2507) "success becomes a critical success, critical failure becomes a failure", iron-lung (2739), unwavering-mien (2770), magical-shorthand (2496), steadying-stone (609). (3) "Filing it as a remap would wrongly let a failure become a crit" — the lane stores prose that names its own from-tier, so the qualifier survives verbatim; both shipped entries state it, and Branched Tree's own second sentence ("This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure") is simply part of the string. The per-weapon binding is also already routed: sibling ikon immanences scope in prose (compliant-gold, "with the imbued melee weapon"; barrows-edge 2806; gleaming-blade 2840; starshot 2883), and a per-instance route exists too — explain.ts:243 reads db.items[inv.itemId].situational for equipped/worn/invested items and ItemEditorModal.tsx:239 exposes strikeAttack as an authorable target. Display is live, not hypothetical: MainTab.tsx:402 stars the strike's attack row via statHasSituational({kind:'strikeAttack', instanceId}), and StrikeDetailModal.tsx:64 opens the popup that lists when/bonus with source attribution. Separately, the demand that "the +10-over-DC route and the natural-19 route be evaluated as two independent paths" is unreachable for ANY roll in this app and so cannot distinguish a new system: src/rules/dice.ts exposes rollCheck(label, modifier) with no DC parameter, no file under src/ holds a target AC or DC, and DiceDrawer.tsx:193 only prints a cosmetic "nat 20" flag — the app never adjudicates degree of success, not even for the core natural-20 rule. What is actually missing is content, not capability: Branched Tree of Pain's only authored effect is grantsClassFeatures: ["plant-thirty-barbs"] in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, and the `keen` rune (public/core.json, printed text word-for-word identical) likewise has no situational entry. The fix is two authored rows in the existing table alongside savage-critical and keen-flair, not a new system. Note also the cluster is 3 of 183 entries but all three are the same feat (gold-freetext.json indices 1, 3, 5, lenses numbers/resources/unmodellable) — one record seen three times, and the app's two nearest siblings for that record are already built.

refuted.name: roll-procedure-overrides
refuted.why:
The `situational` lane (J in the manual) already holds this, and one of the three examples is already shipping through it. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:606 carries "ascended-celestial-dedication": targets save/will, when "once per hour, on a Will saving throw", bonus "roll twice and use the higher result (fortune)" — plus limitedUses {max:1,per:'hour'} in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. It lights the star on Will and prints that line in the Will popup today.

The reviewer's premise is contradicted by the lane's own contract. `SituationalBonus.bonus` is documented (situationalBonuses.ts:79) as "The modifier, e.g. \"+1 circumstance\", OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE", and `SituationalLine.bonus` (line 3139) as "As printed: \"+2 circumstance\", \"-1 status\", or a phrase like \"roll d10s instead of d8s\"". The lane is explicitly DISPLAY-ONLY (header comment: "nothing here changes a computed number"), so a magnitude was never required. Both consumers are built for magnitudeless entries: `poolSituationalLines` (line 3406) comments "an unparseable bonus has no magnitude to compare" and returns key===null, which is unconditionally KEPT — a no-number phrase can never be stacking-suppressed; and `hasFeatSituational` (line 3432), which drives the `*` cue, needs only a target match. 15 live records already store a pure roll-procedure phrase as the whole `bonus` value (28 mention reroll/fortune overall).

The "keep the two variants separate" requirement is already met by prose, with four precedents for replace-the-result specifically: blessed-medicine "fortune: reroll and use the new result", redsand-hourglass "reroll it and must use the new result", premonition-of-clarity "you reroll it and must take the second result", turn-back-the-clock "you must use the new result even if it's worse". Compare-two-results sits alongside them (derring-do, incredible-luck, whispering-staff, laurel-of-the-empath, starsong-nectar, acrobat's staff), and perfected-form even stores "treat an attack roll lower than 10 as a 10 (fortune)". So minor-omen is a coverage miss in an existing lane — the manual's "promised but empty" bucket, one authoring line: targets save/reflex, bonus "fortune: reroll and use the new result, even if worse". Not a missing system. Its limitedUses is already stored.

The one-fortune-per-roll stacking rule needs no new machinery: src/rules/glossary.ts:115 already reads "Fortune: roll twice and take the higher result; only one fortune effect can apply to a roll", and minor-omen carries traits [archetype, fortune, occult], so `traitDesc` surfaces that rule on the record's trait chip in FeatDetail. Per the manual's NOT-lanes, "restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere" is not a lane. There is also nothing to override procedurally: src/rules/dice.ts is a manual tray — roll(label, count, sides, modifier) with a nat-20/nat-1 flag — and grep finds no fortune/twice branch anywhere in the roll pipeline. The app never resolves a check, so per the manual ("the app lists the action; the player performs it"), roll procedure is display, which is what `situational` is.

The third example does not belong to the cluster at all. guide-the-timeline puts the fortune on an ALLY's next attack/skill check and the misfortune on a FOE's — neither is a roll on this sheet. That is the manual's NOT-lane "effects on enemies... rather than on your own sheet", and the app has already ruled this shape: ascended-celestial-dedication's own ally clause is stored in situational as when: "ALLIES inside your active nimbus...", and aura-of-courage's RECORD_MARKERS comment states "Only the PLAYER half is modelled — ... an ally's conditions are not this sheet." Its remaining needs are other clusters already logged in gold-freetext (the chronoskimmer archetype DC; the 24-hour per-target immunity list), not roll procedure.

For the record, the app has a SECOND home for zero-magnitude roll-procedure changes when no stat row fits: RECORD_MARKERS (situationalBonuses.ts:3179, "Some things change no number the sheet holds"), already carrying magic-hands "roll d10s instead of d8s", experienced-professional "crit fail -> fail", fancy-moves "you can roll Performance instead of Intimidation to Demoralize". Two built lanes cover this, not zero.

refuted.name: live-condition-state
refuted.why:
The reviewer checked the wrong neighbour. They compared against `mode` and `note` and never opened the `situational` lane, whose implementation file (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts) contains RECORD_MARKERS — a registry whose entries are shaped `{ on: 'condition' | 'action', id, value?, note }`, i.e. a record attaching a rule to ONE named condition as it sits on THIS character's sheet. It is read by `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'condition', c.id)` (src/rules/explain.ts:297) and rendered by src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1026 as a star on that condition's own pill, opening the source record's carve-out text. The comment there is the owner's Ruling D verbatim: 'something that changes how a condition works FOR YOU ... marks the condition itself'. That is the missing system, already built and already populated: 50 live `on:'condition'` marks across off-guard(4), frightened(4), dying(6), quickened(10), cursebound(11), deafened(3), persistent-damage(4), clumsy, concealed, controlled, doomed, fatigued, unconscious.

All three asserted capabilities have a route.
(1) PROVENANCE. A mark is keyed by its source record id and only reaches the sheet for a character who owns that record (characterSituationalIds + the gated `grantMarkers` channel, types.ts:3469), and the popup names the source. `uncanny-dodge` files 'you are NOT off-guard to hidden/undetected/flanking foes of your level or lower' onto the off-guard pill; `come-and-get-me` files a self-inflicted off-guard with its own rider. A zombie's Slowed pill would carry a star reading 'Zombie Dedication — deterioration: removable only by 10 minutes of repairs, by no other means'; a non-zombie's identical Slowed 1 carries no star. The two are distinguished on the pill, which is where the reviewer says nothing can distinguish them.
(2) REMOVAL RULES ON A CONDITION INSTANCE. Shipped, repeatedly: `stone-blood` / `stone-blood-stonebound` / `mutated-fleshwarp` mark persistent-damage with 'the flat check to end persistent BLEED damage on you is DC 10 instead of DC 15'; `steelskin-hobgoblin` sets DC 13; `aura-of-courage` and `face-your-fears` change how the frightened value steps DOWN for you. Those are removal rules written against the condition, discriminating bleed from other persistent damage, with named provenance — the exact three properties claimed absent. And note stone-blood proves the app already discriminates a persistent-damage SUBTYPE on the pill, which a bare `character.conditions` predicate could not do (the `persistent-damage` condition is untyped), so the proposed predicate would answer blood-and-spirit's question WRONG where the existing lane answers it right.
(3) THE SELF-INFLICTED TOGGLE. The zombie's Slowed is not an 'incoming condition' at all — it is an author-defined state attached to a record, which is the `mode` lane's definition, and the reviewer's claim that modes 'carry no removal rules' is false: of 429 shipped modes, 417 carry a printed `duration`, 44 carry `survivesRest` (the rest-cycle clearing rule; play.ts:1625), 206 carry `appliesWhen` (a printed circumstance gate on a modifier), modes can be gated to a feat id so only Zombie Dedication holders see it (ModeDef.feats), 52 carry PENALTIES that pool with condition penalties by PF2e worst-of-type (modes.ts poolTypedMods + conditions.ts conditionTypedMods), and — decisively — VitalsRail.tsx:1063 renders active-mode pills in the SAME pill list as the conditions, each with its own name, duration and its own X. A 'Deteriorated (Zombie Dedication)' pill therefore sits beside a spell's Slowed pill and is removable only by its own control. Non-item modes are not cleared by rest, which matches deterioration exactly.

On 'the sheet must be able to know its own live condition state': it already does, and not decoratively. `character.conditions` drives AC, all saves, Perception, every skill, class DC, spell attack, spell DC, attack rolls, damage, Speed, max HP (drainedHpLoss) and the death threshold (dyingDeathThreshold) — 14 derive.ts call sites — and play.ts:256 AUTO-INJECTS `encumbered` from carried bulk, an app-sourced condition the player cannot remove because its only remedy is dropping weight. That is a working precedent for a derived, source-owned, player-unremovable condition instance.

What is genuinely absent is an EVALUATED gate that suppresses an activity until a condition holds. That is not a hole; it is the doctrine in docs/mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes section — 'The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane (grantsAction)' — and the app's consistent answer for an unverifiable play-time requirement is to print it: Feat.requirements (free text, types.ts:1435), StanceDef.requires.text ('for requirements we can't check', 47 stances), and 206 mode `appliesWhen` strings. blood-and-spirit's 'While you are taking persistent bleed damage, you can Interact to…' is that clause, and its natural home is a persistent-damage condition mark alongside the four already there.

Finally the cluster does not hold up as evidence. It is '3 of 183' but only TWO distinct clauses: zombie-dedication's slowed carve-out is counted twice (numbers lens and resources lens), and blood-and-spirit's bleed gate once. I measured the corpus — exactly 1 of 6,312 feat descriptions uses 'While you're taking persistent…' phrasing, and the only sibling of the zombie clause, giant-instinct's 'You can't remove this clumsy condition … by any means while wielding the weapon', is already handled as a rage-state effect. Both cited records simply have the field EMPTY (zombie-dedication carries grantedStrikes and immunities but no note and no marker; blood-and-spirit carries only a holy/unholy choice). By the audit manual's own taxonomy that is 'promised but empty — a likely defect', not 'no lane at all'. The correct action is to author two RECORD_MARKERS entries and one mode, not to build a condition-instance engine.

refuted.name: condition-definition-override
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the `note` lane (mechanic-lanes.md section J) covers it, and the reviewer's reason for rejecting `note` rests on a factual claim about the app that is false.

1) The premise fails. The reviewer says `note` is insufficient because "the condition the app already knows keeps its printed behaviour everywhere it is displayed or applied." Both halves are wrong. APPLIED: C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/conditions.ts is the app's only condition-mechanics layer — a map `CONDITION_EFFECTS` of typed numeric penalties. There is no `confused` key, and the file header states the design decision explicitly: "Out of scope (no flat number to display): action-economy conditions (Slowed, Stunned, Quickened), and situational ones (Blinded, Dazzled, Deafened, Confused, …)". Confused is applied at zero sites, so there is no behaviour anywhere for an override to reach. DISPLAYED: exactly one site, ConditionsModal.tsx:120 (`cond-row-desc`). And the app does not "already know" confused's behaviour at all — `interface Condition` (src/rules/types.ts:2775) is {id, name, description, descRefs, valued, group, source}. A paragraph of prose, not a behaviour model. You cannot override a definition the engine does not hold.

2) The clause is already on the sheet, at the point of use. FeatsTab.tsx:64-90 renders the feat's full description — which contains the sentence verbatim ("If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends") — plus `descRefs`, which turns the word "confused" into a clickable link into the glossary, plus a bold "Note:" block from `feat.note`. The player reads the character's exception immediately adjacent to the condition it modifies. For a clause the reviewer concedes changes no number anywhere, printing it where it is read IS the whole deliverable.

3) What is being overridden is GM adjudication, excluded twice by the lanes doc. The confused text in core-descriptions.json reads: "You use all your actions to Strike or cast offensive cantrips, though the GM can have you use other actions… Your targets are determined randomly by the GM… If it's impossible for you to attack or cast spells, you babble incoherently, wasting your actions." The app has no action economy and no turn engine; it never spends actions or picks targets. mechanic-lanes.md NOT-lanes bars "Anything the GM adjudicates" and "the internal steps of an activity — the app lists the action; the player performs it." Note also that the feat's rewrite just lands the character in a branch confused's own printed text already contains ("wasting your actions").

4) Where a condition-definition override DOES have a computable footprint, the app already does it per character. `Feat.dyingThresholdBonus` (types.ts:1521) → `Character.dyingThreshold` (types.ts:3447, built at build.ts:3407-3410) is read by `dyingDeathThreshold()` (conditions.ts:128), play.ts:537 and VitalsRail.tsx:176. That is Diehard rewriting the *dying* condition's definition for one character, reaching both engine and display — same route serving unbreakable-bond (megafauna companion dies at dying 5) and soul-well; mountains-stoutness likewise remaps the recovery DC. So this family is not unbuilt: its numeric members are built, and the non-numeric member has nothing to compute.

5) The cluster is inflated. "3 of 183" is ONE feat — ascended-celestial-dedication — counted through three lenses (entries 27, 30, 32 of scripts/audit/gold-freetext.json, lenses numbers/resources/unmodellable). I swept all of public/core-descriptions.json for condition-rewrite sentences (173 hits across 11 collections) and found exactly one other record of this pure non-numeric shape: `courageous-tanuki` (fleeing — "instead of having to spend all your actions trying to escape, you can act normally for one action"). Two records, both pure action-economy prose. Everything else in the 173 is a different, already-built shape: condition substitution (commitment-to-valor, thousand-year-grudge, greater-cruelty), an effect's own outcome tier (silencing-strike, tears-of-pearl), a numeric definition remap (diehard, mountains-stoutness), or a situational bonus (grim-insight, starlit-eyes).

RESIDUAL DEFECT worth acting on, in an existing lane: ascended-celestial-dedication carries no `note`. Its situationalBonuses.ts:606 entry covers the Will reroll and the ally fear bonus, `grantsActions: ['bless-ally']` and `limitedUses` are present, but the confused clause is unauthored. courageous-tanuki is the same. That is two 'promised but empty' `note` fields — a data gap in a built lane, not a missing system.

refuted.name: level-derived-value-expressions
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The premise — "rankUpgrade / usesUpgrade are the only level-stepped structures in the vocabulary" — is false. The app has a general, CSP-safe level-derived value-expression engine plus a level-banded ladder idiom, both load-bearing today, and both of the cluster's numbers land inside them.

(1) THE EXPRESSION ENGINE. `resolveFormula` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/derive.ts:1330, with `substituteTokens` at :1302) is exactly "a number inside a record computed from character level": a value typed `number | string`, where the string is substituted for `@actor.level` (also ability mods, the character's own Speeds, archetype feat counts) and then parsed by a recursive-descent grammar over floor/ceil/max/min and + - * / . It refuses rather than guesses on an unknown token. Live consumers span four different value kinds and several lanes in the manual: the `resistance`/`weakness` lanes (`IwrEntry.value` — types.ts:309-313, e.g. `max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))`, `3+floor(@actor.level/2)`), the `speed` lane (types.ts:452-454, formula SpeedGrants), `languageChoices` (build.ts:983), and `dailyItems` maxLevel (dailyItems.ts:95). So thermal-nimbus's "resistance equal to your level" and eternal-blessing's "half your level" — the same lens, same file — are already expressible. There is also a whole scaling-rewrite layer on top of it: `HALF_LEVEL` / `withFullLevelResistance` (derive.ts:1404-1454) rewrites a half-level formula to a full-level one when a feature upgrades it.

(2) THE LEVEL-BANDED LADDER IDIOM, highest-band-reached-wins, stored on records: `innateSpells[].heightenAt: {level, rank}[]` (types.ts:1207-1209, "the highest entry whose level the character has reached wins" — 18 feats carry one: dragon-prince `[{12,4},{15,5},{18,6}]`), `heightenHalfLevel` (build.ts:4028), `critSpecLevel` (26 feats), `whileActive[].minLevel`, `maxHpBonus.perLevel`, `shieldReinforcingByLevel`, `resistanceLevelUpgrade`, plus `rankUpgrade`/`usesUpgrade`. That is the exact semantics shame-the-sin needs.

(3) LEVEL-BANDED DAMAGE DICE SPECIFICALLY — the reviewer's "a static stored damage figure is simply wrong at 13th and 17th level" — is a SHIPPED behaviour, not an absent one. `precisionDice: {dice, die, upgradeAt: {level, die}}` (types.ts:604) is a damage figure ON A FEAT that changes at a named character level (sneak-attacker: 1d4, d6 at 6th). `strikePrecisionRiders` (derive.ts:2192-2250) computes `dice = 1 + [5,11,17].filter(l => c.level >= l).length` and renders "Nd6 precision" with its condition note — literally the 1d6 → 2d6 → 3d6 shape at named thresholds, recomputed every derive and re-displayed as the character levels; Ranger Precision does `level>=19?3:level>=11?2:1` d8 two lines later; `RAGE_DAMAGE` (derive.ts:2256+) bands flat damage at tiers [3,7,13]. On the spell side `heightening.type:'fixed'` + `fixedLevelAt` + `scaleDamage` (src/rules/heightening.ts:100-127) is a level→dice band table with highest-reached-wins, rendered inline by `injectDamageArrow` in SpellsTab.tsx. At most `StrikeDamageRider.dice.n` (types.ts:2859) needs the same `number | string` widening `IwrEntry.value` already has — a new consumer of an existing lane, not a new system.

(4) SHAME THE SIN HAS A ZERO-SCHEMA-CHANGE HOME TODAY: the `situational` lane, `kind: 'strikeDamage'`, prose `bonus` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts). 61 entries there already spell level bands in the prose — sly-striker reads "+1d6 precision (2d6 at 14th level if you'd deal 3d6+ sneak attack)". That is the app's own established route for conditional strike damage whose condition reads off the target, and the manual explicitly routes "a bonus to one specific roll / in a specific circumstance" here.

(5) THE DC HALF DIES TWICE. First, it is inside the existing grammar: I verified `14 + @actor.level + floor(@actor.level/3)` reproduces the entire level-based DC table exactly for levels 0-20 (L3=18, L6=22, L9=26, L15=34, L18=38), and `+5` is the very-hard adjustment — 43 at 18th, all of it floor/+// that `resolveFormula` already parses. So it is not "a table that does not exist as a value." Second, what is genuinely missing is a CONSUMER, and that consumer is out of scope by the manual's own non-lane list: "the internal steps of an activity — 'make a Strike', 'you may Step', 'attempt an Athletics check'. The app lists the action; the player performs it." "Attempt an Incarnation Lore check against a very hard DC of your level" is that step; the DC is its parameter, rolled at the table. Note the app already carries the part of On My Best Day that does land on the sheet — situationalBonuses.ts:768 has an `ac` entry covering the +1 to +3 status bonus and the critical-failure narrowing.

SECONDARY GROUND, if (1)-(4) were somehow rejected: the cluster is NOT-ONE-SYSTEM. Its three entries split into two consumers that share nothing but the word "level" — a damage rider on a Strike, and the DC of a skill check the player rolls. Building either delivers none of the other, and the sheet has no "DC I roll against" slot anywhere (every DC it models — class DC, spell DC, save DC — is a DC someone ELSE rolls against). The residue after the DC entry is removed is one record's damage rider.

Finally, shame-the-sin's actual primary effect (the demon suffers its OWN special vulnerability; the dice apply only if it has none, only on a critical hit, only against the demon trait) is enemy-facing and GM-adjudicated — the manual's "effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet" non-lane. The gold-freetext note that the printed base die is missing ("takes an additional damage") is a source-text defect, not a missing lane.

refuted.name: damage-type-substitution-by-source-family
refuted.why:
Refuted by the `situational` lane (doc section J: `situational` / `situationalBonuses.ts`) — the surface the reviewer looked past because they only checked weaponRider and modifiesGrant. Each of the three claimed impossibilities has a shipped precedent there, one of them in this feat's own family.

1. "keyed on a damage TYPE, must reach grants that know nothing about this feat": situational entries are keyed on the SOURCE record and target a stat KIND, never a named grant. explain.ts:957-985 (strikeDamage case) states the contract outright — "Feat/item damage bonuses are listed for every Strike... a target carries no weapon narrowing... The `when` clause on each line is what tells the player whether it applies." One entry on energized-spark with targets [{kind:'strikeDamage'},{kind:'spellDamage'}] and when: "spirit damage dealt by your exemplar abilities" reaches every strike and the spell-damage surface, and no target record has to know the feat exists. spellDamage is documented as deliberately PROSE-ONLY for exactly this reason (situationalBonuses.ts:47-57).

2. "nothing expresses substitution": the registry is full of it, including numberless substitution. poolSituationalLines' own comment: "A bonus with no number ('roll d10s instead of d8s') never pools." Live entries: harming-hands/healing-hands ("roll d10s instead of d8s"), frost-fair-yanyuedao ("the weapon becomes +3 major striking instead of +2 greater striking" — restating ANOTHER record's line), guards-fury ("+4 instead of Rage's +2"), crimson-fulcrum-lens ("+4 item (instead of the usual +2)"). parseBonus returns null on a non-numeric phrase, so a substitution clause adds nothing to any total — correct here, because spirit→fire moves no number the player's sheet holds; damage type only meets IWR, which is the target's sheet.

3. "elected per instance, the player may keep the original": field-discovery-bomber already reads "...when you choose to", and gird-champion (situationalBonuses.ts:2628) is this very mechanic, already authored and already rendering — bonus: "+1d6 spirit (or your domain's damage type)", a player-elected per-instance damage-type swap on spirit damage from an exemplar-adjacent source. castigating-weapon (:2701) carries the TRAIT half in the same string ("...and your weapon and unarmed Strikes gain your holy or unholy trait").

The pick needs no new lane either: public/core.json shows energized-spark ALREADY carries the `choice` lane — {flag:'energizedSpark', kind:'array'} with all 12 printed trait/type options — plus maxTakable: null, so each repeated copy stores its own answer. The reviewer's two companion gold entries about repeatability are already-carried, not absent.

Scale check that collapses the "whole FAMILY" framing: derive.ts strikeDamageRiders is fed by exactly THREE spirit riders in the entire database (spirit-striking, greater-spirit-striking, gird-champion). All the other exemplar spirit damage — hands-of-the-wildling, titans-breaker, barrows-edge, gleaming-blade and 9 more — is ALREADY authored as strikeDamage situational stars in this same registry (13 spirit entries among 199 strikeDamage / 26 spellDamage stars). The substitution clause belongs beside them, in the same lane, read from the same popup.

This is settled owner policy, not a cop-out: Ruling N (the artillerist-dedication comment in situationalBonuses.ts) chose "a single star whose note covers all four, over building a marker surface" for a case with less on-sheet content than this one. The only thing genuinely missing is interpolating the stored pick into the star's text — a nicety, not a capability, and no other one of the 224 entries interpolates a choice into its `when` either.

Load-bearing files: C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts (interface :15-80; gird-champion :2628; castigating-weapon :2701; harming-hands :2731; frost-fair-yanyuedao :2600; poolSituationalLines :3395-3410), C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\explain.ts:957-985, C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\derive.ts:2422-2480, C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\public\core.json (feats.energized-spark).

refuted.name: self-damage-as-cost-and-unresistable-damage
refuted.why: The proposal's premise is factually wrong. (1) A damage application exists: applyDamage at src/rules/play.ts:538, reachable from HpControl.tsx:54 (and its N/-N/tN command parser at line 70), HpNumpadModal.tsx Damage mode, and companions. (2) There is no defence stack in that path to bypass — applyDamage reads only tempHp and max, never resistances/weaknesses/immunities. The sole IWR arithmetic is an OPT-IN one-tap chip (HpNumpadModal.tsx:127) the player must press instead of the plain 'Deal Damage' button, and a device pref (hpIwrButtons===false, wired at VitalsRail.tsx:1130) removes the chips entirely. Unresisted application is therefore the default and only automatic behaviour, so 'can't be resisted in any way' needs zero new machinery: type 6, press Deal Damage. A bypass flag would be a no-op against machinery that does not exist. (3) The HP payment is an internal step of an activity, which mechanic-lanes.md excludes by name ('make a Strike', 'attempt an Athletics check' — the app lists the action, the player performs it), and also falls under 'restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere': the app automates no damage from any source. (4) The 'two mutually exclusive requirements with HP as fallback' is the established mode idiom — all 203 entries in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json state player-verified preconditions via duration+note, e.g. armored-resistance duration 'while you Intercept an Attack in medium or heavy armor' + note 'Switch it on when you Intercept.' Blood and Spirit's real payload (until end of turn, +1d6 spirit damage of the chosen trait on Strikes with that weapon) is a mode, and the bleed-or-pay-1d6 branch is exactly what duration/note carry. The printed clause additionally has two live slots on this very record: the note lane (FeatsTab.tsx:75, 595 records carry it) and per-option choice notes rendered as 'Your choice: Holy — …' (FeatsTab.tsx:65-66) — blood-and-spirit already carries that choice (holy/unholy). Supporting: the cluster is inflated — '3 of 183' is three gold-freetext.json rows of ONE feat seen through the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses; a full description sweep finds 11 records and they are not one shape (left-hand-blood and willing-death already carry the real payload as limitedUses, see effect-backfill.json:71009; lifes-blood's unresistable damage is dealt to a TARGET, i.e. out-of-scope enemy-facing text; destructive-block and vicious-vengeance are GM arithmetic). The proposal is also not one system — it conjoins a damage application, an IWR-exemption flag, and condition-gated availability, the last of which gold-freetext.json lists as its own separate entry for this same feat. The reviewer checked the right neighbours (resistance/immunity/hpBonus) and correctly ruled them out, but those are build lanes; self-damage lives in the play layer, which they never examined.

refuted.name: downtime-output-multipliers
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the lane exists, and this exact feat is already authored in it and rendering. The reviewer checked only the FLAT-MODIFIER half of `situational` (FEAT_SITUATIONAL). The same file's other half is the action/condition marker lane (`RECORD_MARKERS` + `markersFor`, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3167-3211), whose doc comment states its purpose in exactly the reviewer's words: "Some things change no number the sheet holds... None of those has a stat row, and starring the nearest roll would be a lie." The owner's ruling (Ruling D) was to attach the mark to the thing it modifies and show the changed value inline.

Experienced Professional is ALREADY THERE, at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3230, with BOTH clauses in one entry:
  'experienced-professional': [{"on":"action","id":"earn-income","value":"crit fail -> fail","note":"When you use Lore to Earn Income a critical failure becomes a failure; if you're an expert in Lore, a failed check earns twice as much income (unless it was originally a critical failure)."}]

It reaches the sheet in two places, both verified: src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:502 (activity rows) and src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:183 (the Lore skill popup's "Actions you can take" list), each rendering `(crit fail -> fail)` inline plus a star whose tooltip prints the full note. The keys resolve: `actionId`/`actionSlug` slug "Earn Income" -> "earn-income", core.json has both `actions['earn-income']` and `feats['experienced-professional']`, so the marker is live, not dead.

Each of the three "pieces with no home" has one:
1. Multiplier on a non-roll ACTIVITY OUTPUT — this is what the lane is FOR, with four shipped precedents of the identical shape: `magic-hands` (Treat Wounds heals d10s instead of d8s), `crafters-eyepiece` ("Repair restores 10 + 10 per proficiency rank" — a rank-SCALED non-roll output), `armbands-of-athleticism-greater` (+10 feet on a successful Climb/Swim), `black-powder-boost` (+10 feet to a Leap). Doubling Earn Income's payout is structurally the same object as upgrading Treat Wounds' healing die.
2. Proficiency-RANK gate evaluated at use time — already first-class, and independently of this lane. `SkillAction.tiers[]` (src/rules/skillActions.ts:19) is defined as "Proficiency-gated upgrades to the SAME action", and `skillActionsFor` (line 1007) filters them with `rankAtLeast(rank, t.rank)` against the character's LIVE rank in that skill. Lore's Earn Income already ships four such tiers (lines 478-500) including an explicit `expert` one about a higher income column. A rank gate on Earn Income's monetary output is a shipped, rendered capability. The `situational` half also carries rank-tiered text: `contract-negotiator` = "+1 circumstance if expert in Diplomacy, +2 if master, +3 if legendary".
3. Degree-of-success remap — same lane, existing precedent: `the-publican` carries `value: "crit fail -> fail"` on Aid; `defy-death` remaps recovery DCs; `grub-gloves-*` carry "a success becomes a critical success".

The "provenance memory / the two clauses must know about each other" requirement dissolves rather than needing a mechanism: both clauses are ONE marker with ONE note on ONE row, so there is no cross-clause state to keep and nothing to launder. That requirement is an artifact of assuming the app computes the coin.

Secondary refutation (out-of-scope): it does not compute the coin, deliberately. There is no currency figure in the app for a multiplier to operate on — the GM sets the task level and the secret DC and awards from the Income Earned table. mechanic-lanes.md excludes this twice under NOT lanes: "Anything the GM adjudicates" and "The internal steps of an activity... The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane." So the proposal asks for a multiplier with no operand.

Tertiary (not-one-system): the cluster is not 3 records. gold-freetext.json entries 71, 73 and 75 are the SAME clause of the SAME feat under the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses (entries 70/72/74 are its other clause, which the proposal excludes). This is one sentence of one 1st-level general skill feat, already built.

refuted.name: flat-check-as-a-roll-target
refuted.why: The `situational` lane covers it (docs/mechanic-lanes.md §J, satisfied by src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), and NINE live records already express this exact clause shape. The reviewer's objection rests on a category error: they assume `situational` needs "a statistic for passiveEffects.saves to hook onto". It does not. situationalBonuses.ts states at the top that the registry "is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number" — `targets` is a display ANCHOR (where the star goes), not a modifier destination. A flat check needing no statistic is therefore no obstacle. Two live routes, both in situationalBonuses.ts: (1) FEAT_SITUATIONAL with `targets:[{kind:'hp'}]` and the flat check named in `when` — 5 records: cindersoul (line 2703, when: "on the flat check to recover from persistent acid, bleed, or poison damage", bonus: "DC 10 instead of 15…"), fire-lung (2722), fire-savvy (2723), scar-thick-skin (2757), scorched-on-the-crackling-mountain (2758); the HP row stars via statHasSituational(character,{kind:'hp'}) at src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:328 and opens in StatDetailModal. (2) RECORD_MARKERS with `{on:'condition', id:'persistent-damage', value, note}` — 4 records: stone-blood (3240), stone-blood-stonebound (3241), mutated-fleshwarp (3278), steelskin-hobgoblin (3286). `persistent-damage` is a real condition id among core.json's 57 conditions, and src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1026 calls recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'condition', c.id) to render a star + note popup on that condition's pill. The RecordMarker interface's own doc comment was written for exactly this problem: "Some things change no number the sheet holds… starring 'the nearest roll' would be a lie." The damage-type addressability they claim is impossible is already carried in the marker prose: stone-blood's value is "bleed flat check DC 10"; steelskin-hobgoblin's note distinguishes "physical (including bleed), energy, or poison damage".
