The cluster is also one record, not three: all 3 gold-freetext entries are the same feat and the same clause (divine-health, "and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage") viewed through the numbers / resources / unmodellable lenses. divine-health ALREADY has a FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry (line 180) covering the save half — targets save/all, when "saves against diseases and poisons", bonus "+2 status" — while its printed text (public/core-descriptions.json) reads "+2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage". So the residual is one unworded half of one existing registry entry, i.e. mechanic-lanes.md's "promised but empty" bucket: author one more line for divine-health following the nine existing precedents. That is a content defect in a single entry, not a missing system.

refuted.name: named-derived-dc-statistics
refuted.why:
REFUTED on the record's own text. The reviewer's factual premise is wrong: the chronoskimmer DC is not computed from its own key attribute, proficiency and level. Chronoskimmer Dedication (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json, feats/chronoskimmer-dedication) ends with: 'The DC for these abilities is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your chronoskimmer DC'. It is a NICKNAME for max(class DC, spell DC) — two statistics this app already derives and already displays. There is no independent statistic to bring into existence: no new proficiency rank, no key attribute of its own, no advancement track, and no way it could ever diverge from the two numbers it aliases.

The number is already on the sheet. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx pushes both into the defences rail side by side — line 296 `{ label: 'Class DC', value: classDc.dc, ref: { kind: 'classDc' } }` and line 300 `{ label: 'Spell DC', value: sc.dc, ref: { kind: 'spell', entryId: entry.id, which: 'dc' } }` — each with a StatRef that opens its StatDetailModal breakdown. A chronoskimmer player reads their chronoskimmer DC off the sheet by taking the larger of two adjacent tiles. A non-casting chronoskimmer has only the Class DC tile, and that IS their chronoskimmer DC.

The only residue is the sentence that assigns the nickname, and that is the `note` lane in Section J of C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/docs/mechanic-lanes.md ('a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable') — and it is in fact already printed verbatim, because the Dedication's description text quoted above renders on the sheet and is pinnable.

Two measurements kill the generalisation. (1) 'class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher' is standard PF2e boilerplate: 232 records across items, feats, actions and familiar abilities carry it (the-fiend, breath-of-the-dragon, razmiran-priest-dedication, steal-time, energy-emanation, dazzling-show, …). The chronoskimmer is the one that gives the boilerplate a nickname; the arithmetic is identical everywhere. A lane for this would have 232 members and no computation of its own. (2) I scanned every description in the corpus for a bespoke named DC — patterns /is called your X DC/ and /your X DC is equal to|calculated/ — and got exactly ONE hit in the whole dataset: feats/chronoskimmer-dedication. No record anywhere defines a named DC from its own proficiency and key attribute. The proposed system as specified has zero members.

Cluster integrity is not the problem: all 3 gold-freetext entries (lines 687-695 and 711-713 of C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/audit/gold-freetext.json) are the same feat read through three lenses, all making the same claim, so 'not-one-system' does not apply — the claim is simply false. The two genuinely separate needs the same feat raises (a 24-hour per-target immunity list, and a one-shot fortune effect on an ally's next roll) are other creatures' sheets and were already scoped out by the reviewer's own notes.

refuted.name: build-time-validation-timing
refuted.why: Covered by grantsFeatChoice (featPickGrants), plus the lane doc's own NOT-lanes rule. (1) mechanic-lanes.md line 164 explicitly excludes "Prerequisites, access clauses..." from being lanes at all; this clause is a prerequisite clause verbatim, so the gold entries are a classifier error against the manual they were produced under. (2) The clause was judged TRUNCATED at "...in order " — the real text in public/core-descriptions.json ends "in order to determine which prerequisites you meet", which is paper-worksheet procedure advice, not a sheet mechanic. (3) The premise 'legal picks are wrongly rejected' is false: src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:200-228 pickableFeats filters ONLY on level/category/traits/dynamicTrait/excludes and never consults prerequisites; the file header states the convention — "the picker is at worst slightly permissive, never blocking a legal pick." (4) There is no evaluation order to defer: Builder.tsx:255 `const featPrereqChar = useMemo(() => buildCharacter(build, ovContent), [build, ovContent])` — checkPrerequisites has exactly 3 callers (Builder.tsx 1437, 1893, 2001), all against the FULLY derived character from the entire BuildState, recomputed on every edit, and it is never called inside buildCharacter or pickableFeats. Order-independent validation against the finished build IS the architecture. (5) The slot already sits open without error: build.ts:2752-2757 silently `continue`s an unresolved pick and `continue`s an illegal one (`// ignore an illegal pick`) WITHOUT deleting the stored choice, so it revives when a later edit makes it legal; the pick-grant UI (Builder.tsx 1233-1246, 1604-1623) is a bare PopupSelect with a placeholder, the `lvl-pending "!"` incomplete marker exists only for subclass/umtFeatId/empty feat slots (1313, 1425, 1469) and never for pickFeatChoices, and there is no submit or finish-validation gate anywhere. (6) The one real consequence of deferred validation is already built: Builder.tsx 1428-1437 re-validates a picked feat against the finished build and warns only, "never auto-remove", honouring overrides; and featPickGrants already encodes prerequisite WAIVERS where they matter (ancient-elf maxLevel 2 = "even though you don't meet its level prerequisite"). (7) Cluster inflation: gold-freetext.json has 183 entries but only 37 distinct feats; all three rows are the same natural-ambition clause under the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses, so the cluster is 1 record, not 3.

refuted.name: per-foe-state
refuted.why:
The cluster fuses two unrelated capabilities, and it needs the bundling to reach size 3: entry 69 (cornered-fury) is a conditional attack modifier; entries 116 and 119 (guide-the-timeline) are a persistent 24-hour roster. Different lifetimes (rounds vs wall-clock), different storage (none vs a persisted ledger), different consumers (a star in a stat breakdown vs a legality gate on re-activating one feat). 'Keyed to a creature' is the only word they share. Taken separately, each is refuted differently.

HALF 1 (cornered-fury) is already-expressible via `situational`. The reviewer's objection — 'situational scopes a bonus to a circumstance, not to a specific creature, and has no timer' — misreads the lane as a computation engine. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts states in its header that it is 'DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number'; the sheet stars the stat and prints the trigger, and C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:108 labels the section 'Situational (apply when it fits)'. `when` is free prose, so a named creature and a round clock are trigger CONTENT, not missing capability — and both already appear dozens of times. `predictable`: 'against the creature you used Predictable! on, until the start of your next turn' is the exact asserted-impossible combination. Also `unfazed-assessment`, `scour-the-library`, `monster-warden`, `boasters-challenge`, `avowed-insight`, `surgical-shock`, `feeding-frenzy`, `lock-on`, and `harsh-judgment` ('while you have a condemned foe: … that foe' vs 'anyone other than that foe' — a designated-foe state with a counter-scope). The size gate has precedent too: `kaiju-defense-oath` ('against creatures at least 2 sizes larger than you'), `dragons-presence`. `cornered-fury` simply has no entry (grep of src/ returns nothing) — a promised-but-empty slot in a built lane, the audit's most common finding. Furthermore the reviewer's '+2 circumstance bonus on my attacks' is their own arithmetic transposition: PF2e puts off-guard on the FOE as -2 circumstance to ITS AC, which the lanes doc excludes as 'Effects on enemies'. And that half is already built in this app, on the foe's row: C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/tracker/src/utils/conditionEffects.ts:128 folds off-guard into -2 circumstance AC for any combatant, and tracker/src/store/combatStore.ts:493 ticks a round `duration` and expires it — per-creature state with a round clock, embedded via src/integration/CampaignTracker.tsx.

HALF 2 (the 24-hour immunity roster) is out-of-scope, and gold entry 116 concedes it in its own text: 'This lives on other creatures rather than on the character's own sheet, so at most it is a printed reminder — flagged because a use-tracking lens would otherwise expect a counter here and there is nothing on-sheet to count.' That is the auditor documenting a lens artifact. It is also already gated: guide-the-timeline carries `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}` (backfilled in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, live on the record in public/core.json). A per-target immunity list could only ever bite if the feat were usable twice on the same creature inside 24 hours, and limitedUses forbids a second use at all — so the roster enforces nothing the sheet does not. Temporary immunity is additionally a PF2e general rule attached to effects broadly ('Restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere'). Its display route is the live `note` lane (read at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:75).

Note: the two other guide-the-timeline needs the reviewer did not cite — the archetype-specific 'chronoskimmer DC' (115, 118) and the fortune effect on an ally's next roll (117) — are separate questions and are not evidence for this one.

refuted.name: spell-selection-eligibility-widening
refuted.why: The lane is spellListAdd, and its as:'list' variant exists specifically to express picker eligibility as distinct from castability. src/rules/types.ts:2965 defines as?: 'list' | 'repertoire' | 'font', and src/rules/build.ts:3294 documents the split verbatim: "'list' widens the picker (you may LEARN it), 'repertoire' means you already know it, 'font' makes it a legal divine-font choice." The reviewer's premise describes as:'repertoire'; as:'list' does nothing BUT feed selection. It has exactly two consumers in the whole app, and both are repertoire-eligibility functions: src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:275-278 -> traditionSpellsByRank -> optionsFor(rank) at :327 (the in-play Manage-Spells add/remove/swap picker), and src/builder/Builder.tsx:441 -> listAdditions -> eligibleSpells(rank) at :490 (the build-time repertoire picker, whose docstring says it was added because "a caster building a repertoire here could never pick the spells their own feat had just granted them"). There is no separate level-up-swap subsystem to plumb into: a swap is remove+add through optionsFor, a rebuild is eligibleSpells, and both are fed. SpellAccessGrant even carries the exact divine-access resolver: from?: 'deity' documented as "your deity's spells (spells your deity grants to clerics)" plus max, and blessed-blood-sorcerer already ships {from:'deity',max:3,as:'list'} for a description that is the identical mechanic in identical words ("They are not automatically added to your repertoire, but you can select them just as you would spells normally on the divine spell list"), covered by test/spell-access-lanes.test.ts and test/spell-list-additions.test.ts ("The lane widens the POOL only. You still spend a repertoire slot"). divine-access's failure is stale DATA, not an absent system: scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:37724 marks it inert because "deity data doesn't record which cleric spells a deity grants", which is no longer true (472 of 485 deities in public/core.json now carry spells). Its only distinct wrinkle is resolving from against a chosen deity rather than build.deityId, a one-field extension of a working lane. Side defects worth logging separately: Builder.tsx:529 eligibleSpells2 (dual-class second caster) ignores listAdditions, and the "3 of 183" cluster is one clause on one feat seen through three lenses.

refuted.name: feat-to-owned-item-binding
refuted.why: Covered by the designated / ItemDesignation lane, which the reviewer did not consider (it is absent from docs/mechanic-lanes.md, which explains the miss). src/rules/types.ts:2933 defines `ItemDesignation = 'innovation' | 'weapon-implement' | 'bonded' | 'ikon' | 'rune-source'`, stored as InventoryItem.designations (types.ts:3001) — 'ikon' is already one of the five. Its doc comment (types.ts:2991-2999) states the reviewer's case verbatim as the lane's reason for existing: 'The app never linked a class choice to an inventory item... every one says "your innovation..." and nothing knew which object that meant', and pre-empts their warning with 'A rider filtering on a designation applies to NOTHING when none is set. There is deliberately no "first weapon" fallback.' Player-chosen and visible ON the item: ItemDetail.tsx:475-494 renders a 'This is my -> Ikon' toggle, offered to exemplars at InventoryTab.tsx:636; re-pointable and exclusive via setItemDesignation (play.ts:1219, which MOVES the designation); persisted through build.ts:4452/4622 and data/transfer.ts. The central claim — 'nothing lets the strike breakdown ask does this weapon carry that feat' — is false: weaponMatches at derive.ts:2394-2396 resolves per strike via `inv = c.inventory.find(i => i.instanceId === strike.instanceId); return inv.designations.includes(w.designated)`, and the same gate runs for weapon riders (derive.ts:2556), armour restat (derive.ts:597) and rune capacity (derive.ts:1480) — four readers. Their 'wrongly applies to every strike' worry is the exact bug the comment at derive.ts:2391-2393 says was designed out. The damage-type legal-set filter is the weakest part: the lane already solves pick-legality with a second gate (derive.ts:586-590, 'the item must carry the designation AND be one the record names... nothing stops a player marking their full plate as the innovation'), so a damageType key alongside match.items/groups/anyTrait is one field in an existing match object. Live in production 12 times in core.json (Hampering Spikes, Razor Prongs, Modular Head, Integrated Gauntlet, Tangle Line, Hefty Composition, Inconspicuous Appearance, Inventor Weapon Expertise, Initiate Benefit (Weapon), Rod of Rule, Heavy Construction, Rune Capacity). Two caveats, both inside the lane: (1) `"designated":"ikon"` appears 0 times in core.json today — all 21 ikon records deliver effects as situationalBonuses prose (situationalBonuses.ts:2706/2806/2864), so the ikon designation is currently write-only; populating it is a data edit into scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, not a new system. (2) setItemDesignation is exclusive per kind while an exemplar picks 3 ikons at level 1 (classes.exemplar extraChoices ikon, pickByLevel {1:3}), so per-ikon granularity needs the union widened or the designation to carry the granting record id — a granularity change to a built mechanism. Cluster strength is also thin: all 3 entries are the same record and the same clause (branched-tree-of-pain's **Usage** line) restated once per lens; the 4th entry for that feat (crit on a 19) is a different capability.

refuted.name: grants-onto-another-characters-sheet
refuted.why:
The residual capability, once the existing lanes are applied, is literally "render a record on a different character's sheet" — the reviewer's own need text says so three times ("puts a reaction on ANOTHER creature's sheet", "appears on ANOTHER character's sheet", "sourced from someone else's sheet"). Four things make that out-of-scope rather than a missing lane.

1) The app already SETTLED the ally-facing direction, and its answer is never to write to the ally. Ruling F (memory: project_hh_rulings_dfgh, built 2026-07-30) decided: ally-instant → nothing at all; ally-timed → a display-only mode on the ACTIVATOR, gated by `feats:[id]`. That shipped: `feat-aegis-for-the-innocent` and `feat-tweak-appearances` in public/core.json `modes` are benefits that land on an ALLY and are rendered on the holder's own sheet as a mode + note. So the reviewer's "mirror image of the ally-facing aura system" does not need building — the aura system itself does not project onto other sheets. The same convention applies with `grantsActions`/`note` carrying an action instead of a number.

2) The half of Vantage Shot that belongs on this sheet is already fully expressible by `grantsAction`, and the trigger-phrased-around-another-creature part is already live in this very archetype. `grantsActions` (src/rules/types.ts:245, consumed at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:229) lets a PASSIVE record name an action id, which then renders in the encounter action list; and MainTab's `isActionCost` already surfaces any reaction-cost feat/feature directly. Proof from the same archetype: `exploit-opening` (reaction, trigger "Your spotter critically succeeds at a Strike") and `tag-team` (reaction, trigger "You or your spotter misses with a Strike") are already ordinary sheet reactions. Tag Team is the SAME outbound shape the reviewer calls impossible — "your spotter can use their reaction to make a melee or ranged Strike" — and it sits on the holder's sheet with no new system. Vantage Shot only looks different because Paizo printed it with a passive cost instead of a reaction cost; `grantsActions` exists precisely to close that gap. Vantage Shot is also RECIPROCAL ("Similarly, when your spotter successfully makes a ranged Strike…, you can use a reaction…"), so the holder does get a real reaction of their own to surface.

3) There is no sheet on the other side to grant onto. Sniping Duo Dedication states "your spotter doesn't need to spend any feats of their own to grant the effects" — the spotter owns no record, so nothing could carry the grant on their build. And architecturally the app forbids the write: teammate sheets in Campaigns/Party are explicitly read-only (`CharacterSheet readOnly`, PartyMembers/useMemberViewer), the only cross-character write channel is GM silent edit (`gm_character_edits`, GM-only, a wholesale sheet replacement), and the spotter need not be a Heroes Heaven user at all. This is the same class the lane manual already excludes: "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet."

4) The cluster is thin and internally mixed. All 3 of the 3 entries are ONE feat, vantage-shot. One of the three (the `numbers` lens) does not even isolate the proposed capability — its need bundles "(a) a persistent named ally relationship, 'your spotter'" with "(b) a grant that lands on that ally", i.e. it folds in the separate spotter-pointer capability the reviewer split out into a different cluster.

What IS real here is a per-record defect, not a system: all nine sniping-duo feats carry zero mechanic fields (`vantage-shot` has only id/name/level/category/traits/rarity/source/prerequisites/actionCost/archetype/edition). Vantage Shot should carry `grantsActions` naming a Vantage Shot reaction (trigger: your spotter's successful ranged Strike; effect: Stealth vs the foe's Perception DC, foe off-guard to your next attack) plus a `note` for the spotter-facing half — the app's established ally-facing rendering. That is promised-but-empty in an existing lane, which is exactly what the mechanic-lanes comparison is built to catch.

refuted.name: conditional-damage-riders
refuted.why: The `situational` lane covers it, via `SituationalTarget.kind: 'strikeDamage'` (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:36) — a first-class target kind whose in-code comment records that omitting it once left 338 verified strikeDamage bonuses with nowhere to be stored. 204 strikeDamage entries are live. The reviewer's premise that "situational expresses a bonus to a roll, not conditional damage dice" is empirically false: `SituationalBonus.bonus` is documented as "the modifier ... or a short effect phrase" and `when` is free prose, so all three gates are string composition, not a new capability. Each claimed-unwritable gate already ships: DEGREE OF SUCCESS + FIXED-TYPE DICE together in one entry — `chain-of-command` (line 2596) is `{kind:'strikeDamage'}, when:"on a critical hit with the chain of command", bonus:"+1d6 mental"`, i.e. the disputed clause minus the demon; TARGET CREATURE TRAIT — `demonbane-warrior` (498) `when:"...against demons"`, the same trait; TARGET LACKING A NAMED PROPERTY — `sly-striker` (2762) `when:"you hit a creature that isn't off-guard...", bonus:"+1d6 precision (2d6 at 14th level...)"`, which also settles the separate level-banding complaint, as do `deadly-aim` (516) "+4 (+6 at 11th level, +8 at 15th)" and `emblazon-energy` (444) "+1d4 extra damage of the chosen type". Display is verified, not write-only: explain.ts:982 folds featSituationalLines into the strike's Damage breakdown under `case 'strikeDamage'`, rendering source, `when`, and `bonus` clickable to the feat, with the in-code note that the `when` clause is what tells the player whether it applies. The second clause — the strike invoking a property on the target's stat block — is a distinct capability stapled onto the first, and the gold entry itself concedes nothing can sit on the sheet beyond printing the sentence; docs/mechanic-lanes.md:159 lists effects on enemies as a NOT-lane, and the prose already reaches the sheet through the feat description and the `note` lane. `grep -c shame-the-sin src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts` = 0 while the feat carries only limitedUses (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:73136), so this is mechanic-lanes.md's "promised but empty" bucket — one missing row in a built lane, fixable as: "shame-the-sin": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'strikeDamage' }], when: "when you critically hit a demon that has no special vulnerability (once per hour)", bonus: "+1d6 mental (2d6 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th)" }]. Caveat for whoever authors it: the AoN text is defective ("takes an additional damage" is missing its die), so the base 1d6 must be inferred from the 13th/17th progression.

refuted.name: activation-time-effect-variants
refuted.why: Covered by the `mode` lane (manual section J), specifically `ModeDef.exclusiveGroup`. The reviewer only tested `choice`/`dailyChoice` and correctly ruled both out, but never checked modes — whose type comment literally says "Only one active mode per group at a time (e.g. bard compositions, rage states)". Every axis they list has a field: several alternative packages = N ModeDefs sharing one exclusiveGroup, all gated to the same source record via `feats: [...]`; single-activation lifetime = `PlayState.activeModes`, where `toggleMode` (src\rules\play.ts:1397-1406) evicts the group sibling on activate, and rest deliberately leaves player-toggled modes untouched (play.ts:1619-1626) so it is neither build state nor daily state; re-entry giving a different answer = the player picks which group member to switch on each time; bonus size = `modifiers[].value`; whether a resistance is included at all = `resistances` present or absent; level vs half level = the IwrEntry formula `@actor.level` vs `floor(@actor.level/2)`, evaluated in derive.ts:1405-1451; how long each lasts = a per-mode `duration` string surfaced as "while active · <duration>" (derive.ts:1597-1602). This is not theoretical: scripts\data\toggle-modes.json already ships curse-of-creeping-ashes-1..4 — ONE record (feats: ["curse-of-creeping-ashes"]) producing FOUR packages in one exclusiveGroup that differ in weakness magnitude (flat 2 vs "5+@actor.level"), in whether the −2 ranged-attack modifier is present at all, and in duration; 20 modes live under `oracle-cursebound` this way. That is the reviewer's "four complete packages keyed to four outcomes" shape, built and read. Per record: elemental-evolution's build-time `choice` (flag `damage`, 7 options) records WHICH second type you have, and the per-Rage swap is two feat-gated modes in the existing `barbarian-rage` group each carrying a `strikeDamage` rider with its own damage `type` (reader at derive.ts:2444; live precedent item-iron-wine in consumable-modes.json) — unauthored data, not an absent field. on-my-best-day's "+1 AC against the next attack" is exactly `ModeModifier.appliesWhen`, the conditional modifier that leaves the number alone, underlines the stat and prints its scope; its Sustain-clock and consumed-on-first-use "needs" in gold-freetext ask for a timer engine that is a stated non-goal ("The app has no clock — this tells the player what they are tracking; they switch it off", modes.ts:326) and are not part of the proposed system's own definition. Weaker fallbacks if this were rejected: the cluster is also not-one-system (a player-facing variant picker vs a roll-outcome resolution table — the reviewer concedes the degree-of-success selector "is not a player choice at all"), and the selector half is out-of-scope under the manual's NOT-lanes rule that the app lists an activity while the player performs and resolves it.

refuted.name: healing-source-inversion
refuted.why: REFUTED. The lane exists and is called `negativeHealing` (surfaced as "Void healing"). It is a first-class boolean on `export interface DefenseGrants` (src/rules/types.ts:404, field at :655), which Feat (:1412), Heritage (:1212), ClassFeature (:1609) and ItemBase (:1936) all extend — so zombie-dedication can set it today with one field. deriveDefenses aggregates it in src/rules/derive.ts:1756 from heritage + feats + invested items into CharacterDefenses.negativeHealing (declared :1264, sitting in the same interface as resistances/weaknesses/immunities). It is rendered in BOTH defence surfaces, three lines above resistances in the same card: src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:738-750 prints "healed by void, harmed by vitality" with an InfoTerm reading "You are healed by void (negative) energy and harmed by vitality (positive) energy, as if you were undead", and src/sheet/DefensesPills.tsx:81-88 prints the same pill. It is durable across `npm run data` — 4 entries already in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. 5 live records carry it (dhampir heritage; aeon-stone-mottled-ellipsoid, emerald-fulcrum-lens, pierce-the-veil, aon-pierce-the-veil), and companionGrants.ts:292 / companions.ts:840 carry the companion-side wording. The reviewer read docs/mechanic-lanes.md, whose section C (Defences) lists only resistance/immunity/weakness/hardness — `negativeHealing` and `breathesWater` are both absent from the manual despite being live fields with readers. That doc omission, not an absent capability, produced this finding. The reviewer's own escape route also fails on its own terms: the bar they set ("the number has to arrive at HP with the opposite effect") is met by NO IWR lane in this app — applyDamage(play, amount, max, deathBase) in src/rules/play.ts:538 takes an untyped bare number and HpControl.tsx offers no damage-type entry, so resistance and immunity are likewise stored-aggregated-and-displayed with a source breakdown, never applied arithmetically. `negativeHealing` clears the exact same bar the whole family clears. Even the finer interaction is already routed: situationalBonuses.ts:950 attaches a modifier to `{kind:'hp'}` for "the Hit Points a Harm spell restores to you (requires void healing, which the lens grants)". The bundle packaging the reviewer conceded is likewise a non-issue: zombie-dedication ALREADY carries the immunity half of "basic undead benefits" inline (immunities: death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep), and grantsClassFeature/grantsFeat exist if a shared bundle record is preferred; "no need to breathe/eat/drink/sleep" is the `note` lane. Net: the only real finding here is a one-field data defect — zombie-dedication is missing `negativeHealing: true` (add to effect-backfill.json so it survives regen) — which is the "promised but empty" bucket, plus a docs gap: add `negativeHealing` and `breathesWater` to section C of mechanic-lanes.md or this false positive will recur on every undead/dhampir record. Note also the stated cluster is not 2 records: both gold-freetext.json entries are the SAME feat and the SAME clause (zombie-dedication / "and the basic undead benefits") seen through the `numbers` and `unmodellable` lenses, so the evidence base is a single record.

refuted.name: named-ally-relationship-slot
refuted.why:
The `choice` lane (section G) already carries exactly this, via `FeatChoiceDef` with `kind: 'text'` — and the live precedent is not a stretch, it is the same shape item-for-item. Cape of Justice ships as `choice { flag: 'capeOfJusticeOffender', prompt: 'Your designated offender', kind: 'text', daily: true, note: '...applies only to this creature...' }` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json). Its printed text says 'you must designate a single creature as your offender', and THREE separate clauses of the record dereference that designation: +1 item bonus to Demoralize that creature, 2d4+2 instead of 1d4+1 on the Force Shuriken against them, and the -1 Perception penalty for failing to designate. A persistent, player-chosen pointer to one specific other creature, stored on this sheet, read by multiple halves of the record — that IS the reviewer's spec, already built.

The lane is documented for precisely this case. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:1340 — "'text' — free text the player types, for picks whose vocabulary the app has no data for... the player supplies the word and it is recorded." A teammate's character name is the canonical no-vocabulary pick: a solo player, an offline player, or anyone not in a campaign has no party at all, so no content-derived option list can exist. 45 records already use it (feats/secret-speech, feats/spell-mastery, items/storied-skin...). Build-time (non-daily) answers persist in `BuildState.featChoices` keyed by carrier, rendered by the shared picker at src/builder/shared.tsx:2518 and src/builder/Builder.tsx:285, with `def.note` printed alongside.

"Referenceable by feats" is not missing either. Cross-record dereference of an earlier pick already exists: `spellListReplacement.choiceId` "names the effectChoice on the carrier that holds the pick" (types.ts:814), and `grantedFeatByChoice` branches on one. So both halves reading one stored designation is a shipped mechanism.

Most decisively, the Sniping Duo archetype is ALREADY BUILT through this route. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts carries entries for four of its six feats whose `when` clauses name the relationship in prose: sniping-duo-dedication line 629 ("on the damage roll of your next Strike against a target your spotter just hit..."), exploit-opening line 630 ("after your spotter critically succeeds at a..."), duos-aim line 631, triangulate line 2769 ("if you and your spotter see the target"). The relationship is reachable on the sheet today. `vantage-shot` and `targeted-redirection` merely lack their entries — a promised-but-empty defect in an existing lane (`situational`, plus a `choice`/`kind:'text'` slot on the dedication for the spotter's name), which is the ordinary output of this audit, not a hole in the vocabulary.

And a structured pointer would buy zero computation over the free-text one. Every Sniping Duo benefit is gated on an in-play event the app never observes: "whenever you or your spotter successfully Strikes a target", "your spotter critically succeeds at a Strike", "as long as both you and your spotter can see the target". Even a perfect live link to the teammate's sheet cannot tell the app whether the spotter hit. The pointer's entire yield is substituting a name into a `situational.when` string — presentation of a recorded pick, which the choice lane does already. A picker that autocompletes from `party.ts` summaries instead of accepting free text would be a UI refinement of an existing lane (compare `OpenChoiceFrom.type: 'own-companion'`), not a new capability.

Two further notes against the proposal. The dedication text explicitly says "your spotter doesn't need to spend any feats of their own to grant the effects" — so nothing needs writing to the other sheet, and there is no data to push across the party link. And the owner already ruled on ally-facing effects generally (Ruling F): ally-instant grants nothing at all, ally-timed becomes a display-only mode on the ACTIVATOR. Nothing is ever written to another character's sheet by design, so a slot whose purpose is to address one has no consumer to serve.

refuted.name: material-on-unarmed-strikes
refuted.why:
Covered by the `grantsStrike` lane's `unarmedTraits` rider, routed off the pick the record already stores.

First, the premise fails. The reviewer disqualifies `unarmedTraits` because "it is the material specifically that resistance and weakness text keys on," implying the app has a material-versus-resistance engine that a trait tag would be excluded from. It does not, for any item. `item.material` (types.ts:1967) is read in exactly three non-mechanical places: ItemDetail.tsx:118-121 + :293 build a display label ("Cold iron (high)"), ItemEditorModal.tsx:183/:596 edit it, filterSpecs.ts:137 uses it as a shop facet. The `Strike` interface (derive.ts:1837-1883) has no material field at all, and nothing in derive.ts's strike pipeline reads `item.material`. Verified against live data: Eclipse carries `material: {type:'cold-iron',grade:'low'}`, and its Strike renders traits agile/deadly-d6/finesse/light/magical/thrown-20/versatile-s with no material anywhere. So the item-only `material` lane never fires material-vs-resistance either; the distinction between "a material field" and "a trait tag" is a distinction without a difference here — both are display strings, and only one of them reaches the strike. (The resolution the reviewer wants — 'resistance 10 except cold iron', 'weakness 5 to cold iron', bypassing Hardness — is on the DEFENDER, which a character sheet does not model; mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list excludes "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet.")

Second, the player-facing capability has a complete existing route, no new engine. The record already stores the metal: `precious-alloys` in public/core.json carries `choice: {flag:'material', kind:'array', options:[adamantine, cold-iron, silver]}` with `maxTakable: 3` — so "there is nowhere to store it" is already false. Set `choice.ownsFeature: true` and point the three option values at feature records; `choiceOwnedFeatureIds` (derive.ts:2159-2167, reached from ownedFeatureIds at derive.ts:2131) turns each pick into an owned class feature; `applyUnarmedRiders` (derive.ts:3017) reads `unarmedTraits` off owned class features (derive.ts:3023) and merges `add: ['cold-iron']` into every unarmed Strike's trait list via mergeTraits (derive.ts:3041), with `match`/`fromRecord` available to narrow to specific attacks; MainTab.tsx:377-386 renders `s.traits` on the strike row as clickable InfoTerms and StrikeDetailModal opens on it. 24 feats already ship this exact `{add:[...]}` shape (effortless-reach, deadly-strikes, mischievous-tail).

The accumulation worry also dissolves: three copies of the feat are three entries in `c.feats`, each with its own `choice.value`, and choiceOwnedFeatureIds iterates that array — three owned features, three tags on the strike. Net result: `unarmedTraits` gives an unarmed attack a strictly BETTER material surfacing than the item `material` lane gives a real cold-iron longsword, whose material never reaches its Strike at all.

refuted.name: character-projected-emanations
refuted.why: Lane J `mode` covers this, and it is already doing so in production for both halves of the cluster. (1) `mode` is defined in docs/mechanic-lanes.md as "a state you turn on and off — a stance, a rage, AN AURA, 'while X is active'", satisfied by the record's `modes`/`stances` data plus `note` for clauses that are worth printing but not computable. The reviewer compared against sense/vision and correctly rejected it, but never tested the lane the manual actually points auras at. (2) The thermal-nimbus damaging aura is ALREADY stored and ALREADY displayed: scripts/data/stances.json `thermal-nimbus` = "Choose cold or fire; you and allies in your kinetic aura gain resistance equal to your level to that type, and creatures starting or moving into the aura take half-your-level damage of the chosen type", and src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:878-880 renders the active stance's note as `.stance-note` under the stance chips. Radius, damage amount, damage type and both positional triggers are on the sheet, owned by the character, appearing only while the toggle is on — which is precisely what the gold entry demands. The self-side resistance is separately computed via effectChoices -> resistances `@actor.level` in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. (3) Light emission at exactly the claimed shape is live in ~9 modes in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json: `item-bioluminescent-stripes` ("You shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for the next 20 feet"), `item-draft-of-stellar-radiance`, `item-golden-wings`/`-greater`/`-major`/`-true`, `starlight-armor`, `item-abysium-chunk`/`-ingot`. So "nothing expresses light emission" is factually false. Ascended Celestial Dedication's own text ("You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action") makes it a textbook `mode`; the missing thing there is one authored mode row of a kind that already exists 203 times, not a system. (4) A radius emanation with a trigger on creatures entering it also already exists as a feat mode: `feat-aegis-for-the-innocent` (category "Ally effects", predefined, feats-gated) — "An ally inside your nimbus is barriered: they have +1 status AC and enemies in/entering it must save vs your class or spell DC. While it runs, your nimbus area is halved." Also `form-a-flock` ("Enemies in the flock aura are dazzled") and the three `item-maelstromic-destabilizer-*` modes. Two reinforcing refutations if the mode lane were somehow disallowed. NOT-ONE-SYSTEM: the cluster's two members share only the unit "feet". Illumination has bright/dim tiers, no target, no roll, and changes no number; the kinetic aura has dice, a damage type and two turn-timing triggers resolved against other creatures. Building either buys nothing toward the other — by the "has a radius" test, senses (darkvision 60 ft), speeds (fly 40 ft) and reach would also be one system. OUT-OF-SCOPE: the damage half is squarely on the manual's NOT-lane list ("Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet"), needs per-creature positions this app deliberately does not model (the embedded tracker holds initiative and stat blocks, not a grid), and illumination level is battlefield/GM state. The owner already ruled on exactly this and the ruling is written into the data: the destabilizer notes say the emanation's weakness "is target-facing and isn't applied to your sheet", and Ruling F set ally-timed radius content as a display-only mode on the activator. Residual real work: author one mode row for ascended-celestial-dedication (bright 30/dim 60, ally +1 status vs fear, suppress/reestablish as 1 action). That is a data gap in an existing lane, not an absent system.

refuted.name: strike-availability-gates
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The reviewer's floor -- print the restriction ON the strike rather than in the feat's description -- is exactly what the `situational` lane (section J) already does, and the reason given for rejecting it ("this is not a modifier") is false about the lane's contract.

1. situational is not a modifier lane. Its header in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts says "It is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number," and `SituationalBonus.bonus` is documented as "The modifier, e.g. \"+1 circumstance\", **or a short effect phrase**." 343 of the 4,097 shipped entries carry a non-numeric `bonus`. One of them is a `strikeAttack` entry with no number at all: `see-the-unseen` -- when "targeting an adjacent undetected creature of your level or lower", bonus "it is only hidden from you (DC 11 flat check) rather than undetected". Pure prose about the TARGET's state, filed on a strike.

2. It lands on the strike, not on the feat. src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:402 calls `statHasSituational(character, { kind: 'strikeAttack', instanceId: s.instanceId }, content)` and renders a `*` on that strike's row; src/rules/explain.ts case 'strikeAttack' (line 932) and case 'strikeDamage' (985) print every `when`/`bonus` line in that strike's own breakdown popup. The strike row and the strike's breakdown are the two surfaces the reviewer asked for.

3. The identical clause already ships, on a granted Strike, keyed to the same target state. situationalBonuses.ts:723 -- `"strangle": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'strikeDamage' }], when: "on a successful Strangle Strike against a creature you already have grabbed or restrained", ... }]`. Also `fierce-grasp` (line 212, "against attacks from a foe you have grabbed or restrained"). "Grabbed or restrained by you" is already a first-class `when` string in this app.

4. There is a second existing route with a live precedent. `caustic-nectar` is the one feat in public/core.json carrying BOTH `grantedStrikes` and `note`, and its note is precisely a per-strike usage clause: "Your nectar adds no critical specialization effect, and you are immune to your own." That renders via src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:75 (`withPicks` appends "Note: ...").

5. zombie-dedication already carries its `grantedStrikes` entry in public/core.json (Jaws, d8 piercing, brawling) and has no `note` and no FEAT_SITUATIONAL key. By the lanes doc's own taxonomy that is "promised but empty" -- a missing one-line authoring on an existing lane, not a lane this app has never built. Compare the doc's two real holes (`builtInRunes`, `armorTyped`), where the note reads "no field exists."

6. The ceiling the reviewer actually wants -- a machine-evaluated legality predicate that suppresses the row -- is independently out of scope, so no residue survives. mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list excludes "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet"; `Character.conditions` (types.ts:3415) holds only the character's OWN conditions and there is no target/enemy model anywhere in src/rules. The codebase has already ruled on this shape twice in situationalBonuses.ts: Ruling M chose "a PERMANENT star with the positional condition in the note" for a condition "the app can never know," and `aura-of-courage` is commented "an ally's conditions are not this sheet." A predicate would have nothing to read.

7. The cluster is also not two records. Both gold-freetext.json entries (indices 19 and 25) are the SAME clause of the SAME feat, zombie-dedication, seen by the `numbers` and `unmodellable` lenses. Cluster size is one feat, double-counted.

Per-strike addressing, if ever wanted for a narrower star, also already exists: `UnarmedRider.match` (name substring) and `UnarmedRider.fromRecord` (the granting record's id, fails closed) at types.ts:325.

refuted.name: subsystem-retagging-of-a-grant
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The proposal's stated mechanism does not exist, in the rules or in this app.

1) The rules do not key on the 'revelation spell' category. C:\wonderers guide\aon-2e-archive\data\by-category\class\class-61.json (Oracle, Player Core 2) defines the trigger as a TRAIT: "Abilities with this trait... When you use a cursebound ability, you become cursebound 1, or... increase the value... by 1." Escalation keys on `cursebound`, not on being a revelation spell. The app already stores that trait on the spell record (`spells[<id>].traits`; 5 spells in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\public\core.json carry `cursebound`). There is no 'revelation spell' trait in PF2e at all — the `revelation` trait that does exist in core.json is the divination trait on Truesight/See the Unseen, unrelated. So the carrier the reviewer says is missing is a trait field the app has.

2) This app has no cursebound engine to fail to fire. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\classResources.ts:112 defines Cursebound as a MANUAL counter (`kind:'counter', meter:true, refresh:'rest'`) whose own note reads "Rises when you use cursebound abilities" — the player ticks it. The stage effects are four manual exclusive modes (src/rules/modes.ts:150-154, `cat-cursebound-1..4`) plus per-curse notes (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3299-3312). Nothing in src/ reads the `cursebound` trait — grep returns only those manual definitions. A native mystery revelation spell escalates the curse exactly as much as the Domain Fluency grant does: zero, by design. The delta the proposal depends on is nil, so nothing is "silently not firing".

3) The app never partitions focus spells by subsystem, so there is no wrong bucket to be in. build.ts:2457-2487 pushes ONE entry named 'Focus spells' whose `tradition` and `keyAbility` come from `focusCls` — the character's own focus-casting class. Grep finds no 'Revelation spells' / 'Domain spells' / 'Composition spells' sections anywhere. That means the mechanically load-bearing half of "which you cast as a revelation spell" — the spell uses the ORACLE's divine tradition, Cha, spell DC and attack rather than a cleric's — is already correct and automatic, precisely because the app is subsystem-blind. Storage also already declines to treat it as domain access: core.json's `domain-fluency` carries only `focusPoolBonus: 1` plus `effectChoices` with `grant.focusSpells`, and no `domains` entry.

4) Nothing in PF2e consumes the category either. Of 6,206 feats only 8 mention 'revelation spell' (domain-acumen, domain-fluency, advanced/greater/first-revelation, diverse-mystery, blaze-of-revelation, paradoxical-mystery) and every one of them GRANTS a named spell or gates on the Cursebound VALUE (blaze-of-revelation: "Requirements You are Cursebound 4"). No feat reads a set of revelation spells. There is no consumer for the tag to feed.

5) Even Foundry declines. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\.import-src\pf2e\packs\pf2e\feats\class\oracle\level-12\domain-fluency.json and level-2\domain-acumen.json both have `rules: []`. The reference implementation with a full rule engine adds no trait and no retag. Whether the remaster grant is even cursebound is a GM ruling: the LEGACY mystery text said "cast as a revelation spell with the cursebound trait", the remaster feats deliberately drop that clause.

Existing route for the only residue that remains (a printed reminder): the `note` lane — a feat's own `note` renders on the Feats tab (src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:75, live since 2026-08-06) — plus `spellSources` (build.ts:2486, types.ts:3100), which already labels the spell "· from Domain Fluency" on the Spells page (SpellsTab.tsx:1299-1305). Concrete fix: one `note` on `domain-fluency` in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json saying the granted spell is cast as a revelation spell and, if your GM rules it cursebound, tick the Cursebound meter. That is a field on one existing lane, not a system.

Finally, the cluster is not a cluster: both gold-freetext entries (lines 891-901) are the SAME feat and the SAME six-word clause under two lenses. Domain Acumen, its identical-clause prerequisite, is not even in the cluster.

refuted.name: recurring-upkeep-obligations
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The primary lane is `mode` (mechanic-lanes.md §J), with `grantsAction` for the clearing activity; `dailyChoice` also works, and the reviewer's objection to it is factually wrong.

1. The printed text is a STATE, not an obligation. Verified against the pristine AoN archive (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-3557.json) and public/core-descriptions.json: "Each day after your rest period, your body is deteriorated due to natural decay... While your body is deteriorated, you're slowed 1. You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints... to recover from deterioration." mechanic-lanes.md line 124 defines `mode` as "a state you turn on and off - a stance, a rage, an aura, 'while X is active'". Deteriorated is that, verbatim. 203 modes ship in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json; 97 are feat-gated by exactly the field a zombie mode needs (`feats: ['zombie-dedication']`), and ModeDef already carries `duration` ("the printed duration... The app has no clock - this tells the player what they are tracking; they switch it off") and `note`. Modes with `modifiers: []` carrying only a note and a duration are the shipped norm, not a workaround. Modes are pinnable to the vitals rail (src/data/prefs.ts `pinnedModes`, src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:106), so the state sits visibly on the sheet until cleared - which IS "an outstanding item surfaced that the player clears".

2. THE DECISIVE POINT: the proposed system is a WORSE model than the lane that already exists. The same paragraph gives deterioration a SECOND entry route that has nothing to do with rest - "some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body." That arrives mid-adventure, off a die roll. A rest-cycle to-do list would cover one trigger and be silently wrong for the other. A toggleable state covers both, whatever caused it. Building the reviewer's system would replace a correct model with an incomplete one.

3. The clearing activity is `grantsAction`. scripts/data/effect-backfill.json already carries 162 `grantsActions` backfills whose whole purpose is surfacing an activity described inside a granting record's own text (types.ts:242 - "the action was described inside the granting record's text and sat in content.actions unowned"). An authored "Repair Deterioration" entry in scripts/data/actions-additions.json plus one backfill row is the same data edit made 162 times already.

4. "Neglect has a mechanical consequence" is already wired. Slowed is first-class valued play state (core.json conditions.slowed `valued: true`; condAdd/condSet/condRemove in src/rules/play.ts:897-907), and `restConditions` deliberately does NOT clear Slowed - rest() only removes Fatigued/Wounded/Dying and steps Doomed/Drained. So a deterioration Slowed 1 correctly survives sleep and goes away only when the player clears it. That is precisely the persistence the reviewer says has no home.

5. The reviewer's stated reason `dailyChoice` cannot express it - "there is no answer here" - is wrong on its own terms. The answer is "did you spend the 10 minutes": a two-option `choice.daily` array whose "skipped" branch carries the payload through `dailyChoiceGrants` (src/rules/derive.ts:1048), which re-derives nightly so today's answer replaces yesterday's. And the "to-do rather than a picker" distinction they want already exists behaviourally: in src/sheet/CharacterSheet.tsx the "Prepare for the day" button is `disabled={needsAsking.some((ch) => !dailyAnswer(ch.key))}` with the title "Make each of today's choices first". An unanswered daily item literally blocks the daily-preparations flow until it is cleared. That is a blocking to-do, not a picker.

6. Cluster size is 1 of 183, and it is a singleton by measurement, not by luck: 123 feats in core-descriptions.json reference "daily preparations"/"after your rest period", and every other one of them already sits in `dailyChoice` or `dailyItems`. The app even has the analogous precedent one level out - rest() comments "vehicles & siege weapons need Repair, not rest", i.e. a body that does not heal overnight and needs a repair activity is a shape this codebase already reasons about.

SEPARATE, REAL, AND NOT THIS SYSTEM: core.json's zombie-dedication record is genuinely thin - it has `grantedStrikes` and `immunities` (from effect-backfill.json) but no `modes`, no `grantsActions`, and no `speedPenalty` for "Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet", and its jaws strike carries no availability restriction. Those are missing BACKFILL ROWS in lanes that already exist (`mode`, `grantsAction`, `speedPenalty`), not evidence of a missing lane. Fixing them requires zero new engine code.

refuted.name: degree-of-success-remap
refuted.why: The `situational` lane already IS this system, and a second lane (`RECORD_MARKERS`) covers the action-scoped half. The proposal rests on a false premise about the field's type: situationalBonuses.ts:74 declares `bonus: string` with the doc comment "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE". Nothing parses it as a number — featSituationalLines passes it through verbatim, situationalList interpolates it, statMarkClass stars the stat on presence alone. 118 distinct records already use it for exactly this shift, including the canonical PF2e family (agile-mind, anvils-hardness, battle-hardened, juggernaut, resolve, evasion, will-of-the-pupil, irrepressible, haughty-obstinacy, dragonblood, fluid-contortionist), plus nocturnal-navigator ("one degree of success better"), savage-critical ("a natural 19 that would be a success is a critical success instead" — the branched-tree-of-pain shape), and sacred-body itself. Two more are authored in DATA and survive `npm run data`: hunters-hagbook and immaculate-instrument in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json. Every filter the reviewer calls missing exists and is in use. (1) Named skill ACTION: RECORD_MARKERS is keyed on the action slug and quick-unlock is already filed under id:'pick-a-lock' (slug = name.toLowerCase().replace(...), so "Pick a Lock" → pick-a-lock); sure-feet is `{on:'action', id:'balance', value:"success -> crit success"}`; nine marker records carry remaps (the-publican, student-of-the-canon, sturdy-bindings, sure-feet, caveclimber-kobold, cliffscale-lizardfolk, fishseeker-shoony, paddler-shoony, experienced-professional). Rendered live by MainTab.tsx:502, StatDetailModal.tsx:183, VitalsRail.tsx:1026. (2) Incoming effect's trait: irrepressible "against an emotion effect", cantorian-reinforcement "against a disease or poison" — verbatim adhyabhau's and divine-health's filters. (3) Activity + skill CATEGORY: the `lore:*` wildcard is live in targetMatches, and celebrity-dedication is already [crafting, performance, lore:*] + when "to Earn Income…"; unmistakable-lore is lore:* + "critical failure becomes failure". (4) Someone else's roll: aon-vulture ("this applies to the VULTURE's saves, not yours"), shared-resolve ("you and your eidolon"), artillerist-dedication ("whole crew") — the established Ruling N/G shape; a non-party patient is another creature's sheet, which mechanic-lanes.md lists under NOT-lanes. (5) Self-only vs ally-shared inside one feat: scope is per ENTRY, not per record — precedent bravos-brew-greater (two save entries, one reading "this replaces the +3, it does not stack; a success against fear becomes a critical success"), born-of-item, steadying-stone. (6) Gated on owning Sacred Body: a real built mechanism — modifiesGrant.from + actionRider (types.ts:764) produces grantMarkers in build.ts:3274 ONLY when ownedIds.has(mod.from), rendering by the same marker route; prose precedent in cantorian-reinforcement, irrepressible, hardened-harrow-deck, animal-skin. Two of the six named exemplars already carry the whole thing: experienced-professional's marker note contains both clauses AND the ordering caveat ("a critical failure becomes a failure; if you're an expert in Lore, a failed check earns twice as much income (unless it was originally a critical failure)"), and hydraulic-maneuvers line 2655 carries all three of its clauses in one bonus string ("range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure"). robust-recovery line 2219 carries the +4-instead-of-+2 replacement with the patient framing. adhyabhau and divine-health have entries with only the numeric half authored, and adroit-manipulation has none — those are mechanic-lanes.md's "promised but empty" bucket, one-line authoring gaps in existing lanes, not a missing lane. Closing the case architecturally: the app never computes a degree of success at all — dice.ts rolls a d20 and flags only outcome?:'crit'|'fumble' from the natural face, and no DC is ever compared anywhere — so a remap in this app can only be an authored player-facing statement on the right stat or action row, which is precisely what both lanes do and what the manual states as their design ("DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number"). Secondary: the cluster also conflates unrelated capabilities behind the shift — bonus suppression and range-on-a-skill-action (hydraulic-maneuvers), flat-check targeting (already conventionalized as kind:'hp' + "on the flat check to recover from persistent X" in cindersoul/fire-lung/fire-savvy, plus persistent-damage condition markers on stone-blood/mutated-fleshwarp/steelskin-hobgoblin), ally-scoped output at a different value, and an Earn Income money multiplier for a downtime activity the app only lists as text (actions.ts:123) and never computes.

refuted.name: timed-effect-tracker
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the lane is `situational` (lane J, C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), and three of the reviewer's four example feats are ALREADY carrying exactly the clauses they claim have nowhere to go. The premise fails at the data.

1) The reviewer's "situational is only for bonuses" is false by the lane's own contract. `SituationalBonus.bonus` is documented as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE", and the `when` string is the scope. Both are rendered: explain.ts:405 `situationalList()` -> StatDetailModal.tsx:106 prints the star and the full when/bonus pair in the stat popup.

2) `hydraulic-maneuvers` (situationalBonuses.ts:2655) already ships all three of its "unmodellable" needs verbatim: when = "on the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers", bonus = "range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure". The "pending one-shot rider that fires only if your next action is one of three named maneuvers" IS the `when`. Also: hydraulic-maneuvers is itself a 1-action activity, so this is the internal resolution of the action it grants — a NOT-a-lane per mechanic-lanes.md ("The internal steps of an activity … Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane").

3) `on-my-best-day` (situationalBonuses.ts:768) already ships: when = "until the end of your next turn after an Incarnation Lore check with On My Best Day…", bonus = "+1 to +3 status (by degree of success; on a critical failure it applies only to the next attack against you)". The one-shot "consumed by the next attack against you" scope is stored, and so is the four-outcome degree-of-success scaling. The Sustain-with-a-cap shape is a shipping, authored pattern in the same table: `tidal-shield` (line 490) = "…until the end of your next turn (Sustain up to 5 rounds)"; `soul-vessel-mount` (line 605) = "for 1 minute after it consumes a stored soul (Sustain Seize Soul)"; `empowered-onslaught` (line 2458) = "once per round when you critically hit and Sustain your own Benediction…" — which is simultaneously a Sustain cap AND a roll-RESULT trigger, the two things the reviewer says are unrepresentable.

4) `critter-shape`: the "1-hour lockout measured from when it ENDED" is Paizo's own printed frequency — the feat's FIRST sentence is "Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape" — and the record already carries `limitedUses {max:1, per:'hour'}` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, and live in public/core.json). The audit's assertion that "a cooldown measured from when the effect ended is not the same thing as a per-hour use allowance" is contradicted by the source text, which wrote it as a per-hour allowance. The 10-minute cap is the printed-duration lane (ModeDef.duration, and NOT inert: durationMinutes() parses it, `match.minDurationMinutes` selects on it, Extend Elixir doubles it). The revert to hybrid shape is Change Shape, an action the text names and the app links; `exclusiveGroup` already makes shape states mutually exclusive.

5) `inspire-imitation` has nothing to store on THIS sheet. Aid's bonus lands on the ALLY's check (the app models the receiving side as mode `cat-aid` with appliesWhen "an ally successfully Aids this check"); what remains for this character is a permission — Aid without Prepare to Aid — i.e. lane J `note`. "Remember which skill you last critically succeeded with" is only a requirement if the app resolves checks against DCs and gates reactions off the outcome, which it does not do; that is VTT automation, not a sheet field.

6) The load-bearing claim "the app has no clock" is a quote about the modes TOGGLE, not about the app. Heroes Heaven does have live effect instances with real lifetimes, a clock that expires them, and cooldowns — in the tracker: `AppliedCondition.duration` in rounds with `autoDecrement`, ticked at turn start (combatStore.ts:75 tickConditionsAtStart) and turn end (combatStore.ts:489-501), removed on expiry, applied to PC combatants as well as monsters; user-authorable via `CustomCondition` (tracker/src/store/customConditionsStore.ts) which carries name, description, defaultDuration in rounds, isPermanent, autoDecrement, typed `mods`, and situational `condMods` with a `when`; and StatBlock.tsx:892 `rollAbilityCooldown` AUTO-GENERATES a cooldown — it reads "can't use again for 1d4 rounds" out of ability prose, rolls it, and applies a same-named condition for that many rounds. That is the round clock, on the surface where PF2e actually measures encounter durations.

Secondary refutation if any of the above were doubted: the cluster is also not-one-system. It bundles a wall-clock lifetime on a persistent form (critter-shape), an action-economy Sustain relationship (on-my-best-day), two event-consumed one-shot scopes with no clock at all (the next incoming attack; your next action), and a roll-outcome memory that would require a check-resolution engine (inspire-imitation). Building a clock delivers none of the last three, so "timed-effect-tracker" is not the shape of the alleged gap.

Honest residual (not a system): nothing on the SHEET auto-extinguishes a mode pill when its printed duration lapses — the player switches it off. That is a documented deliberate decision (modes.ts:316 and ModeDef.duration), and the missing piece is automation of clauses that are already stored, already displayed, and already gated by limitedUses — not a missing capability.

refuted.name: standard-action-overrides
refuted.why:
Covered by the `situational` lane — specifically its action-marker half, `RECORD_MARKERS` in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3181 (RecordMarker: {on:'action'|'condition', id, value?, note}), reachable from data via `modifiesGrant.actionRider` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:764, applied in build.ts:3264-3290) and rendered by `recordMarkersFor` (src/rules/explain.ts:297).

The reviewer measured src/rules/skillActions.ts and stopped there. They missed C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:183 — `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionSlug(a.name))` runs for EVERY row of the catalogue they say has no per-character layer. The layer exists: it is keyed by action slug, gated on records the character actually owns, and shows the changed value inline in parentheses plus a star to the source. And the catalogue itself is already per-character on both axes the reviewer wanted: `skillActionsFor(skill, rank, hasFeat)` (skillActions.ts:1007-1014) filters by the character's live rank in THAT skill and by `hasFeat`, recomputed on every open — StatDetailModal.tsx:55 feeds it the character's own feats. So 'gated per-skill on being master, recomputed as proficiencies rise' is the mechanism's default behaviour, not a gap.

Each of the four named asks already has a shipped precedent of its exact shape:

1. Rewrite an action's cost, gated on master in one skill (quick-recognition) → RECORD_MARKERS['quick-unlock'] = [{on:'action', id:'pick-a-lock', value:'1 action', note:'You Pick a Lock using 1 action instead of 2.'}] (situationalBonuses.ts:3209). Quick Unlock is the same feat shape (level 7 general skill feat, prerequisite master in Thievery, actionCost passive, and it carries NO other field in core.json). Same lane again in 'swift-prey' (hunt-prey → 'free action (first action of your turn)') and 'unlimited-esoterica' (exploit-vulnerability/intensify-vulnerability → 'free action', with the once-per-round clause carried in the same note — quick-recognition's entire clause, already built for another feat).

2. The reviewer's stated reason for rejecting modifiesGrant is factually wrong about this app's data. 'Recognize a Spell is a universal basic action, not something a specific record granted' — in core.json it is the FEAT `recognize-spell` (level 1, category skill, actionCost reaction), which is Quick Recognition's own printed prerequisite. `modifiesGrant.from` gates on owning exactly that record, and `actionRider.actionId` defaults to `from` for the documented 'or IS, when `from` is itself an action record' case. The catalogue row 'Recognize Spell' even slugs to `recognize-spell`, so the marker lands on it.

3. Waive a usage prerequisite of a universal action (inspire-imitation / Aid) → RECORD_MARKERS['the-publican'] already puts {on:'action', id:'aid', value:'crit fail → fail'} on the Aid row, so Aid is a live override target. Prerequisite waivers on universal actions are routine here: 'woodstalker-lizardfolk' on take-cover ('even if you are not next to an obstacle'), 'vine-leshy' on climb ("you don't need any hands free"), 'athamasi' on climb and grab-an-edge ('even if one or both primary hands are full'), 'stitch-flesh' widening Treat Wounds' legal targets, 'feather-step' on step ('You can Step into difficult terrain'). 'fancy-moves' even rewrites which skill Demoralize rolls.

4. Give a melee maneuver a range (hydraulic-maneuvers) → ALREADY BUILT, situationalBonuses.ts:2655: bonus: 'range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure', scoped by when: 'on the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers'. All three sub-clauses the gold entries call unmodellable are on the sheet today. SituationalLine.bonus is documented as accepting non-numeric phrases, and distance values already ride action rows ('black-powder-boost' leap +10 feet, 'armbands-of-athleticism-greater' climb/swim +10 feet, 'dancing-leaf', 'fantastic-leaps'). Disarm/Shove/Trip rows exist with slugs disarm/shove/trip and 'the-harder-they-fall-ranger' already marks trip. Degree-of-success remaps are also a shipped pattern: 'experienced-professional' earn-income 'crit fail -> fail', 'defy-death' on dying.

5. Lift a rank gate (clever-improviser) → `situational` with targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'all'}], precedent RECORD in situationalBonuses.ts:246 — 'innate-understanding', whose `when` is literally 'attempting a trained-only skill action while untrained'. The app already has an authored entry at exactly that scope. Clever Improviser's other half is already carried (featFeatGrants.ts:42 → untrained-improvisation).

Secondary refutation if the primary were rejected: the cluster is also not-one-system. 'A per-character override of a catalogue field' bundles a blanket display-filter permission (clever-improviser), a cost rewrite (quick-recognition), a waiver keyed to a transient roll-OUTCOME state (inspire-imitation), and a one-shot pending next-action rider carrying a range plus bonus suppression plus a degree shift (hydraulic-maneuvers). The genuinely hard parts of entries 3 and 4 are the transient-state machinery, which has nothing to do with overriding a catalogue field and which the gold entries themselves file as separate needs.

Net: quick-recognition and inspire-imitation are 'promised but empty' — the lane exists, is in use on close cousins, and these two records simply have not been authored into it. That is the manual's defect bucket, not a missing lane.

refuted.name: referenced-record-parameter-overrides
refuted.why:
Refuted on all three exemplars, and the framing premise is backwards.

(1) "Import just one piece" — hybrid-study-spell is ALREADY BUILT and correct. In C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json the feat carries `focusPoolBonus: 1` plus an `effectChoices` block listing all eight hybrid studies, each option's payload being exactly `grant: { focusSpells: ['<conflux spell>'] }` and nothing else. The claim that "the choice lanes hand over whole options, so nothing keeps this from silently granting a full subclass" is false at the type level: `EffectChoice.options[].grant` is an `EffectGrant` — an authored literal payload, never a pointer to the referenced record. Whole-record inheritance is the OPT-IN, not the default: `FeatChoiceDef.ownsFeature` exists solely for that, and its doc comment in src/rules/types.ts:1330 says it is "OPT-IN on purpose … An accidental match would hand a dragon disciple an oracle subclass." The reviewer has the polarity inverted — partial import is what the lane does by default (247 records use effectChoices), and total import is the flag you must set.

(2) "Pin Bless's emanation at 15 feet" is a no-op override. bless already ships `baseArea: { value: 15, kind: 'emanation' }`, carries no `heightening`, and `baseArea` has exactly one reader (src/rules/heightening.ts:132 → SpellsTab.tsx:180, heightened-area DISPLAY). There is no live, mutable radius anywhere in the app, so the value being "overridden" is already the printed value and no code path could ever show anything else. The residual clause ("you can't increase it") is a prohibition on performing Bless's Sustain-to-expand — an internal step of an activity, which docs/mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list explicitly excludes. And the record is built: mode `feat-eternal-blessing` exists in core.json with `modifiers: [{ target: 'attack', type: 'status', value: 1 }]` and a note carrying "radius 15 feet (it cannot be increased)". (That also refutes the gold entry's separate claim that "the vocabulary has no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all" — mode attack modifiers reach the strike total at src/rules/derive.ts:2653.)

(3) "Deny the fly Speed pest form would give" has no referent. The spell schema has no speeds/AC/strike fields at all (spell fields are: area, baseArea, baseDamage, cast, damageKind, defense, description, duration, edition, heightening, id, name, range, rank, rarity, ritual, ritualPrimary, save, source, spellLists, targets, traditions, traits), and `pest-form`'s record is pure printed text. No route exists by which this app grants a speed from a spell, so there is nothing to subtract. critter-shape's mechanical half — re-entry once per hour — is already carried as `limitedUses: { max: 1, per: 'hour' }` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:67879).

More fundamentally, the capability class the reviewer says is absent is a shipped family of lanes, all with live readers:
• override a referenced record's printed parameter — `modeAdjust.doubleDuration` (src/rules/modes.ts:362 `adjustModes`, which reads another record's mode and returns an altered COPY per character, explicitly non-mutating); `entryRetune` (build.ts:4118, rewrites a granted spellcasting entry's tradition/key attribute); `subclass.slotProgression`; per-instance item `heldSpells` override; per-spell innate daily-uses override.
• disable one of its sub-mechanics — `modeAdjust.suppressNegativeModifiers` ("you do not suffer its drawback" — every negative modifier on the referenced mode stops applying); `checkPenaltyRelief.ignoresNoisy` (cancels a trait); `classArchetype.armorCap`/`weaponCap`/`slotCap`, whose comment states outright that adding-only fields "can take training AWAY … so a removal needs its own lane".
• deny a grant it would otherwise make — `removesWeaknesses` (derive.ts:1746, "you no longer gain silver weakness from Werecreature Dedication"); `subclass.suppressedFeatures` (build.ts:2448); `classArchetype.suppressFeatures` (build.ts:3106, 6 records); `BuildOverrides.removedFeatIds`; `modifiesGrant.deityDomainsFromChoice` (Splinter Faith REPLACES the deity's printed domains and demotes the displaced ones — derive.ts:846/`applySplinter`).

Secondary refutation, if the above is contested: the cluster is also not-one-system. Its 8 entries are three unrelated claims — a display-only spell-area value, a battle-form stat block this app never models, and a choice payload — that die to three different arguments and share no mechanism. The only thing worth logging is documentation debt: `modeAdjust`, `removesWeaknesses`, `entryRetune`, `suppressedFeatures`/`suppressFeatures` and the Overrides layer are NOT listed in docs/mechanic-lanes.md, which is very likely why a classifier reading that doc alone concluded the app can only add.

refuted.name: movement-cost-and-terrain-exemptions
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The lane is `situational` — which mechanic-lanes.md (section J) declares satisfied by "`situational`, `situationalBonuses.ts`" — specifically its RECORD_MARKERS sub-shape `{on:'action'|'condition', id:<slug>, note, value?}` declared at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3169 and exported at :3182. The reviewer's premise that "situational only modifies rolls" is factually wrong: RECORD_MARKERS lives inside that very file and by design targets an ACTION or a CONDITION, not a roll (see `quick-unlock` "Pick a Lock using 1 action instead of 2" and `feather-step`, neither of which touches any roll). It is not a bare `note` either — it renders as an action-mark tag with value + note on the specific action row it governs.

The decisive evidence: `water-dancer` at situationalBonuses.ts:3254 is fishblooded's clause-for-clause twin and ALREADY carries both of the reviewer's supposedly-unmodellable shapes:
  'water-dancer': [{"on":"action","id":"stride","note":"In an aquatic or swamp environment you ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain."},{"on":"action","id":"swim","note":"Swimming up or down isn't difficult terrain for you."}]
Shape 1 (ignore difficult terrain gated on an aquatic environment) → the `stride` marker. Shape 2 (vertical swimming stops being difficult terrain — the rule removed rather than terrain ignored) → the `swim` marker. Fishblooded's printed text is the same two sentences.

Seven more live siblings in the same lane: `feather-step` (:3233, id 'step'), `rite-of-passage` (:3285), `stonestep-shisk` (:3287), `tunnel-rat` (:3291), `unimpeded-journey` (:3292 — which even carries "treat greater difficult terrain as difficult terrain"), `wildwood-halfling` (:3295), plus `natures-edge` (:2863) using difficult terrain as a `when`. The lane has real readers, not write-only data: src/rules/explain.ts:297 `recordMarkersFor` → src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:502 (action rows), src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:183, src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:1026. Stride/Step/Swim all exist with matching slugs (src/rules/actions.ts:29,30,69) so the markers land.

Shape 3 (march-of-law: suppress terrain cost for one action's movement) is covered twice over. First by the feather-step/unimpeded-journey precedent — `{on:'action', id:'march-of-law'}` resolves, because a feat with an `actionCost` surfaces as an activity row at src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:238 and MainTab's `actionId()` slugifies its name to 'march-of-law'. Second, and more damning, by mechanic-lanes.md's own NOT-lanes rule: "The internal steps of an activity — 'make a Strike', 'you may Step'… The app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane." "Stride… ignoring difficult terrain" is a step inside March of Law's own printed text, already displayed in full on the sheet.

The extra requirement the reviewer bolts on — "'aquatic environment' must exist as a state the sheet can be in" — was already ruled against by the owner. Ruling M, documented at situationalBonuses.ts:84-90, covers precisely this: for a positional circumstance "which the app can never know," the owner chose the condition in the NOTE over a mode-gated star or a state model. And the `mode` lane already carries environment/terrain-conditioned variants anyway: `cyclonic-ascent` ("You can move upward without treating it as difficult terrain"), `item-chromatic-jellyfish-oil-lesser` ("ignore difficult terrain from tight spaces"), `geomancer-dedication` (per-terrain attunement) in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json. The project has even ruled the terrain half explicitly battlefield-side: `item-aged-arbor-wine`'s authored note ends "that is battlefield-side, not on your sheet."

So this is a COVERAGE gap — fishblooded and march-of-law are two records missing registry entries that nine siblings already have — not a missing system. Both would be fixed by appending two lines to the existing table. This is the exact failure mode project_hh_lane_measurement warns about: a gap inflated because the predicate knew only one storage location (record fields / speed lanes) and never looked at the registry that mechanic-lanes.md names as the lane's satisfier.

refuted.name: ally-facing-effect-publication
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The system as defined ("modifiers and defences that ... land on OTHER party members' sheets ... scoped by an aura radius") is out-of-scope on both of its own defining clauses: it targets another creature's sheet, and its only scoping instrument is battlemap distance. Six pieces of evidence.

1. THE OWNER ALREADY ADJUDICATED THIS EXACT QUESTION. C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\work\rulings\DECISIONS.md, section "F - Bonuses that land on someone else (17 + 3 from E) - DECIDED": "1. The bonus goes to a teammate, not you -> NOTHING on your sheet. No star, no modifier. The feat's own description already says what the ally gets. 2. BUT if it runs for a LIMITED TIME, the character who activated it gets a DISPLAY-ONLY mode ... It changes none of their numbers." Built 2026-07-30 (memory project_hh_rulings_dfgh). The reviewer's core observation - "nothing computes them or delivers them to the teammate sheets" - is the DECIDED behaviour, not an absent capability. The adjacent "D leftovers - target-side bonuses - DECIDED" ruling is the same shape: "this dosent need to have an effect the player will tel the gm", applied to Bomber's Eye Elixir and Execution Powder because "the app models neither target AC nor cover".

2. RULING F'S MECHANISM IS LIVE IN THE DATA. scripts/data/toggle-modes.json ships a mode category literally named "Ally effects" - Aegis for the Innocent and Tweak Appearances, both `modifiers: []` with notes ending "Your own AC is unchanged" / "Your own checks are unchanged". That is ruling F case 2, shipped.

3. THE REVIEWER'S HEADLINE EXAMPLE IS ALREADY BUILT, WHICH BREAKS THEIR OWN CORRECTION. They assert "only its always-on and ally-facing halves are gaps" for eternal-blessing. But toggle-modes.json contains `id: "feat-eternal-blessing"`, `duration: "permanent - you may Dismiss it, and it returns automatically after 1 minute"`, `modifiers: [{target:'attack', type:'status', value:1}]`, with a note carrying the ceil(level/2) rank, the fixed 15-foot radius, and the ally clause. The always-on half computes; the ally half is the ruling-F note. Their one "correction to the readers" is the only part they got right, and the part they kept as a gap is built.

4.
