THE RECEIVING DIRECTION HAS A FULL ROUTE - THE `mode` LANE, AND IT IS THE SHIPPED DESIGN, NOT A WORKAROUND. src/rules/modes.ts encodes ally-facing effects RECEIVER-SIDE: cat-bless (`m(1,'status','attack')`, note "Allies in the aura gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls"), cat-inspire-courage, cat-rallying-anthem, cat-song-of-strength, cat-triple-time. The ally toggles it and the number folds in through poolTypedMods with real PF2e stacking and a named breakdown line. ModeDef (src/rules/types.ts:2458) carries far more than check bonuses: `resistances`, `weaknesses`, `immunities`, `senses`, `speeds`, `grantedStrikes`, `strikeDamage`, restricted spell slots - and 75 shipped modes already carry `resistances`. So requirement 3, "resistance rather than a check bonus handed to allies" (thermal-nimbus), has an exact home; the ModeDef doc comment even names this class of case: "Triple Time (+10 ft Speed to allies) shipped as `modifiers: []` with a note, because there was no field for it" - a hole that was identified and closed. Requirement 1, "a value that differs for allies (+1 where the bearer gets +2)" (divine-health), is not a new dimension at all: the bearer's +2 is a situational star on the bearer, the ally's +1 is a separate mode on the ally. Modes are also player-authorable (ModesPanel "New mode"), so any unlisted aura is expressible without a code change.

5. THE ONE IRREDUCIBLE REQUIREMENT IS PURELY POSITIONAL - A VTT CONCERN. The radius IS the scoping instrument, and no positional model exists anywhere: `radius|emanation` in src/rules/types.ts returns nothing; `distanceTo|gridPos|coordinate` across src/rules/ and src/sheet/ returns nothing; the tracker's only `radius` hits are CSS borderRadius. "A radius borrowed from another class feature that itself grows with level" (champion's aura) is a distance with nothing to compare it against - there is no creature-to-creature distance in this app or its initiative tracker. docs/mechanic-lanes.md already excludes this under NOT lanes: "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet."

6. DELIVERY IS ARCHITECTURALLY THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT EXISTS. src/data/party.ts: a teammate is a PUBLISHED SNAPSHOT in Supabase `campaign_characters`, fetched "lazily when a card is tapped", and "All calls degrade to no-op/empty when signed out or the table is missing." A party member is not a live participant in another character's derive(). "Compute on the holder's sheet, land on the teammate's" would be a cloud-mediated cross-character derive that silently yields nothing offline - so the Campaigns feature the reviewer cites as making delivery a short hop is precisely what makes it unsound.

SECONDARY: the cluster is not one system either. robust-recovery's "or someone else uses one of these actions on you" is not publication - it sits on the holder's own sheet, and its real content is (a) overwriting a skill activity's printed output, for which ruling D already built RECORD_MARKERS on the action ("Treat Wounds shows (d10) * from Magic Hands"), and (b) degree-of-success promotion, which the same gold-freetext entries raise independently for divine-health and ascended-celestial-dedication and which is a different proposed system. Bundling an inbound outcome-tier remap with outbound aura geometry conflates unrelated capabilities.

Net: everything in this cluster that belongs on a character sheet is already expressible through the modes lane; the residue is another creature's sheet plus battlemap distance, both already ruled out by the owner and by the manual's own NOT-lanes list.

refuted.name: repeatable-record-cross-instance-rules
refuted.why:
The proposal is a conjunction of three capabilities with three different statuses, welded together by nothing but the words "selected more than once".

(1) Per-taking independent picks — EXISTS, and the reviewer concedes it. choiceKeys() (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/build.ts:437), build.ts:2721 pushing `choice: featChoiceById[slotKey], slotKey` per taking, grantedBySlot at build.ts:2766, round-trip at build.ts:5007.

(2) "All the answers together form one menu" — EXISTS structurally and needs no new system. The built feats array is a MULTISET: one entry per taking, each with its own choice, and every effect lane iterates it per instance — choiceGrants[fc.choice.value] in the proficiency loop (build.ts:2927), grantedStrikes/FEAT_CHOICE_STRIKES (build.ts:1212), counterMods.ts's `repeatable` flag, and build.ts:1009 which says outright "NOT deduped: Multilingual is repeatable and taking it twice grants twice as many languages". For divine-access the accumulator is already built and already a Set union feeding the repertoire add/swap picker (Builder.tsx:441-469), with spellListAdditions {from:'deity', max:3, as:'list'} shipping on blessed-blood-sorcerer and 472 of 485 deities carrying their granted spells.

(3) Cross-taking exclusion — a DIFFERENT thing from (1) and (2): a builder-side legality filter, not a sheet mechanic, and it is already shipped twice. shared.tsx:3538 (LanguageEditor) and shared.tsx:3491 (SkillEditor) compute `available` by excluding every answer already chosen by ANY source or taking, so repeatable Multilingual's four slots pool into one list with one exclusion-filtered picker. armorCascade (build.ts:2964-2970) is the state-gated form: each taking reads what earlier takings granted, advances to the next option, and writes its own answer onto that taking's fc.choice so three identical rows read Light/Medium/Heavy. What is genuinely narrow is only FeatChoiceDef.distinct's scope inside choiceOptionsFor (build.ts:443) — an existing flag with a one-slot scope, and the choice lane already ships the designated route for a printed restriction it cannot enforce (FeatChoiceDef.note, types.ts ~1380; divine-access already carries one).

The "one menu at use time" half is also factually false for two of the three named feats. Precious Alloys' answers apply simultaneously and passively — the reviewer's own words are "three metals both live on your unarmed strikes", which is a union with no menu. Divine Access's answers widen a build-time picker, no menu, and duplicate answers cannot change the sheet because the accumulator is a Set. Only Energized Spark has a per-use election, and it has that election at ONE taking too (spirit or fire?) because its EFFECT is elective; repeatability merely lengthens the list.

Strip the conflation and the 7 entries resolve into three unrelated absences already logged separately in the same gold file — precious material on a non-item strike (144/145; types.ts:1968's Item.material is the only material field) plus a level-gated option list (146); the deity-to-spells wiring on the existing spellListAdd lane (108/110/112, and the record's own `inert` string names that cause); and elective source-scoped damage-type substitution (153/155/156) — with a duplicate-pick guard as the residue. That is two or more unrelated capabilities in one cluster, not one missing system.

refuted.name: modifier-and-penalty-suppression
refuted.why:
REFUTED by the `situational` lane, and the exemplar record already carries it verbatim. The premise "every modifier lane adds and none withholds" is factually false about this app. `SituationalBonus.bonus` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts, interface ~L71) is documented as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE" — a free string, not a signed number — and the registry is declared display-only ("nothing here changes a computed number"). Of 4,097 live bonus strings, 88 withhold rather than add: "ignore the range increment penalty" (masterful-hunter L2130, shootists-edge L2610), "no range penalty (cancels the usual -2)" (triangulate L2769), "-1 instead of -2 range penalty" (far-throw L2719), "armor check penalty does not apply" (x2), "the -2 item penalty does not apply", "ignores the -4 circumstance penalty for not sharing a language", "ignore Demoralize's -4 circumstance language penalty". Separately the `mode` lane carries 95 negative-valued modifiers across 429 modes (ModeModifier.value is a plain number; ModeDef is documented as "a toggleable bonus/PENALTY set"), with `appliesWhen` making a mode conditional. Both lanes withhold today.

SUB-SHAPES 1 AND 2 ARE ALREADY STORED. hydraulic-maneuvers — the record the reviewer picked as proof of absence — is at situationalBonuses.ts:2655 with targets [{kind:'skill',detail:'athletics'}], when "on the Disarm, Shove or Trip check made right after Hydraulic Maneuvers", bonus "range 15 feet; you lose all item bonuses and all body-related circumstance bonuses; a critical failure becomes a failure". That one string contains BOTH the wholesale item-bonus exclusion AND the body-related circumstance subset. It reaches the sheet via statHasSituational -> featSituationalLines -> situationalList in src/rules/explain.ts (~L265-410), which stars Athletics and renders "{bonus} from {source} — {when}" in the stat popup. "Cannot express it" is refuted by the exemplar itself.

THE "SOURCE TAG" DEMAND IS OUT OF SCOPE, NOT MISSING. "Circumstance bonuses related to your physical body" is not a machine-decidable set — the rules never enumerate which circumstance bonuses are bodily, so it is a table call. Foundry pf2e, which DOES tag every modifier by type and slug, ships this exact clause as a `Note` rule element and mechanizes none of it (verified: .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/ancestry/azarketi/level-13/hydraulic-maneuvers.json — only AdjustDegreeOfSuccess is mechanical, and that is a different proposed system). Demanding a bodily-vs-not tag on every bonus asks this app to adjudicate what the reference VTT declines to.

SUB-SHAPE 3 HAS NOTHING TO SUPPRESS. The app never computes a range-increment penalty: grep for rangePenalt|range penalt|increment penalt outside the situational registry = 0 hits; targetDistance|distanceToTarget|feetToTarget|tokenDistance = 0 hits. The -2/-4 is a function of measured token-to-token distance, i.e. the battle map — which mechanic-lanes.md excludes by name ("Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet"). Foundry can emit ignore-range-penalty:3 only because it owns the map. And the reviewer's stated blocker — that bands need per-band penalties a record can override — is already demonstrated in-lane: triangulate stores "-3 at the 3rd increment, then -2 more per further increment (-5/-7/-9)", a full per-band table, and far-throw stores a per-increment substitution. Building a targeting system first, then suppressing its output, is the VTT lane this app deliberately lacks.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: twirling-throw has no situationalBonuses.ts entry at all, so its clause is unsurfaced. That is the audit method's own "promised but empty" bucket — a missing ROW in a lane that exists and that four siblings already use for this precise clause — not "no lane at all". Fix is one line copying masterful-hunter's shape: targets [{kind:'strikeAttack'}], bonus "ignore the range increment penalty (2nd and 3rd increments)". A missing entry is a defect, not a missing system.

Note: the 6-entry cluster also drags in a degree-of-success remap (critical failure -> failure) and a one-shot "your next action" pending state. Those are distinct proposed capabilities, not what this system claims to be; the suppression slice is what is judged here, and it is expressible.

refuted.name: activity-output-values
refuted.why:
The premise is factually wrong on three counts, and both example feats are already authored.

(1) The lane exists and is not `note` — it is the action/condition MARKER lane (`RecordMarker` / `RECORD_MARKERS`, src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3167-3181), the structured form of `note`. It is exactly 'a value a record can overwrite on an activity': `{ on:'action', id:<core.json action id>, value:<the CHANGED value>, note }`. The interface comment names value as "The CHANGED value, shown inline in parentheses on that row", and the lane's own docstring is the reviewer's use case verbatim: "Magic Hands makes Treat Wounds heal d10s instead of d8s… attach the mark to the thing it modifies and show the changed value inline". ~100+ records use it, including outputs that are replacements (magic-hands treat-wounds value 'd10' replacing d8s; quick-unlock pick-a-lock value '1 action' replacing 2), rank-SCALED outputs (crafters-eyepiece repair value '10 + 10 / 15 + 15 per rank'), and outputs that land on another creature (the-harder-they-fall-ranger trip value '+1d8 bludgeoning', vicious-vengeance 'the ENEMY takes…'). So 'the number lands on the patient rather than the actor' is not a new capability either.

(2) experienced-professional is ALREADY in that registry (situationalBonuses.ts:3230): { on:'action', id:'earn-income', value:'crit fail -> fail', note:'…if you're an expert in Lore, a failed check earns twice as much income (unless it was originally a critical failure)' }. It renders live: src/sheet/StatDetailModal.tsx:183 calls recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'action', actionSlug(a.name)), and actionSlug('Earn Income') === 'earn-income', so the Lore/Crafting/Performance Earn Income row shows '(crit fail -> fail)' plus a star whose tooltip carries the doubling and the expert gate.

(3) robust-recovery is ALREADY authored (situationalBonuses.ts:2219) as { kind:'save', detail:'all' }, bonus '+4 circumstance (instead of the usual +2)', when 'on your save against a disease or poison after anyone uses Treat a Disease or Treat a…'. The stored text carries the REPLACEMENT ('instead of the usual +2') and the inbound case ('after ANYONE uses'), which is the precise thing the reviewer says situational cannot do. And the lane already has a first-class concept for numbers that are not the character's own roll: SituationalTarget.dcOnly, "the bonus moves the SAVE DC — the number other creatures roll against". If the +4 is also wanted on the Medicine action rows, a RecordMarker with id 'treat-disease' / 'treat-poison' renders by the same route with no new code — that is authoring, not a missing system.

The two prerequisites claimed absent are both present. The proficiency-RANK gate: SkillAction.tiers (src/rules/skillActions.ts:19) is `{ rank: ProficiencyRank; note }`, rendered as a tier list, and Lore's Earn Income already carries trained/expert/master tiers. The level-based income table: it IS data — the full Income Earned grid (task level x trained/expert/master/legendary, including the Failure column) sits in public/core-descriptions.json under actions['earn-income'] and renders as a table in the app.

There is also a DATA-field route, not just a hand registry: modifiesGrant.actionRider (src/rules/types.ts:764) = { actionId?, value?, note }, converted to a RecordMarker in src/rules/build.ts:3277-3288 and displayed through the same single path — so a record, including homebrew, can write an activity-output override as a field.

Two fallback refutations if any of the above were disputed. not-one-system: the cluster's 6 entries are 2 clauses x 3 lenses, and the two clauses need unrelated machinery — one is a circumstance bonus routed onto a patient's save against an affliction, the other is a downtime currency calculator with a rank-gated payout multiplier and provenance memory of whether a 'failure' was laundered from a crit fail. A field satisfying one buys nothing for the other. out-of-scope: literally computing a doubled Earn Income payout requires resolving a roll against a DC the GM sets SECRETLY, for a task level the GM assigns, over a duration the GM determines (all three phrases are in the app's own earn-income text) — the 'anything the GM adjudicates' exclusion in docs/mechanic-lanes.md. The app's contract is to show the table and star the modifying note; the player adds the coin.

refuted.name: alternative-activation-costs
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The reviewer measured the wrong layer: they checked the build-time lanes (limitedUses/focusPool/spellSlot) and never looked at the play layer, where this app actually keeps costs. Every cost in this app is a manual, player-clicked counter — nothing is ever auto-debited when an ability is used. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/play.ts:861 `setFocusUsed(play, used, max)` is a bare setter; featUses and item charges are pips. So 'a cost the sheet debits' is not a capability this app has for ANY currency, including the three the reviewer concedes. The question is only whether HP and spell slots have the same kind of counter as focus does. Both do.

(1) HP AS A COST — already there, and the 'unresistable' half is vacuous. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/HpControl.tsx exposes a Damage field that accepts any number and calls `applyDamage` (play.ts:538), whose signature is `applyDamage(play, amount, max, deathBase)` — it takes a RAW amount and never consults IWR. Resistance is opt-in only: HpNumpadModal.tsx:120-144 renders resistance/weakness chips that pre-compute `Math.max(0, n - r.value)` and then call the SAME `onDamage`. Its own comment says 'you type the damage the GM said, then tap the type it was'. So unresisted damage is the app's DEFAULT and only automatic path; there is no auto-application to exempt and no number a 'bypasses IWR' flag would change. The reviewer's claim that 'the resistance lanes only grant defences, they do not model a source exempt from it' describes a problem that cannot arise here. Paying 1d6 to yourself is then the player typing 4 and pressing Damage — and the lanes doc's own NOT-lanes list rules this out explicitly: 'The internal steps of an activity … The app lists the action; the player performs it.' The printable clause is the `note` lane (types.ts ContentBase.note: 'This record works; here is the part you apply yourself').

(2) SPELL SLOT AS A COST — already there, and the reviewer's own words give away the conflation. They say 'The spellSlot lanes only ADD slots.' True of the build-time lane; false of the app. play.ts:615 `toggleExpended(play, key)` flips one individual prepared slot spent/ready, keyed by entry+rank+index — exactly the index-addressing they say makes it hard — and play.ts:623 `setSlotsUsed(play, key, used, max)` sets a spontaneous per-rank count. Neither takes a spell, a caster, or a reason. Both are wired to bare pip clicks: SpellsTab.tsx:1063, :1201, :1237 (`onPip`) and :1153 for the spontaneous pool, with the title text 'Click to cast (expend slot)'. 'The player must pick one unexpended slot of rank >= N and mark it spent' IS clicking that pip. The rank>=trigger constraint depends on the rank of an incoming ENEMY spell, which the lanes doc puts out of scope ('Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet').

(3) THE MAGNITUDE FEED — also already expressible. 'Resistance equal to twice the expended slot's rank' is a temporary resistance from a toggleable state = the `mode` lane, ModeDef.resistances (types.ts:2492), whose docstring was written for exactly this ('resistance 5 to fire until the start of your next turn'). 75 modes in public/core.json already grant resistances, 28 with formula values, and `adept-benefit-amulet` already ships `type: 'chosen damage type'` — the player-chosen-type precedent the reviewer says is missing. Graded variants per rank are the established pattern (crimson-godsblood-serum ships lesser/moderate/greater/major as separate modes, joinable by exclusiveGroup).

SECONDARY REFUTATION (not-one-system) if the above is contested: the definition's own 'hit points, OR an expended spell slot' is the tell. The two branches share no storage, no consumer, and no UI — one touches PlayState.damage/tempHp via applyDamage, the other touches PlayState.expendedSlots/slotsUsed on the Spells tab plus a variable resistance grant. Building either buys nothing for the other. A third unrelated thing (a damage-application flag that bypasses IWR) is smuggled in, which is not a cost or a resource at all. And the cluster's 6 entries come from just 2 records.

WHAT IS REAL: both records are bare — public/core.json has blood-and-spirit carrying only `choice` (holy/unholy) and energetic-resonance carrying only `actionCost: reaction`; neither has note, modes, resistances, strikeDamage, or situational. blood-and-spirit is missing its actual mechanic (mode + strikeDamage: +1d6 spirit with the chosen trait on Strikes with the coated weapon) and energetic-resonance is missing its mode-granted resistance. Those are 'promised but empty' defects in lanes that already exist — a data backfill, not a new system.

refuted.name: cross-sheet-grants-and-partner-links
refuted.why: The lane is `situational` (FEAT_SITUATIONAL in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), plus the shipped PARTY_SHARED_FEATS route — the reviewer considered neither. (1) The spotter relationship is ALREADY a named referent in the situational `when` clause, live on 4 of the Sniping Duo archetype's 9 feats: `sniping-duo-dedication` (line 629) `when: "…against a target your spotter just hit…"`, `exploit-opening` `when: "reaction, on the ranged Strike you make after your spotter critically succeeds at a…"` (a reaction-shaped entry), `duos-aim` `when: "…within your spotter's…"`, and `deflecting-shot` `when: "to the ally who was hit…"` — an ally-TARGETED bonus already in the table, as is `ascended-celestial-dedication`'s `when: "ALLIES inside your active nimbus…"`. vantage-shot simply carries no entry: promised-but-empty inside an existing lane, the exact bucket docs/mechanic-lanes.md line 13 names, not a missing lane. Note also that the 'your spotter' designation is not printed on vantage-shot at all — it is on its prerequisite sniping-duo-dedication ('choose one willing, non-minion ally… change by spending 3 days of downtime'), and `note` is documented in src/rules/types.ts:231 for exactly this shape ('a clause the rules leave to the table (which ally wears your relic)'). (2) Ally-facing payloads were RULED, not overlooked: Ruling F (work/rulings/DECISIONS.md, per project_hh_rulings_dfgh) — ally-instant → nothing at all; ally-timed → a display-only mode on the ACTIVATOR, feat-gated via modes[].feats. 29 of 203 modes in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json are ally-facing (Aegis for the Innocent, Tweak Appearances, Eternal Blessing). guide-the-timeline is ally-INSTANT — 'the next time within the next round', one roll — so the settled ruling is 'nothing at all', and the record already carries the trackable part (limitedUses 1/day, scripts/data/effect-backfill.json ~line 74001). (3) The cross-sheet grant is SHIPPED, not absent: src/sheet/partySummary.ts:28 `PARTY_SHARED_FEATS = ['battleforger']` + PartySummary.sharedFeats + src/data/partyCapabilities.ts `partyHasFeat()`, consumed at src/sheet/ItemEditorModal.tsx:1191 (`character.feats.some(f=>f.featId==='battleforger') || partyHasFeat('battleforger')`) — one PC's feat surfacing a usable control on ANOTHER PC's sheet, campaign-scoped through campaign_characters. Adding 'vantage-shot' is a one-line registry change. It is also the architecturally correct route, since player-facing teammate sheets are deliberately read-only (only the GM writes, via gm_character_edits). (4) Roll-mode changes are already vocabulary in the same lane: `derring-do` 'fortune: roll twice and use the higher result', `incredible-luck` 'roll twice, keep the better result (fortune)', `starsong-nectar`, `acrobats-staff`, `laurel-of-the-empath`, `agent-of-all-holds` (crit-fail→fail) — all rendered live via characterSituationalIds in src/rules/explain.ts. (5) Half of vantage-shot's payload lands on the HOLDER by its own text ('when your spotter successfully makes a ranged Strike… YOU can use a reaction'), which is plain grantsAction — the lane the reviewer conceded. The residue is explicitly a non-lane: the Stealth check is an internal step of an activity, and 'the foe is off-guard' is an effect on an enemy; docs/mechanic-lanes.md lines 158-162 excludes both, leaving only the reaction's EXISTENCE, which grantsAction + PARTY_SHARED_FEATS cover. Supporting (not needed for the verdict): the 6 entries (indices 175-179 + 117) also conflate three unrelated capabilities — a downtime-set designation printed on a different record, an outward-facing grant, and an instant fortune/misfortune on a target chosen at use time that is as often a foe as an ally; vantage-shot has no roll-mode and guide-the-timeline has no pointer. Separately, three guide-the-timeline entries demand a new 'chronoskimmer DC' statistic; chronoskimmer-dedication's own text refutes that — 'either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher' — i.e. max(classDC, spellDC), a label over two numbers the app already derives.

refuted.name: condition-instances-and-per-character-definitions
refuted.why: The reviewer's own wording concedes the split ("Both needs sit just outside it"), and the 5 entries divide 2/3 across two capabilities that share nothing but the word "condition". Half A (gold entries 18, 21, zombie-dedication) wants PLAY-STATE bookkeeping: provenance + a removal-immunity flag on an ActiveCondition instance in PlayState. Half B (entries 27, 30, 32, ascended-celestial-dedication) wants a CONTENT-DEFINITION rewrite: per-character replacement of a global condition's rules prose in the content DB. Different store (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/play.ts runtime state vs core.json's `conditions` collection), different consumer (a removal path vs description rendering), different lifetime (a transient instance vs a permanent build fact), and entry 32 itself says of half B "Nothing on the sheet changes numerically" while half A is pitched as guarding a number. Building either gets you none of the other. Each half also fails on its own, so nothing survives even split apart. Half A is already-expressible via the `mode` lane (doc section J) plus `note`: the app has NO automated condition-removal to be immune to. Conditions are only ever added/removed by the player clicking Apply/Remove in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/ConditionsModal.tsx, and the single automated remover, restConditions() at src/rules/play.ts:1524, touches only fatigued/wounded/dying/doomed/drained — its own comment says "Other conditions persist … the player clears those manually", so Slowed is untouched by rest already. A per-instance "unremovable" flag would therefore guard against code that does not exist. The route the app actually has for "a named state from one specific source that only its own remedy ends" is a mode: ModeDef (src/rules/types.ts:2458) carries a name, a `feats: ['zombie-dedication']` gate, `duration`, `note`, `survivesRest`, and — per src/rules/play.ts:1619-1626 — a feat-borne mode is deliberately never cleared by rest ("Modes the player toggled themselves are left alone"). Because activeModes is a different list from conditions, a mode-borne "Deteriorated Body" is inherently distinguishable from a player-applied Slowed 1, which is the provenance the entry asks for; and the 10-minute repair "as part of your daily preparations" is the existing `dailyChoice` lane. There is also nothing numeric to distinguish: src/rules/conditions.ts declares action-economy conditions out of scope by design ("Out of scope (no flat number to display): action-economy conditions (Slowed, Stunned, Quickened)"), and CONDITION_EFFECTS has no `slowed` key, so both hypothetical Slowed 1 instances contribute exactly 0 to every derived value. Half B is out-of-scope, and the residue is already printed. `confused` in core.json is {id, name, valued:false, group:null, edition} — no behaviour, and conditions.ts lists Confused among the situational conditions it deliberately does not model. So there is no engine-held "attack wildly" to override; "attack wildly" vs "stand still wasting actions" is table behaviour executed by the player/GM, which the doc's NOT-lanes list rules out twice ("Anything the GM adjudicates" and "the internal steps of an activity … the app lists the action; the player performs it"). The reviewer's framing of a "global definition per condition" in conditions.ts is also inaccurate: that file holds only numeric penalty rows, and the condition-versus-condition interactions that ARE mechanical already have lanes — mode `immunities: ['confused']` (see the shipped `scouring-spark` mode in core.json) for immunity, and `situational` for the ~7 records granting bonuses on saves against becoming confused (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts). What is left of half B is one sentence of prose, i.e. the `note` lane, and it is already on the sheet verbatim in the feat's description with a live desc-ref link to the confused condition (core-descriptions.json feats.ascended-celestial-dedication, refs include {label:'confused', key:'conditions'}). Wanting that same sentence to also appear on the Confused row of the conditions modal is display placement, not an absent capability.

refuted.name: runtime-resolved-grant-parameters
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The `spellcasting` lane (`spellcastingGrant`) plus the `innateSpell` lane already express both Lore Seeker clauses, and the conditional branch lives in the ENGINE rather than in the data — which is precisely what 'computed from the character at build time' means.

The site is C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/build.ts, lines 3898 and 4060-4076. `const caster = spellcasting.find(e => e.type === 'prepared' || e.type === 'spontaneous')` IS the predicate 'could you already cast spells', evaluated off the character. The innate entry is then built as:
  tradition: <tally of grants naming one> ?? caster?.tradition ?? 'arcane'
  keyAbility: caster?.keyAbility ?? profile?.keyAbility ?? 'cha'
  proficiency: maxRank(caster?.proficiency ?? 'untrained', profile?.proficiency ?? 'trained')
where `profile` is the feat's own `spellcastingGrant`. Read the two clauses against that:

(1) 'you use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability … and become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs' — the else-branch only. `caster?.keyAbility ?? profile?.keyAbility` already means 'the class caster wins if there is one, the feat's profile applies only if there is not'. The reviewer's 'trained spellcasting statistic that exists solely because of this feat' is the `innate-casting` entry itself, which for a non-caster is created with the profile's attribute and trained rank. This is not hypothetical: 36 live records carry `spellcastingGrant`, and TWO are the same printed conditional word-for-word — `entities-from-afar` ('If you couldn't already cast occult spells, these spells use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability, and you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for occult spells; if you could already cast occult spells, your proficiency … increases to expert') and `words-of-unraveling`, both stored as the flat `{tradition:'occult', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}` with the branch supplied by `maxRank`. `crystal-ward-spells` and `spellshot-dedication` are already the exact `{arcane, int, trained}` triple Lore Seeker needs.

(2) 'If you could already cast spells, these spells are of the same tradition. Otherwise, they are arcane spells' — `?? caster?.tradition ?? 'arcane'` is that sentence, verbatim, already in the code for exactly this parameter. The reason Lore Seeker does not get it is that its three `innateSpells` grants each store `tradition: "arcane"` as a literal, which pins the tally and shadows the character-read fallback. That is a stored value shadowing a working resolver — the failure mode docs/mechanic-lanes.md names in its own closing section ('It compares presence, not value'), not an absent route.

The generalized 'system' framing fails hardest. Grant parameters resolved off the character with conditional branches are pervasive here, not missing: `entryRetune.keyAbilityFromClass` reads a parameter off ANOTHER spellcasting entry rather than naming it ('your PSYCHIC spellcasting attribute' — `ancestral-mind` ships it, scope 'innate'); `heightenHalfLevel`/`heightenAt` compute a grant's rank from level; `darkvisionIfAncestryLowLight` branches on what the ancestry already gives; `apexAttribute` is '18, or +2 if already 18+'; `featGrantsAuto.redundantFallback` is 'if you would already be trained, choose another'; `ItemPassiveEffects.speeds` accepts a formula ('floor(@actor.speed.land/2)'); `choiceOptionAdditions.addIfSanctified` branches on sanctification; `spellSlotBonus.exceptHighest` is computed from the character's own slot table; `modifiesGrant` fires only when the character possesses the named record. And because build.ts recomputes the whole sheet from BuildState, the reviewer's 'the answer changes if they gain casting later' is automatic — `caster` is re-evaluated and the branch flips.

What actually survives is smaller than a system and splits in two directions. The real defect: Lore Seeker is missing `spellcastingGrant: {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}`, so a non-caster scrollmaster's three innate spells currently key off Charisma (the `?? 'cha'` tail) instead of Intelligence — one 'promised but empty' record on a built lane. The residual: for a character who DOES cast, the pooled innate entry would label these three spells Arcane rather than inheriting; that is a tradition LABEL on the entry, not a number (the DC and attack come from keyAbility + proficiency, the three spells are a fixed list, and innate has no slots for restrictedSlots.ts to filter), and `entryRetune` scope 'innate' is the existing home for retuning it. The reviewer's own 'undefined if they have two traditions' sub-case is unanswerable in print and is GM adjudication, which docs/mechanic-lanes.md explicitly excludes from being a lane.

refuted.name: dynamic-picker-eligibility
refuted.why:
The 5 entries bundle three unrelated capabilities in three different subsystems, and the two that carry the cluster are already built or explicitly not lanes.

(1) 'One record making spells legal candidates in a LATER repertoire add/swap flow' (divine-access, 3 of the 5 entries) is the existing spellListAdd lane, and the reviewer's stated reason is factually inverted. SpellAccessGrant (src/rules/types.ts:2945) has as:'list'|'repertoire'|'font'; build.ts:3291-3297 documents 'list' as 'widens the picker (you may LEARN it)' and test/spell-access.test.ts:7 says spellListAdditions 'widened the PICKER and nothing else'. Both selection flows read it: SpellsTab.tsx:275-278 folds it into traditionSpellsByRank, which feeds optionsFor(rank) in ManageSpellsModal (the spontaneous add/swap picker), and Builder.tsx:441-470 does the same for build-time repertoire, its comment noting the sheet picker already did. Divine Access's exact shape (deity-derived, capped at three, still costing a slot) already ships as Blessed Blood (Sorcerer) via from:'deity' + max (build.ts:3326, Builder.tsx:457-458), tested in test/spell-access-lanes.test.ts:22-37 against the 450+ deities that now carry `spells`. Divine Access is promised-but-empty: effect-backfill.json gives it only a kind:'text' choice whose `inert` note claims deity cleric-spell data doesn't exist — stale as of the 472-deity backfill. Residual is one resolver argument (read the feat's chosen deity rather than build.deityId), not a lane.

(2) 'The printed options PLUS anything you have access to' (devout-blessing, 1 entry) is an access clause, which mechanic-lanes.md:164 lists under NOT lanes, and GM/campaign permission (line 157-158). `access` is free text on records (types.ts:1436) for that reason. It also has no referent: the app's whole blessing inventory is blessed-armament / blessed-shield / blessed-swiftness — exactly the printed list. And the widening capability exists regardless: choiceOptionAdditions (types.ts:571) + effectiveChoiceOptions (derive.ts:984-1009) is one record injecting candidates into another record's picker, deduped, tested in test/choice-additions.test.ts on this same blessing family (Radiant Armament / Greater Armament, plus addIfSanctified keyed to the character's own answer). blastTypeAdditions is a third instance of the same shape.

(3) A character-LEVEL gate on one option (precious-alloys adamantine at 13th, 1 entry) is the only residual, and it is a field on an existing lane, not a system: options[].requiresSkillRank + qualifiesForOption (derive.ts:1024) is already the option-gate mechanism, and character-level gating of choice availability already exists as SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel, featGrants.minLevel and whileActive.minLevel. Across ~6,200 feats only precious-alloys and versatile-mutation need it. 'A pick made earlier must still be re-openable' is free — build-time answers are editable PopupSelects. Note for follow-up: qualifiesForOption/effectiveChoiceOptions run in dailyChoices.ts and at grant-resolution but not in the build-time array picker (Builder.tsx:282, shared.tsx:2532); no live case is affected because both choiceOptionAdditions targets are daily:true.

So: a spellcasting-pool widening that is built and tested, a rarity/permission clause the manual rules out and that has no referent in the data, and a two-record option gate that is one field on the choice lane. There is no single missing system here.

refuted.name: creature-traits-on-the-character
refuted.why:
The blocking claim — "Nothing in the vocabulary stores traits ON THE CHARACTER - only weapon and unarmed traits exist" (gold entry 15) — is factually wrong, and the app already ships the exact capability the reviewer describes.

1) A creature trait IS stored on the character and IS keyed off by another record. Lane G (`choice` / `effectChoices`). `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json` → `feats/sanctified-soul` carries `choice: { flag: 'sanctification', options: [{value:'holy'},{value:'unholy'}] }`, and its printed text is literally "You gain either the holy trait or the unholy trait" — holy and unholy are creature traits, produce no number of their own, and exist to be read by other things. The pick persists on the character in `Character.effectPicks` (`src/rules/types.ts:3385`), is read back by name at `src/rules/derive.ts:969` (`sanctificationOf(c)`), and a DIFFERENT record keys off it: Radiant Armament's `choiceOptionAdditions.addIfSanctified` (`src/rules/types.ts:579`), consumed at `src/rules/derive.ts:1003`, adds the Holy rune only to a holy character and the Unholy rune only to an unholy one. That is character-level creature trait → first-class stored data → another record reading it. 274 records in core.json touch this trait.

2) A second shipping instance of "the character counts as having trait X, and another record keys off it": `Heritage.extraAncestryFeatTraits` (`src/rules/types.ts:1227`), read by the ancestry feat-slot filter at `src/rules/featSlots.ts:93`. Its doc comment is precisely the reviewer's use case — "you can select elf, half-elf, and human feats" — and the field was created because "a heritage that opens a THIRD ancestry's list had nowhere to say so."

3) The display surface already exists as a first-class row. `src/sheet/DetailsTab.tsx:407-419` renders a **Traits** row on the character, one glossary-linked `InfoTerm` pill per trait, resolved through `traitDesc(t, content)` against core.json's 563-entry `trait` collection — which already contains `undead`, `zombie` AND `mindless`. The row is fed from `ancestry.traits` today; feeding heritage/feat grants into it is adding a source to an existing row, not building a system.

4) The undead trait's actual sheet-side payload has dedicated lanes, and Zombie Dedication already carries half of it. `immunity` lane: the record ships `immunities: ["death effects","disease","paralyzed","poison","sleep"]`. Healing inversion: `negativeHealing` is a real field on DefenseGrants (`types.ts:655`), Heritage (`1237`) and ItemBase (`1994`), aggregated from heritage + FEATS + invested items at `derive.ts:1756-1759`, and rendered as "Void healing — healed by void, harmed by vitality" (`DefensesPills.tsx:81`, `VitalsRail.tsx:738`). Zombie Dedication simply fails to set it — a promised-but-empty defect in an existing lane (and that clause is gold entries 16/23, deliberately NOT part of this 4-entry cluster).

5) The negation half collapses on inspection. `mindless` is not among the app's 57 conditions and nothing in the app ever asserts a zombie is mindless, so there is no implication to negate — a negation needs something positive to cancel. The clause is a disambiguating sentence for the reader, which is exactly what `note` (`ContentBase.note`, rendered under the description on the Feats tab) is for. The reviewer's own gold entry 17 concedes this: "Only worth carrying as printed text if character traits are not modelled at all" — and they are modelled, per points 1 and 3.

What genuinely remains is narrower than a system: there is no field for a FIXED (unchosen) trait grant, only for a chosen one (0 single-option choices exist in the data). That is a sourcing gap on an existing row and an existing lane — the same shape as `extraAncestryFeatTraits` before it was added — not a capability with no route. The remaining consumers the reviewer names ("what can target you", "undead-only effects", "spells with creature-trait restrictions") are resolved on the caster's side; this app evaluates no targeting at all — feat `prerequisites` are unevaluated free text (zombie-dedication's is the string "You died and were animated as a husk zombie.").

refuted.name: fortune-misfortune-and-reroll-modes
refuted.why: The `situational` lane covers this, and the reviewer's reason for rejecting it rests on a false premise about that lane's contract. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:74 documents the `bonus` field as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR A SHORT EFFECT PHRASE" — the contract is display-only, not numbers-only, so a roll-mode phrase is in-contract content, not an abuse of a numeric field. The registry already holds 23 such entries in 15 distinct phrasings, and it already distinguishes the very two policies the proposal says are conflated: acrobats-staff carries "fortune: reroll and take the better result" while blessed-medicine carries "fortune: reroll and use the new result" — the replace-not-compare policy claimed to have no home. perfected-form carries a third shape ("treat an attack roll lower than 10 as a 10 (fortune)") and phantom-charm a misfortune-triggered one. Both example feats are fully expressed today, on every half: (1) THE EFFECT — situationalBonuses.ts:606 files ascended-celestial-dedication as targets [{kind:'save',detail:'will'}], when "once per hour, on a Will saving throw", bonus "roll twice and use the higher result (fortune)". targetMatches (line 3059) matches it to the Will save ref, statHasSituational (explain.ts:268) puts the `*` on the Will row, and situationalList (explain.ts:405) renders "roll twice and use the higher result (fortune) from Ascended Celestial Dedication — once per hour, on a Will saving throw", clickable back to the feat. (2) THE FREQUENCY — scripts/data/effect-backfill.json gives ACD limitedUses {max:1,per:'hour'} and minor-omen {max:1,per:'day'}, drawn as tickable pips. (3) THE ONE-PER-ROLL RULE — src/rules/glossary.ts:115-116 defines fortune as "roll twice and take the higher result; only one fortune effect can apply to a roll" and misfortune alongside it; FeatDetail.tsx:74 renders every trait pill as an InfoTerm carrying that text, and minor-omen's traits in public/core.json are ["archetype","fortune","occult"] — so the rule is stated on the record itself, at the point of use. That also refutes the proposal's premise that minor-omen "is not fortune": Paizo tags it fortune; it is simply a fortune effect whose reroll policy is 'use the new result'. (4) THE TRIGGERED REACTION — minor-omen carries actionCost {type:'reaction'}, so MainTab.tsx:238 lists it in the encounter action list with its Trigger/Frequency text and use pips. (5) THE REROLL RESOURCE — reroll pools are already tracked subsystems: hero points (play.ts:576, VitalsRail.tsx:655) and mythic points with the on-sheet note "Spend 1 point to reroll a failed skill check or save at mythic proficiency (Rewrite Fate)" (VitalsRail.tsx:1002). ACD is itself a mythic destiny dedication, so that pool is on its sheet already. Note also RECORD_MARKERS (line 3167), a second built lane expressly for "things that change no number the sheet holds", which already carries degree-of-success transforms such as the-publican's "crit fail -> fail" on Aid. What is genuinely absent is not a lane but an ENFORCEMENT ENGINE, and that is out of this app's scope by explicit design: CharacterSheet.tsx:360 reads `const diceOff = character.options?.diceRollerOff ?? true` — the dice roller is OFF by default, the app never claims to resolve the character's checks, and rules/dice.ts is a generic label/count/sides/modifier helper. Enforcing fortune would also be WRONG rather than missing: PF2e makes it a player choice when several fortune effects could apply, and it cancels against misfortune effects applied by enemies, which a character sheet cannot know. poolSituationalLines (line 3406) already encodes that correctly — it returns a null dedupe key for unparseable bonuses, so fortune lines are never suppressed and all sources stay visible for the player to choose among. Finally the cluster is not one system even on its own terms: a pre-roll roll-mode change (ACD), a retroactive result replacement with a replace-not-compare policy (minor-omen), and a cross-source stacking arbiter are three unrelated capabilities, and the first two already have homes while the third is a resolution engine, not a data lane.

refuted.name: always-on-spell-effects
refuted.why:
Refuted on every sub-claim, and both example feats already carry data in the shipped build.

1) The standing effect is the `mode` lane (§J of docs/mechanic-lanes.md), and eternal-blessing is ALREADY authored into it. C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/toggle-modes.json and public/core.json both contain mode `feat-eternal-blessing`: duration "permanent - you may Dismiss it, and it returns automatically after 1 minute", modifiers [{target:'attack', type:'status', value:1}], and a note stating the ceil(level/2) rank and the fixed 15-ft radius. So the gold entry's claim that "the vocabulary has no lane for a bonus to attack rolls at all" is simply false: ModeTargetKind in src/rules/types.ts:2434-2444 lists 'attack', 20 shipped modes already use it, and src/rules/derive.ts:2653, 2810 and 2921 fold modeTypedMods(c.activeModes,{kind:'attack'}) into the strike attack pool with typed stacking. The +1 status reaches the number today.

2) "A mode is only a player toggle" is also false as a description of how the lane is used. Modes are the app's declared home for permanent standing effects, with the printed duration doing the talking because the app has no clock (types.ts:2534-2538). Shipped examples with permanent durations: `golden-body` and `grand-medics-mask` both read duration "always active". src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts additionally carries nine entries of the form {on:'condition', id:'quickened', value:'always on'} (eternal-boost, eternal-composition, full-automation, panache-paragon, perfect-readiness, supreme-spellstrike, swift-paragon, weapon-supremacy, abundant-vials) - i.e. "this is permanently running on you" is an existing, live expression, not a missing one.

3) The "no casting, no slot, no per-day use, rank = half level rounded up" resource shape is exactly `innateSpell`, not a gap in it. InnateSpellGrant (types.ts:1192-1210) has `atWill?: boolean` ("no per-day use") and `heightenHalfLevel?: boolean` documented verbatim as "cast at ceil(level/2), the standard innate-heighten ladder ('heightened to half your level')". src/rules/build.ts:4028 computes Math.max(base, Math.ceil(level/2)) at derive time, so the rank is NOT stored - it recomputes on every level-up, which is the reviewer's own stated requirement. build.ts:4055 maps atWill to innateUses=0, and src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:1482,1495 renders that as "rank N - at will - from <feat>" with the per-day pip suppressed entirely. 97 at-will grants and 25 heightenHalfLevel grants already ship in public/core.json, and wildborn-adept uses both flags together - the precise combination the reviewer says has no route.

4) constant-levitation was already ruled on and already fixed. scripts/data/effect-backfill.json contains {category:'feats', id:'constant-levitation', field:'speeds', value:{fly:40}}, and public/core.json's feats['constant-levitation'] carries speeds:{fly:40}. That is the `speed` lane (§D), the same feat->speeds grant path 49 other feats use (derive.ts:1229-1241). A constant Fly spell's only own-sheet consequence is a permanent fly Speed, and the sheet shows it.

5) The leftovers are out-of-scope by the manual's own NOT-lanes list, not evidence of a missing lane. "Largely ally-facing emanation" - the doc excludes effects on other creatures/the battlefield, and the modes lane already has a dedicated "Ally effects" category for the reminder-only half (feat-aegis-for-the-innocent). "Could be counteracted or dispelled" - counteract is GM adjudication; the app's affordance for it is toggling the mode off, which the authored duration string spells out ("you may Dismiss it"). "Radius fixed at 15 ft and cannot be increased" - pure area geometry with no sheet number; the app has no templates, and the note carries the constraint.

Secondary point: the cluster is also close to not-one-system. Its two members resolve through completely unrelated sheet consequences - a movement Speed line (constant-levitation) and an aura-shaped typed attack bonus (eternal-blessing) - sharing only the English phrase "constant spell". Building one "hosted spell instance" subsystem would be a new abstraction over two already-working lanes. Either way it does not survive as real-and-absent: 4 of 183 entries, both feats populated, three lanes covering them.

refuted.name: mythic-proficiency-tier
refuted.why: The lane is `situational`, not `rankUpgrade`, and it is already populated with this exact effect 23 times. (1) docs/mechanic-lanes.md line 165 states the routing rule outright: "A bonus to one specific roll is `situational`, not a flat bonus — do not classify it as skillTrained, acBonus, or saveBonus." A rank substituted into one named check while the skill keeps its rank is precisely a one-roll effect, so rankUpgrade was never the candidate lane; the reviewer measured against a lane the manual forbids for this shape and concluded absence. (2) C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts already carries "at mythic proficiency" on 23 shipped records — prescient-parry, avoid-fates-gaze, become-shadow, binds-that-tie, steadfast-grip, and 18 callings/echoes — across skills, Perception, saves, save-DCs and AC (steadfast-grip: a Reflex DC "calculated at mythic proficiency"; prescient-parry: AC "recalculated at mythic proficiency"). The nearest twin is `sagas-calling`, a classFeature the sheet already reaches via derive.ts:2130: targets skill/diplomacy, when "on Performance or to Gather Information, spending a Mythic Point", bonus "attempt the check at mythic proficiency" — same skill, same activity, same Mythic-Point cost as Guarded Domain. guarded-domain (core.json: level 14, beast-lord, mythic trait, limitedUses 1/day) simply has no FEAT_SITUATIONAL entry, which is the lanes doc's own "promised but empty" bucket, i.e. a per-record defect, not a missing system. The lane accepts this by design: SituationalBonus.bonus is documented as "the modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', OR a short effect phrase", and the whole lane is display-only for every one of its 2,852 entries — so "it doesn't recompute the number" is the lane's uniform design, not a mythic-specific hole (the lanes doc's own closing section names presence-vs-value as the known blind spot of this instrument). (3) The reviewer's proposed prerequisite — a mythic rung in PROFICIENCY_RANKS — would be a defect. AoN local mirror rules-3322.json (War of Immortals p.76): the bonus is 10 + level and "Unlike trained, expert, master, and legendary proficiency, you use mythic proficiency only when an ability tells you to." It is never a rank a character holds. PROFICIENCY_RANKS (types.ts:63) drives skillIncreaseCap (Builder.tsx:912-918, 1722), the builder's selectable rank picker (builder/shared.tsx:2113), rankMax/rankUpgrade stepping (build.ts:768-796) and prerequisite comparison (build.ts:5337); a sixth rung would offer "mythic" as a pickable skill rank and let rankUpgrade climb into it. (4) The companion half is covered twice over: companions.ts:483 computes every companion skill through modeNumberBonus({kind:'skill',detail:sk}), and companionModes (types.ts:3428; play.ts:519-520, 942-948) scopes modes per companion, so a numeric per-companion skill route exists today; and the owner has already ruled how "…or your companion can" is surfaced — situationalBonuses.ts "Ruling N" on artillerist-dedication chose one star on the PC's stat whose note covers the off-sheet actor, explicitly over building a marker surface on the companion block. (Also: the sibling entries' premise that mythic points do not exist is false — MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS = 3 in play.ts:25, mythicPoints in types.ts:3413, spendable pips in sheet/VitalsRail.tsx, plus rules/mythic.ts and sheet/MythicRules.tsx.) Fix: author one FEAT_SITUATIONAL["guarded-domain"] entry — targets skill/diplomacy, when "to Gather Information about a creature that has been in your guarded domain 1+ hour, after 1 minute communing (you or your companion)", bonus "attempt the check at mythic proficiency (prof bonus = level + 10)".

refuted.name: place-attunement-designation
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the designation is a campaign-log entry gated on GM-adjudicated table facts, and the sheet-side residue is already expressible.

1) The cluster is one record, not four. gold-freetext.json holds 11 entries for guarded-domain out of 183; the reviewer's 4 are the same feat read through the resources/unmodellable lenses. The other 7 are the mythic-proficiency and Mythic-Point clauses, which are separate proposals. So this is the bookkeeping half of a single level-14 Beast Lord archetype feat, and no second record shares the shape (the only other attune-to-a-place records, Cube of Recall and Doomsday Door, are stored as activationCost + printed text with no computed consequence: cube-of-recall carries only {type:'actions',value:3}, doomsday-door carries nothing).

2) Nothing on the sheet computes from the designation. The full text (public/core-descriptions.json, feats/guarded-domain) has exactly two consumers: (a) a Gather Information check available only 'If a creature has been in your guarded domain for at least 1 hour while you or your companion are also inside your domain', and (b) a once-per-day 3-action Mythic-Point teleport 'to a location you are aware of within your domain'. Neither reads the place's name or any radius to produce a number. Whether the creature was inside, whether you are inside, whether a destination lies within the domain — every one is a fact only the GM owns. docs/mechanic-lanes.md's NOT-lanes list excludes precisely this: 'Anything the GM adjudicates: exploration outcomes, social consequences, narrative access.' The eligibility clause ('If you spend 1 week of downtime within a settlement or natural area…') is an access clause, also on that list. Building the record would move nothing.

3) The load-bearing premise is a misreading. There is no 'radius the player writes in': 'a settlement or natural area with a 5-mile radius' is a printed constant stating what qualifies as an eligible area. Nothing varies, and the feat's own description already prints the number.

4) The expiry needs a campaign clock this app has deliberately never had, and it is not a sheet concern. grep over src/ for calendar/worldDate/gameDate/daysElapsed/elapsed returns zero hits. The only time boundary the engine knows is rest / daily preparation, which resets per-day resources; 'more than 1 month spent OUTSIDE the domain' is unreachable from rest counts because it depends on where the party has been, i.e. the GM's log. An in-world calendar tracking party location is a campaign/VTT concern, not a character-sheet computation.

5) The part that IS the character's own bookkeeping is already expressible, so even the survivable fragment needs no new system. The modes lane is defined in mechanic-lanes.md as 'a state you turn on and off … "while X is active"' and is not combat-only — ModeDef (src/rules/types.ts:2458) carries note, senses, speeds, resistances, immunities, per-character scope and exclusiveGroup, and the mode editor takes a player-typed name (src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:277), so 'Guarded Domain — Sandpoint' is a nameable, single-record, toggleable state today: the player switches it off when the GM rules the month elapsed and back on after the week of downtime, and renaming it is the exclusivity. The feat already carries limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'} for the teleport. Player-authored place text already has two homes: the Notes tab (src/sheet/NotesTab.tsx, multi-page rich text with description ref-links) and the character's free-text birthplace field (src/rules/types.ts:3151). PopupSelect's addCustom path (src/builder/shared.tsx:807-920, the custom-Lore flow) is the existing precedent for a typed-in choice value.

6) The proposal also bundles unrelated capabilities with different owners — a free-text label (bio/notes), single-slot exclusivity (modes, already built), and a calendar-driven lapse (GM log) — so it is not one system either. But out-of-scope is the decisive verdict: no clause of the feat turns the designation into anything the sheet can compute.

refuted.name: outcome-branched-effects
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The reviewer benchmarked against the wrong lane. `effectGrant`/`choice` are indeed builder-time picks, but the manual lists two OTHER lanes that carry exactly this shape, and both already ship populated with it.

(1) `mode` (docs/mechanic-lanes.md §J; type at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:2458) is the app's RUNTIME branch selector. `ModeDef.exclusiveGroup` means only one member of a group can be on at a time — enforced in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/play.ts:1401-1403, which auto-deactivates the sibling. Every discriminator the reviewer names as impossible is a field on ModeDef: `modifiers` (bonus size, and `appliesWhen` makes it conditional so a one-shot 'vs the next attack' bonus prints as a condition instead of folding into AC — modes.ts:47-61), `resistances?: IwrEntry[]` (types.ts:2492, consumed by deriveDefenses at src/rules/derive.ts:1597-1601 tagged 'while active · <duration>'), so whether resistance is included at all is per-branch, and `IwrEntry.value` accepts a formula string resolved by `resolveIwrValue(value, level)` (derive.ts:1400) — 'equal to your level' is `@actor.level`, 'half your level' is `floor(@actor.level/2)`. `duration` (types.ts:2531) carries how long each branch lasts. Shipped precedents, not hypotheticals: cat-overdrive vs cat-critical-overdrive share exclusiveGroup 'inventor-overdrive' (src/rules/modes.ts:164-165) — one activity, two degree-of-success packages, and the CRITICAL one is precisely the branch that adds resistance, the reviewer's own stated discriminator. scripts/data/toggle-modes.json holds FOUR-member graded groups (oracle cursebound 1-4 per mystery, 20 members in one exclusiveGroup), 75 modes whose resistances use level formulas including banded ones (`5+5*min(1,max(0,@actor.level-14))`), and 9 modes that are explicitly roll-gated — item-cursed-dreamstone literally reads 'Switch this on only if you failed the save against the curse'; spell-survivor is 'Triggered by critically succeeding at a save against a spell' + resistance + duration; extract-vow-of-nonviolence branches crit-success vs success inside one mode. So on-my-best-day is four ModeDefs gated `feats:['on-my-best-day']` (gate honoured at modes.ts:308) in one exclusiveGroup: +3/@actor.level, +2/floor(@actor.level/2), +1/none, +1 conditional 'against the next attack made against you'. Zero new fields.

(2) `situational` (§J) already carries crit-gated damage riders with the `strikeDamage` target kind. chain-of-command (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2596) is `when: 'on a critical hit with the chain of command', bonus: '+1d6 mental'` — the same payload shame-the-sin wants. vicious-fangs:2772 is crit-only AND level-banded ('1d6 persistent bleed (2d6 at 14th level, 3d6 at 20th)'), which is the level-band half of the claim. resounding-bravery:510 branches its value on a target property ('+2 if the crit success was against a fear effect'). observational-analysis:840 branches value by degree of success. 201 lines of that table mention criticals. on-my-best-day ALREADY has an entry (:768) that says in so many words '+1 to +3 status (by degree of success; on a critical failure it applies only to the next attack against you)', and its four branches are stored and rendered verbatim from core-descriptions.json plus `limitedUses {max:1,per:'hour'}` in effect-backfill.json. Nothing about it is missing today except that the four modes have not been authored — population, not capability.

Two supporting kills. (a) not-one-system: the cluster staples an inventory concern onto a damage rider onto a self-buff. The reviewer concedes shame-the-sin also needs per-target-tracking AND level-derived-values, i.e. two OTHER proposed systems — a cluster that cannot function without two siblings is not one system. (b) out-of-scope for twirling-throw: `InventoryItem.equipped` is already documented as 'Held/wielded' (types.ts:2979) and is a player toggle, so on a critical failure the player unchecks it — and the app has no board, so where a thrown weapon landed is a table/VTT fact, excluded by the manual's own NOT-lanes ('effects on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet', 'the internal steps of an activity'). Also note the app never rolls the check, so 'selected by the roll' can only ever mean 'selected at use time from a mutually exclusive set' — which is the definition of the mode lane.

refuted.name: use-time-choices
refuted.why:
Both halves of the definition have existing routes; neither example needs a new lane.

(1) "An answer scoped to a single activation, chosen afresh each time, discarded when it ends" IS the `mode` lane (manual §J). The answer is not stored as a key→value pair — it is stored as WHICH mode is on. `ModeDef.exclusiveGroup` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:2467, commented "Only one active mode per group at a time (e.g. bard compositions, rage states)") plus `toggleMode()` (src/rules/play.ts:1393-1406) means entering one variant evicts the sibling variant, and toggling off deletes it from `PlayState.activeModes` (src/rules/play.ts:109) — a store that is play state, not build state, and that rest prunes (play.ts:1623). The precedent is literally Rage: src/rules/modes.ts:139-142 ships FOUR mutually exclusive `barbarian-rage` variants (Rage / Rage legacy / Rotting Rage / Wooden Rage), and scripts/data/toggle-modes.json ships 20 `oracle-cursebound` variants (5 mysteries × 4 stages) for exactly this shape — "which flavour of the state am I in right now", re-picked every activation. Modes are also gated live against the sheet by `modeRelevant(class/ancestry/featIds)` (src/rules/modes.ts:296).

(2) "The option list must be computed at that moment from other sheet data" is already the `choice` lane. `kind:'skills'` resolves options from the character (build.ts:858: "which skills qualify depends on the BUILD and grows as it grows" → `trainedSkillOptions`); `kind:'domains'` resolves from the chosen deity; `kind:'open'` with `from.type` of `own-spell`/`own-feat`/`own-item`/`own-companion` searches the CHARACTER, not content (types.ts:1050-1055); and `options[].requiresSkillRank` hides options the character does not qualify for. Crucially the DAILY collection point re-runs all of this at answer time: `dailyChoicesFor()` calls `effectiveChoiceOptions(...).filter(qualifiesForOption(c, ...))` and `openChoiceOptions(def.from, db, {character: c})` (src/rules/dailyChoices.ts:44-54). "Offer only the variants for Speeds you actually possess" is a new enum value in that existing machinery, not a new system.

(3) march-of-law's cited clauses are already-lane'd or explicitly NOT lanes. Its +10-foot Speed is ALREADY authored: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:792 — `"march-of-law": [{ targets:[{kind:'speed'}], when:"only for the Stride made as part of March of Law…", bonus:"+10 feet status" }]`. "Ignoring difficult terrain" has an existing lane with seven sibling records using the identical shape — `RECORD_MARKERS` (situationalBonuses.ts:3181) `{on:'action', id:'stride', note:"You ignore difficult terrain…"}` for feather-step (3233), water-dancer (3254), rite-of-passage (3285), stonestep-shisk (3287), tunnel-rat (3291), unimpeded-journey (3292), wildwood-halfling (3295). March of Law simply lacks the entry: promised-but-empty in an existing lane, not a hole. And "use it while Burrowing/Climbing/Flying/Swimming instead of Striding" is the manual's own NOT-lane — "the internal steps of an activity… the app lists the action; the player performs it. Only the action's EXISTENCE is a lane" (mechanic-lanes.md:161-163). Its gate is the character's own Speed list, which lane D (`speeds`) already renders, and nothing computed differs between the four branches — the +10 ft applies to all Speeds equally.

(4) elemental-evolution's standing pick is already on the record (`choice` flag "damage", 7 array options, in public/core.json). The per-rage swap moves no number: rage bonus damage is one typed rider, `RAGE_DAMAGE['elemental-instinct'] = {tiers:[4,6,12], type:'energy'}` (src/rules/derive.ts:2264), and the type is only the word labelling that rider — its actual consequence lands on the target's resistances, i.e. another creature's sheet (also a NOT-lane). Pointing that type string at the player's stored answer is a field the app already has: `StrikeDamageRider.fromChoiceFlag` — "Restrict to the weapon the PLAYER chose, named by the flag of the choice that asked" (types.ts:2867-2870), and `critSpecSources` already substitutes a choice answer into a `{actor|flags.system.*}` placeholder at derive time (derive.ts ~2320).

Secondary refutation, if the above were somehow rejected: the cluster is also not-one-system. elemental-evolution needs a per-activation stored answer with a mechanical consequence; march-of-law needs no stored answer at all (a branch the player narrates) plus a terrain-cost rule the app has no grid for. Bundling them inflates a 4-entry cluster that is really 1 mode variant + 1 missing situational entry + 1 NOT-lane.

refuted.name: per-weapon-critical-threshold
refuted.why: The lane is `situational` (section J), target kind `strikeAttack` — and it already carries this exact rule twice, so the claim that "nothing in the vocabulary expresses a per-weapon crit-range change" is refuted by live shipping data, not by argument. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2755 — "savage-critical": targets [{kind:'strikeAttack'}], when "with a weapon or unarmed attack you have legendary proficiency in", bonus "a natural 19 that would be a success is a critical success instead". And line 2853 — "keen-flair": targets [{kind:'strikeAttack'}], when "with a weapon or unarmed attack you have master proficiency in", bonus "a 19 on the die that succeeds becomes a critical success". Both encode the widened threshold AND the reviewer's "only when the result would already be a success" qualifier, which is precisely the two-independent-routes-to-a-crit semantics they say has nowhere to live. Branched Tree of Pain's clause is the same sentence; it is an unpopulated registry key, not a missing capability. The reviewer's three sub-objections all fail against the code. (1) "It is not a bonus of any type, so situational cannot hold it." The `bonus` field is free player-facing prose and the module header states it is DISPLAY-ONLY: "nothing here changes a computed number." It is already used for non-bonus rule edits — point-blank-stance stores bonus "ignore the volley trait's attack penalty" (line 452), and 10+ entries store pure degree-of-success shifts ("success becomes a critical success", "one degree of success better", "success becomes a critical success; critical failure becomes a failure"). A result-step rule is the registry's normal cargo. (2) "It changes no printed number." That is the entry criterion for `situational`, not a disqualifier: the sheet stars the stat and prints the clause in the stat popup. strikeAttack situationals are addressed per strike INSTANCE (MainTab.tsx:402 statHasSituational(character, {kind:'strikeAttack', instanceId: s.instanceId}); StrikeDetailModal.tsx:64), so the line lands on the individual weapon's own attack-roll breakdown. (3) "Per-weapon." Two existing routes. Prose narrowing via `when` is the app's documented, deliberate ruling — explain.ts ~982: "a target carries no weapon narrowing, so the alternative is to show nothing at all. The `when` clause on each line is what tells the player whether it applies to this weapon" — and savage-critical/keen-flair are themselves weapon-subset-scoped that way. Tighter still, items carry their own `situational` array (src/rules/types.ts:2041, editable in ItemEditorModal.tsx and read by authoredSituational() in explain.ts only for inventory that is equipped/worn/invested), so the entry can live ON the ikon weapon and surfaces attributed to that weapon by name, disappearing when it is unequipped. Reinforcing this: display-only prose is not a compromise here, it is the only correct implementation, because the computed version the reviewer imagines is out of scope for a character sheet. The app's entire d20 crit logic is src/rules/dice.ts:68 — outcome: natural === 20 ? 'crit' : natural === 1 ? 'fumble' : undefined — a cosmetic "nat 20"/"nat 1" chip rendered in DiceDrawer.tsx:193. Nothing in src/ holds a target AC or compares a roll total to a DC (the sole degree-of-success computation in the repo is the GM-side tracker/src/components/DowntimeWidget.tsx:44). The "as long as that result would be a success" test therefore depends on a number that lives on the other creature's stat block; no amount of new schema on the PC sheet could evaluate it. Finally, the cluster is weaker than "3 of 183" suggests: all three entries are the same clause of the same single record, branched-tree-of-pain, viewed through the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses (37 distinct feats span the 183 entries). And the proposed name fuses two capabilities — the crit-threshold rule (already-expressible, above) and the separate "bind this feat to one owned weapon the way a rune is etched" pointer, which is its own set of entries in gold-freetext.json and its own proposal. Judged as the crit-threshold system it names, an existing lane covers it.

refuted.name: record-to-inventory-item-binding
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The lane is the **item-designation lane** (`weaponRider`/`critSpec` narrowed by `designated`, in the manual's vocabulary). The reviewer compared against `choice` and never found it because docs/mechanic-lanes.md never names it — the word 'designat*' appears nowhere in the manual. It is a manual gap, not an app gap.

The mechanism, point by point against the five stated requirements:

1. POINTER INTO OWN INVENTORY, NOT A PRINTED LIST — `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:2933`: `export type ItemDesignation = 'innovation' | 'weapon-implement' | 'bonded' | 'ikon' | 'rune-source';` stored as `InventoryItem.designations` (types.ts:3001). Its own doc comment (types.ts:2985-3000) states the exact problem the reviewer describes: 'The app never linked a class choice to an inventory item… every one says "your innovation…" and nothing knew which object that meant.' `'ikon'` is already in the enum.
2. PERSISTS — round-tripped into the saved build at `src/rules/build.ts:4452` and `:4622` (`...(it.designations?.length ? { designations: it.designations } : {})`).
3. RE-POINTABLE — `setItemDesignation` at `src/rules/play.ts:1219` is exclusive and MOVES the mark: 'a designation moves rather than duplicating… two items both claiming it would apply the same modifications twice.'
4. SHOWS ON THE WEAPON ITSELF — the 'This is my → Ikon' toggle lives in the weapon's own detail panel, `src/sheet/ItemDetail.tsx:475-497`, and is offered ONLY to exemplars: `src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx:636` — `if (owned.has('exemplar')) out.push({ kind: 'ikon', label: 'Ikon' });`. Somebody already built this control for ikons specifically.
5. 'THE IKON' RESOLVES INSIDE THE STRIKE BREAKDOWN, NOT AS A GLOBAL PASSIVE — `applyWeaponRiders` (derive.ts:2525) honours `match.designated` (derive.ts:2556) and is called from `deriveStrike` (derive.ts:2588), so traits/damage die/range resolve per-strike through the pointer. `weaponMatches` (derive.ts:2387-2400) resolves `strike.instanceId` back to the inventory item for crit spec. `WeaponRider.match.designated` (types.ts:386) is documented 'Matches nothing when nothing is designated, deliberately: a "first weapon" fallback would hand a greatsword's modifications to a dagger' — i.e. the anti-global-passive property the reviewer asks for is the lane's stated design point. Same key also on `critSpecWeapons.designated` (types.ts:704), `armorRestat.designated` (types.ts:1655) and `propertyRuneBonus.designated` (types.ts:1671).

The lane is live, not theoretical: `"designated"` appears 12 times in public/core.json — 10 inventor innovation records, 1 weapon-implement, 1 bonded.

What is actually missing is DATA, not a system: `"designated":"ikon"` appears 0 times. That is the manual's 'promised but empty' bucket (a per-record defect on at most 15 records), explicitly distinguished from 'a lane this app has never built'.

The two residual sub-claims are both smaller than a system:
- 'filtered to weapons dealing piercing or slashing damage' — `WeaponRider.match` carries `melee`, `groups`, `anyTrait`, `excludeTraits`, `items`, `categories`, `hands` but no damage-type key. Of the 15 weapon-ikon feats only 2 name a damage type (branched-tree-of-pain 'piercing or slashing', motionless-cutter 'slashing'); the other 13 are already expressible with existing keys ('one-handed'→`hands:1`, 'thrown'→`anyTrait:['thrown']`, melee/ranged→`melee`). And the app's documented answer to 'the designation alone is not enough' already exists as a pairing pattern — `armorRestat.items` at types.ts:1657: 'nothing stops a player marking their full plate as the innovation'. So this is one optional key inside an existing lane. It is also an eligibility/Usage restriction, which mechanic-lanes.md lists under NOT lanes ('Prerequisites, access clauses…').
- exclusivity: only one item can hold `'ikon'` at a time, while an exemplar carries several ikons. That is a real cardinality shortfall in an existing lane — but the reviewer's own proposal asks only for 'a pointer to ONE weapon', so it is not the gap being claimed.

Two further weaknesses in the finding itself: (a) 'cluster size 3' is three lens-duplicates (numbers / resources / unmodellable) of the SAME clause on the SAME record, branched-tree-of-pain — one record, not three; (b) 26 of the 27 `ikon`-trait feats carry a 'Usage imbued into…' line, and 12 of those are body or worn ikons where no inventory pointer is wanted at all (a body ikon is the character's own body), so the proposed system would not even be the right shape for most of the family.

refuted.name: usage-requirements-on-granted-actions-and-strikes
refuted.why:
The lane is `mode` (manual section J: "a state you turn on and off — a stance, a rage, an aura, 'while X is active'"), and it already carries every part of the proposed capability, including the strike half.

1) A mode can GRANT a strike, and the strike does not exist until the toggle is on. `ModeDef.grantedStrikes?: StanceStrike[]` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:2503) is consumed in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/derive.ts:3105 as `...(c.activeModes ?? []).flatMap((m) => (m.grantedStrikes ?? []).map(...))` — sourced from activeModes ONLY, and derived at exactly the point the active stance's strikes are, so it scales identically. That is availability-gating on a granted strike, not a note beside one.

2) A mode can PRINT the un-checkable requirement. `ModeDef.note` (types.ts:2476) is documented as "effects that aren't captured as numeric modifiers (shown in the list)" and renders at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:160.

3) The exact proposed shape already ships. `stonestrike-stance` in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/toggle-modes.json is the only mode with grantedStrikes and it pairs them with `note: "Requires standing on the ground."` — a granted strike plus an availability condition the engine cannot evaluate. Swap the condition text and that record IS the jaws Strike. 24 live modes have a note that is a usage requirement; several are keyed to the character's own live state: `flamboyant-athlete` ("While you have panache"), `shadow-master` ("Only while you are in an area of dim light or darkness"), `item-cursed-dreamstone` ("Switch this on only if you failed the save against the curse"). `ModeDef.feats?: string[]` (types.ts:2472) filtered at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/modes.ts:308 scopes the toggle to characters who own the granting feat, so a zombie-dedication mode surfaces for nobody else.

The reviewer's supporting claim is also factually wrong. "No availability predicate reads the character's own live state" — C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/actionGates.ts is precisely that predicate: `actionGate()` classifies an action's required resource state, and MainTab.tsx:259-262 evaluates it against live `character.classResources`, then renders a lock icon and a "Needs Panache / Rage / Unleashed" badge (MainTab.tsx:521, 545) — the action stays readable but is marked unusable. `StanceDef.requires: { unarmored?, armored?, text }` (types.ts:2594) is a purpose-built usage-requirement field with a machine-checked half and a printed half, enforced in `stanceRequirementIssue` (derive.ts:701) which makes the whole stance inert when unmet. `activeStateGrants` (derive.ts:723) gates grants on resource state, and `conditionTypedMods(c.conditions, ...)` (derive.ts:444, 458, 462) already reads live conditions.

Two further reasons the cluster does not survive as one system. It is NOT-ONE-SYSTEM: "only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you" is a fact about the TARGET, while "while you are taking persistent bleed damage" is a predicate over your own live state — a text attachment and a runtime evaluator, sharing only the word "requirement". And the target half is OUT-OF-SCOPE by the manual's own exclusion list: "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet", plus "the internal steps of an activity … the app lists the action; the player performs it". Whether a creature is grabbed by you lives on that creature's sheet, which this app does not have.

What is actually true here is a DATA defect in existing lanes, not a missing system: public/core.json ships zombie-dedication with `grantedStrikes: [{name:"Jaws", die:"d8", damageType:"piercing", ...}]` and no `note` and no mode entry, and blood-and-spirit with nothing but a holy/unholy `choice`. Both records failed to use routes that were already built — the same "write-only-with-a-reader" shape called out in the reach-and-display sweep. Fix by authoring two mode entries (feats-gated, note-carrying, jaws under grantedStrikes) plus a ContentBase `note` on each feat; no new engine lane is required.

refuted.name: mythic-point-costs
