refuted.why: Covered by limitedUses plus the shipped mythic pool plus the printed-clause (note/description) lane — the same three-part route the app uses for every pooled cost. Concretely: (1) The cluster is one clause on one record. All 3 gold entries are the sentence "you can spend a Mythic Point" on guarded-domain, seen through the numbers/resources/unmodellable lenses. (2) The 'two independent costs' claim is already false on that very record: guarded-domain in public/core.json carries limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}, which renders as spend/refund pips via src/rules/featUses.ts (MainTab.tsx:438-470, FeatsTab.tsx:394), while the mythic point renders as pips on the Mythic card in src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:948-970 whose own comment says the pool exists to be spent from. Both costs for that single activation are visible and decrementable on the sheet today, in the two places this app tracks those two KINDS of cost — a per-record frequency on the record, a character-level pool on the rail. mythic-heightening is the same shape. (3) 'No record can declare spend a Mythic Point' is true but immaterial, because no record declares a cost against ANY pool. I scanned all 70+ collections of public/core.json for focusCost/poolCost/resourceCost-shaped fields: zero hits, and src/rules/types.ts declares none. Focus points — the app's canonical pooled cost — work identically: a focus spell record does not store 'Cost 1 Focus Point', and casting one does not deduct it (setFocusUsed at play.ts:861 is only ever called from the pip clicks in SpellsTab.tsx:1367). A pool cost in this app is expressed as the general rule plus the pool card plus the printed clause, which the lane manual's `note` lane reserves for exactly this ('a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable'). Mythic points already get precisely the treatment focus and hero points get. (4) 'Blocked when the pool is empty' is not a mythic capability at all. setMythicPoints clamps to [0, MAX_MYTHIC_POINTS] so the pool cannot be overspent, which is the only sense in which any character pool blocks. No lane anywhere greys out an ACTION because a resource is empty; the sole auto-deduct-and-gate path is the bespoke staff/wand one (canCastFromItem, src/rules/itemUses.ts:99). Feat uses disable only the spend button at zero (MainTab.tsx:451). Building auto-deduction plus gating for mythic points alone would be an app-wide inconsistency against focus, hero points and spell slots, not a filled lane — it is a UI-automation preference, not a new way of turning printed text into sheet behaviour. The pool's refresh side is likewise already modelled through an existing lane: summon-mythic-power ('You regain 1 Mythic Point') carries limitedUses {1/day} from effect-backfill.json. Real finding in passing, on an EXISTING lane: guarded-domain has actionCost {type:'passive'} and no grantsActions, so the 3-action teleport activity the clause creates never reaches the encounter action list. That is grantsAction promised-but-empty — a defect to fix on the record, not evidence of a missing system.

refuted.name: archetype-named-dc-statistics
refuted.why: REFUTED on the rules. The chronoskimmer DC is not a statistic computed from any archetype-owned proficiency or key attribute — the Chronoskimmer Dedication text defines it as "either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher" (see .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/archetype/chronoskimmer/chronoskimmer-dedication.json), and Foundry encodes Guide the Timeline's save as @Check[will|against:class-spell], the game's generic class-or-spell DC selector used by 166 feat records in the source. So the reviewer's blocker ("no class to borrow, so no way to define a DC from the archetype's own proficiency and key attribute") describes a mechanic PF2e never printed. Both operands are already first-class lanes and both are already on the sheet: Class DC via deriveClassDc (src/rules/derive.ts:438, rank driven by the `advancement` lane and `classDcRank`) and Spell DC via deriveSpellcasting (src/rules/derive.ts:454, rank driven by `profSpell`), pushed into the SAME vitals-rail stat list at src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:296-299, each with a StatRef that opens a StatDetailModal breakdown. The player reads both numbers side by side and quotes the higher one — no secondaryClassDcs borrowing needed, because nothing new is being computed. The archetype's only contribution is nomenclature, and that is already delivered twice over: the dedication's shipped description in public/core-descriptions.json prints the defining sentence verbatim on the Feats tab, and the `note` lane (types.ts:235, rendered at src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:75) exists precisely for a clause worth printing beside a record. The lane doc's own NOT-a-lane list covers this shape: "Restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere." Scope also collapses: across every archetype feat in the game the named-DC tally is 153 "your class DC", 29 "your spell DC", 9 Perception DC, plus skill and save DCs — and 3 "your chronoskimmer DC", all inside the single chronoskimmer folder (dedication, guide-the-timeline, steal-time). The claimed cluster of 3 is three audit lenses (numbers/resources/unmodellable) on ONE feat, not three feats, and it is the only archetype-named DC in Pathfinder 2e. The most that survives is a cosmetic convenience — a rail row labelled "Chronoskimmer DC" showing max(classDC, spellDC) — which is a display alias over existing lanes, not a missing capability.

refuted.name: per-target-state-tracking
refuted.why: REFUTED. The proposal rests on the premise that no lane can express a number scoped to one foe, only a printed reminder — but the reviewer weighed only `situational` (print-only) and `note` and skipped the lane immediately above them: `mode` (docs/mechanic-lanes.md §J). A ModeDef carries a free-text `duration` and modifiers of shape `{ value, type: 'circumstance', target: 'attack' }` (src/rules/types.ts:2447-2470), and an unconditional one is folded into the strike attack total with PF2e stacking at src/rules/derive.ts:2653 and :2921 via `modeTypedMods(c.activeModes,{kind:'attack'})`. So Cornered Fury is authorable exactly as the reviewer specifies it — a mode named for the foe, `duration: "1 round"`, `+2 circumstance` to `attack` — and the printed number moves, then stops when it is toggled off. Target-scoping by toggle is this lane's established idiom, not a workaround: of 203 authored modes in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json, `battle-scars` ("vs. devils") gives resistance only against one kind of foe and `geomancer-dedication` already uses `duration: "1 round"`. The situational lane independently covers the star-and-trigger half, and has this literal clause already authored: `natures-edge` reads `when: "against an enemy in difficult terrain", bonus: "the enemy is off-guard to you"` (situationalBonuses.ts:2863) — alongside `outwit` / `masterful-hunter` ("against your hunted prey's attacks"), `detectives-readiness` ("creatures tied to your open Pursue a Lead") and `destined-victory` ("against an enemy's next attack after it hits you"). The app even computes off a designated single creature already: the `hunt-prey` class resource is a live "Prey marked" toggle (VitalsRail.tsx:886) and `whileState:'hunt-prey'` gates real numbers — Flurry's MAP reduction and Ranger Precision — so they apply "against your hunted prey and nothing else" (derive.ts:1078, :2245; types.ts:444/:617). Two further reasons the cluster does not stand. (a) NOT ONE SYSTEM: the two halves share no machinery. A 1-round attack modifier is encounter-lifetime and consumed by attack-roll math; a 24-hour roster of already-targeted creatures is consumed by legality-of-reuse, survives encounters and rests, and needs creature identity to persist after the combatants are gone. Building either buys nothing toward the other, so the single "per-creature store" the proposal posits is a conflation. (b) The immunity half is a decided boundary, not a hole: 481 records in core-descriptions.json say "temporarily immune" and the app tracks a roster for none of them (the manual's "restating a general rule the app already implements everywhere" plus "effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet"); `guide-the-timeline` already carries `limitedUses {max:1, per:'day'}`, which is the restriction that actually binds this character, and the one comparable printed case, `monster-hunter`'s "only once per day against a particular creature", is already expressed as prose inside its situational `when` plus `limitedUses`. The enemy-side representation also already exists where it belongs: the tracker applies per-combatant `off-guard` (−2 circumstance AC) with a round duration that ticks down and expires (tracker/src/utils/conditionEffects.ts:251, tracker/src/store/combatStore.ts:493-501). Neither feat carries an authored entry today (no hit for `cornered-fury` in src/, scripts/data/, or effect-backfill.json) — but that is the manual's promised-but-empty bucket: missing authoring on two records whose lane already exists and is already in use for the identical clause.

refuted.name: level-derived-value-expressions
refuted.why:
The cluster is 3 entries over 2 records (gold-freetext.json #94 and #95 are the SAME shame-the-sin clause, #128 is on-my-best-day), and it staples together two capabilities that share nothing but the word 'level'. The reviewer's own justification concedes this with 'Separately, …'. Split them and each half dies on its own terms.

HALF A — 'damage dice that step at named levels'. The claim is that the app has no way to hold a damage expression that is a function of character level and re-display it as the character advances. That is false, and the counterexample ships: a cantrip's cast rank is `Math.ceil(character.level / 2)` (C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx:922, autoRank at :114), `SpellHeightening = {type:'fixed', levels: Partial<Record<SpellRank, {damage}>>}` (src/rules/types.ts:1875-1886) stores the exact 'at this step the die count becomes N' ladder, `scaleDamage()` (src/rules/heightening.ts:113-127) resolves it, and `injectDamageArrow` splices the recomputed formula inline into the printed prose. 117 spells carry a fixed per-rank damage ladder, 9 of them cantrips whose ladder is driven by character level directly. The same shape recurs all over the engine: `StanceStrike.strikingByLevel: {level, extraDice}[]` (types.ts:2558, read at derive.ts:3122, populated at modes.ts:222-225) is literally level-keyed extra damage DICE on a granted strike; `precisionDice.upgradeAt {level, die}` (types.ts:603) is a level-keyed damage-die step; sneak attack (1d6→4d6 at L5/11/17), Ranger Precision (1d8→3d8 at L11/19) and rage damage tiers are computed from `c.level` in derive.ts:2192-2250; and `resolveFormula` (derive.ts:1330) is a general CSP-safe evaluator for `@actor.level` expressions with floor/ceil/max/min, already used for resistances, weaknesses, speeds, language counts and daily-item level caps. Add `rankUpgrade` steps, `limitedUses.maxByLevel`, `heightenAt`, `heightenHalfLevel`, `countByLevel`, `spellRankByLevel`, `pickByLevel`, `maxAtLevels`, `whileActive.minLevel`, `advancement.ts`. 'A number in a record's effect that is an expression of character level' is not an absent system in this app — it is one of the most heavily built shapes in it.

What is actually missing for shame-the-sin is not the level expression. Its full text is 'Trigger: You critically hit a demon… the demon also suffers the effects of its special vulnerability. If the demon has no special vulnerability, it instead takes an additional [1]d6 mental damage.' The blocker is the gate — a degree-of-success trigger AND a target creature trait AND the absence of a property that exists only on the TARGET's stat block. That is a different candidate, and the audit already recorded it separately as entry #96. It is also on the wrong side of the manual's NOT-lane 'effects on enemies rather than on your own sheet' — entry #97 concedes 'nothing about this can sit on the character sheet beyond printing the sentence.' With the gate unmodellable and target-dependent, there is no place to compute the number; the surviving route is the existing `note` lane, and the printed sentence already states the whole ladder ('2d6 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th'), so it is not 'wrong at two levels' — it is correct at every level. Today the record carries only `limitedUses` (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json), so this is a promised-but-empty `note`, a defect on an existing lane, not a missing system. The missing base die is an upstream AoN text defect (the known text-formatting corpus), not a capability gap.

HALF B — 'a very hard DC of your level'. This is not a value inside a record's effect at all; it is the target number of a check the player attempts, which the manual explicitly lists as a NOT-lane ('the internal steps of an activity… attempt an Athletics check. The app lists the action; the player performs it'). And the premise that the table and its adjustments do not exist as first-class values is simply wrong: DC_BY_LEVEL {0:14 … 25:50} and DC_ADJUST including ['Very hard', +5] are canonical tables in the embedded tracker (tracker/src/components/GmWidgets.tsx:49-51, surfaced as the 'DCs by level' widget at :32 and :138-163), LEVEL_DC drives the Downtime calculator (tracker/src/components/DowntimeWidget.tsx:10-11), RK_DC_BY_LEVEL is applied computationally in StatBlock.tsx:396, and the in-app searchable rules library ships both Table 10-5: DCs by Level and Table 10-6: DC Adjustments (public/data/rules.json, loaded by tracker/src/data/dataStore.ts:256). The residual ask — auto-substituting '41' into one 18th-level feat's sentence — is a display nicety on a GM-facing lookup, and it has nothing whatever to do with a strike's damage dice: different value, different consumer, different storage, different subsystem.

Neither half is a system, and together they are not one system. Refuted.

refuted.name: damage-type-substitution-by-source-family
refuted.why:
Refuted. The lane that covers it is `note` (J. Conditional and toggleable), with the pick already carried by `choice`. Three measurements do the work.

(1) The choice half is already built. `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json` → feats.energized-spark carries `choice: { flag: 'energizedSpark', kind: 'array', options: [12 damage types] }`. `kind: 'array'` is the repeatable-pick shape, so the reviewer's second clause ("select multiple times, a different type each time, picks accumulate into a menu") is already stored today.

(2) The substitution half changes no quantity the sheet holds — so by the manual's own definition it is not computable, it is a clause left to the table. Energized Spark retypes damage; the amount, the attack bonus, the die count and the DC are all identical before and after. The only consequence lands on the target's IWR, which is not on this sheet. Contrast the two acknowledged missing lanes in the manual: `builtInRunes` makes Obsidian Edge display +21/1d10 instead of +24/3d10+1d6 fire — an actively WRONG number. Energized Spark can never make any number on the sheet wrong. `note`'s own contract in `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/types.ts:227` is exactly this case: "This record works; here is the part you apply yourself… for a clause the rules leave to the table." It renders under the description on the Feats tab (26 records use it).

(3) The shipped precedent is `versatile` — PF2e's own elective, per-instance, replace-not-add damage-type swap. The app's answer is a glossary line, `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/rules/glossary.ts:85`: "Versatile: each Strike can instead deal the listed damage type … of your choice." No computed alternative damage line, no toggle, no restated type — and nobody has filed that as a defect, because the app does not roll damage (DiceTray is a generic roller; strike damage is rendered as a formula string). "Elective per instance" therefore has no state for the app to hold, which is why nothing in the engine sets or overrides a damage type: `applyWeaponRiders` (`src/rules/derive.ts` ~2515-2582) can add/remove traits, set or step the die and change the range increment, but never the type.

The reviewer's central difficulty — "scoped by a source family rather than a named ability" — is a data-shape artefact, the exact trap `project_hh_lane_measurement` warns about. Measured against the app's actual storage, only THREE records carry a spirit-typed `strikeDamage` rider: classFeatures/spirit-striking, classFeatures/greater-spirit-striking (mutually exclusive tiers of one effect) and feats/gird-champion (a champion feat, not exemplar). All 21 exemplar ikon classFeatures carry `grantsClassFeatures` and nothing else — their immanence spirit damage is not computed at all. So the "whole family of abilities that know nothing about this feat" is, in this app, one rider on one owned record — which is precisely the gate `modifiesGrant` already implements (`src/rules/build.ts:3264`).

Correct follow-up: a data fix (add `note` to energized-spark), not an engine system.

Three genuine defects found in passing, all inside EXISTING lanes — do not let them be rebadged as this system: (a) 21 ikon classFeatures promise "deals N additional spirit damage per weapon damage die" in prose and carry no `strikeDamage` — promised-but-empty weaponRider on the biggest exemplar damage source; (b) feats/elemental-wrath's four `effectChoices` options all grant the identical acid-splash innate spell, so the chosen type is discarded (same note fix, same shape); (c) `RAGE_DAMAGE` in `src/rules/derive.ts:2256-2265` prints the literal placeholder "energy" for dragon-instinct and elemental-instinct instead of the chosen element.

refuted.name: deferred-prerequisite-evaluation
refuted.why: Covered by grantsFeatChoice (FEAT_PICK_GRANTS + pickableFeats + build.pickFeatChoices), and the reviewer's premise is factually false. (1) pickableFeats (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:200-228) never reads feat.prerequisites — it filters only on level, category, traits, dynamic class/ancestry trait and exclusions. checkPrerequisites is called from exactly three places, all on the NORMAL feat-slot path (Builder.tsx:1437, 1893, 2001); the granted-pick pickers (Builder.tsx:1604-1624 plus the class-feature, heritage and background twins) pass options with no disabled flag and no prereq call, and buildCharacter's grant step (build.ts:2744-2769) re-checks only pool membership. There is no prerequisite gate on a granted pick, so nothing can wrongly reject a legal choice. (2) I ran the exact scenario: human rogue, Natural Ambition at L1 picking plant-evidence (prereq Pickpocket) with Pickpocket taken in the level-4 skill slot — granted, grantedBy natural-ambition. It is granted even when Pickpocket is never taken at all, and overextending-feint / plant-evidence are both offered while checkPrerequisites reports them unmet. Prereq-bearing L1 options exist in live data for 16 of 27 classes (maguss-analysis, draconic-arrogance, 7 champion cause feats, focused-fascination, ...). (3) 'May stay empty' is already the behavior: build.ts:2752 skips an empty pick silently, pendingCount (Builder.tsx:871-878) does not even count it as pending, and submit (line 888) never hard-blocks an under-built character. (4) There is no 'state when it was offered' to defer past: buildCharacter is a pure function of BuildState, pickFeatChoices is an order-free map, and the only build handed to any prereq check is featPrereqChar = buildCharacter(build, ovContent) (Builder.tsx:255) — the finished character at full level. Even for ordinary slots, a later edit that breaks a met prerequisite warns and never auto-removes (Builder.tsx:1431-1433). (5) The spec vocabulary already encodes prerequisite waivers directly: ancient-elf's maxLevel 2 for 'even though you don't meet its level prerequisite', pirate-combat-training for 'even if you do not meet its prerequisites', advanced-* maxLevel 'half', and the file's stated convention 'at worst slightly permissive, never blocking a legal pick'. Secondary: docs/mechanic-lanes.md:164 lists prerequisites and access clauses under NOT lanes, and all three gold entries key off one such clause, which instructs the player on creation order rather than moving anything on the sheet.

refuted.name: flat-checks-as-a-modifiable-roll
refuted.why:
The `situational` lane covers it, and mechanic-lanes.md row J/`situational` names `situationalBonuses.ts` in full as the satisfier — which is where both routes live.

(1) The reviewer's premise is wrong about the lane. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts header states the registry "is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number" — it flags a surface and prints the `when` for the player to apply. So "the roll is not a statistic the sheet computes" was never a requirement; no situational entry needs its target to be computed.

(2) Five live records already carry this exact clause via `targets: [{ kind: 'hp' }]`: cindersoul, fire-lung, fire-savvy, scar-thick-skin, scorched-on-the-crackling-mountain — e.g. `when: "on the flat check to recover from persistent acid, bleed, or poison damage"`. The damage type rides in the `when` prose, exactly as the reviewer wants it tied. It is not write-only: explain.ts:831 (`case 'hp'`) returns `situational: situationalList([], featSituationalLines(c, db, ref))`, so those lines render in the HP detail modal.

(3) The reviewer read only the `SituationalTarget.kind` union and missed `RecordMarker` in the same file (line ~3155), whose doc comment is verbatim their objection: "Some things change no number the sheet holds… starring 'the nearest roll' would be a lie." Four records already key it to the persistent-damage condition with damage-type-specific values — stone-blood, stone-blood-stonebound, mutated-fleshwarp, steelskin-hobgoblin (`value: "DC 13 flat check"`, persistent physical/energy/poison). `persistent-damage` is a real condition in public/core.json, and VitalsRail.tsx:1026 calls `recordMarkersFor(character, content, 'condition', c.id)`, rendering a SituationalStar on the condition pill that opens the notes — surfacing at the exact moment the player rolls the check. divine-health's clause is one line: `{ on: 'condition', id: 'persistent-damage', value: '+2 vs poison', note: 'Divine Health: +2 status to the DC 15 flat check to end persistent poison damage.' }`.

(4) A numeric BONUS (not just a DC change) landing on a flat check is already expressed: the recovery check is a flat check, and the-survivor carries "+2 item bonus to recovery checks", hero-gods-bond "+2 circumstance bonus to recovery checks", draddeths-edge an item bonus equal to its potency rune — all as `on: 'condition', id: 'dying'` markers.

(5) The cluster size is inflated. gold-freetext.json entries 55, 58 and 62 are the same feat (divine-health) and the same clause, differing only by `lens` (numbers / resources / unmodellable). One clause on one record, not three.

The genuine residual is a data defect, not a missing capability: situationalBonuses.ts:180 gives divine-health only the saves half (`targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'all' }], when: "saves against diseases and poisons"`) and drops "and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage". That is 'promised but empty' in the manual's own vocabulary — a one-line addition to an existing table, identical in shape to cindersoul.

refuted.name: emanation-statistics
refuted.why:
The covering lane is `mode` (docs section J), whose own definition names the shape verbatim: "a state you turn on and off — a stance, a rage, an aura, 'while X is active'" — paired with `note` (also section J: "a clause worth printing on the sheet but not computable"). The reviewer picked the wrong nearest lane: they compared against `sense`/`vision` in section D, so they never tested the lane that was built for auras. Both halves are not merely expressible, they are already SHIPPED.

Aura-as-a-thing-the-character-deals: `core.stances['thermal-nimbus']` in C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core.json already reads "Choose cold or fire; you and allies in your kinetic aura gain resistance equal to your level to that type, and creatures starting or moving into the aura take half-your-level damage of the chosen type." That single field carries the radius (kinetic aura), the amount (half your level), the type (the chosen one), and BOTH positional triggers (starting / moving in). It renders on the sheet at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/MainTab.tsx:878-879 (`content.stances[character.activeStance].note` → `.stance-note`), i.e. exactly the reviewer's stated requirement that "even setting the enemy side aside, that statistic has to be displayed as something the character deals." It is displayed, owned by the character, and gated on the aura being active. 23 of 128 entries in scripts/data/stances.json describe an aura this way; 5 of them are damage auras (crowned-in-tempests-fury "take 2d12 electricity damage", ravel-of-thorns, steam-knight, drifting-pollen, winter-sleet). The chosen energy type is not even freetext — `effect-backfill.json` gives thermal-nimbus an `effectChoices` block whose cold/fire options each grant `resistances: [{type, value: '@actor.level'}]`, so the player's aura choice drives a real number.

Light emission: 12 shipped entries in `core.modes` already carry this precise sentence — item-bioluminescent-stripes: "You shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for the next 20 feet, and you can't be undetected"; item-draft-of-stellar-radiance: "You emanate bright light in a 20-foot radius (dim light for another 20 feet)"; plus the four golden-wings tiers, heartblood-ring, the sprite apples, the abysium chunk/ingot. Mode notes render at C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/src/sheet/ModesPanel.tsx:160. So "nothing expresses bright light to 30 feet and dim light to the next 30" is false — the app expresses it a dozen times over; ascended-celestial-dedication is simply the record that hasn't been given its row.

That leaves the cluster's real residue as a populate-the-lane defect, not a missing system: ascended-celestial-dedication has `limitedUses` and `grantsActions` but no stance and no mode entry, so its nimbus clause is "promised but empty" in the manual's own vocabulary — one data row in scripts/data/toggle-modes.json away. Cluster size 2 becomes 1 record needing an existing lane populated.

Two further refutations stand behind this one if the mode lane were somehow disallowed. (a) not-one-system: a light radius and a damage aura share only the word "radius". Light emission is an illumination fact with no magnitude the sheet can compute; aura damage is an amount, a type and two turn-order triggers. No single field or display could serve both, so the cluster is a coincidence of geometry, not a system. (b) out-of-scope: the only part of either clause that a field could actually COMPUTE — who is inside the radius, whether a creature's turn began there, what the illumination does to concealment — requires positions, and this app models no map, grid, or distance anywhere. That is precisely the manual's NOT-lane "Effects on enemies or on the battlefield rather than on your own sheet," and it is a VTT concern. The mode/stance note is the app's designed answer for exactly this class of clause: print the uncomputable positional part, compute the part that lands on this sheet (thermal-nimbus's own resistance).

refuted.name: healing-source-inversion
refuted.why:
The lane exists as the field `negativeHealing` — the pre-remaster name for the rule the remaster renamed "void healing", which is why a search for "void"-style field names missed it. Declared on `DefenseGrants` at src/rules/types.ts:655 ("Grants void (\"negative\") healing — harmed by vitality, healed by void"), inherited by `Feat` (types.ts:1412 `Feat extends ContentBase, DefenseGrants`) and `Heritage` (types.ts:1212). Read at src/rules/derive.ts:1756-1759, which aggregates it from heritage, ANY feat (`c.feats.some((f) => db.feats[f.featId]?.negativeHealing)`), and invested items, onto `CharacterDefenses.negativeHealing` (derive.ts:1264). Surfaced in two places: src/sheet/DefensesPills.tsx:81-88 renders a "Void healing — healed by void, harmed by vitality" row, and src/sheet/VitalsRail.tsx:738-752 renders it with an InfoTerm whose description is literally "You are healed by void (negative) energy and harmed by vitality (positive) energy, as if you were undead." It is live end-to-end today on the `dhampir` heritage and 4 items (emerald-fulcrum-lens, pierce-the-veil, aon-pierce-the-veil, aeon-stone-mottled-ellipsoid); the audit patch validator already whitelists it (scripts/audit/apply-patches.ts:198); situationalBonuses.ts:950 keys a bonus off "requires void healing"; monsterPartsCatalog.ts:837,892 gate on "undead trait or void healing"; and companionGrants.ts:292 / companions.ts:840 already carry the void-healing clause for undead companions and eidolons. So the reviewer's central assertion — "no field re-routes healing", "the healing inversion is the part with no home anywhere" — is factually false.

Decisive data point: all six records that cite "the basic undead benefits" (ghost-, ghoul-, lich-, mummy-, vampire-, zombie-dedication) ALREADY carry the immunity half of the bundle in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep) — the bundle was already expanded onto each record. `negativeHealing` is simply `undefined` on all six. That is a promised-but-empty defect in the lanes manual's own vocabulary, fixed by a one-field patch per record, not a lane this app never built.

The rest of the proposed bundle decomposes into existing lanes, making this cluster not-one-system as a secondary read: the immunities are the `immunity` lane (already carried); "no need to breathe, eat, drink or sleep" is the `note` lane (section J), live on feats via FeatsTab.tsx:75, with the sibling `breathesWater` sitting in the same DefenseGrants block for the aquatic version of the same shape; "ordinary healing fails" is not a third mechanic but the second clause of the single printed void-healing rule, which the app's own InfoTerm already states; and character creature traits is a genuinely separate question belonging to a different cluster (gold-freetext entries 15/20/22), not this one.

The "must be one named bundle rather than a hand-copied list" objection is authoring ergonomics, not capability: it covers 6 records total (I counted every record whose description text cites "basic undead benefits"), the expansion pattern is already in use on those exact 6 for immunities, `rules | basic-undead-benefits` already exists as a linkable record for the prose, and grantsFeats / grantsClassFeatures / modifiesGrant exist if shared-record reuse were ever wanted.

One genuine finding worth acting on separately: `negativeHealing` and `breathesWater` are missing from section C of C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/docs/mechanic-lanes.md, which lists only acBonus, saveBonus, resistance, immunity, weakness, hardness. A classifier reading that manual cannot name the lane, so every void-healing record will keep being reported as an unbuilt system.

refuted.name: materials-on-unarmed-strikes
refuted.why: The reviewer picked the wrong neighbour lane. The app's route for "a precious material on your melee unarmed attacks" is `situational` (Section J), and it is ALREADY AUTHORED for the identical clause: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:2780 carries "adamantine-strikes": [{ targets: [{kind:'strikeDamage'}], when: "with your unarmed attacks", bonus: "they are treated as adamantine (bypassing adamantine-gated resistances and Hardness)" }]. That record is real — public/core.json classFeatures['adamantine-strikes'], monk level 17, text "Your unarmed attacks are treated as adamantine" — and it reaches the sheet: characterSituationalIds (src/rules/explain.ts:197-201) walks ownedFeatureIds, so class features raise the star, and the line surfaces in the strike-damage breakdown (explain.ts:985). Its sibling classFeatures['metal-strikes'] (monk 9, "treated as cold iron AND silver") shows the two-metals-at-once case is the same lane; it has no entry in src/ or scripts/data/, so it is a promised-but-empty defect INSIDE a built lane, not a missing lane. (2) The accumulation is already stored, not absent: core.json feats['precious-alloys'] already carries maxTakable: 3 plus choice {flag:'material', kind:'array', options:[adamantine, cold-iron, silver]}; maxTakes() (featGrants.ts:330) with featSlots.ts:48 keeps it offered until three copies are held, each taking's answer is keyed to its own slotKey (build.ts:1994-2002, 2721), and FeatsTab.tsx:85 prints each row as "Precious Alloys (Precious Material Cold Iron)". Two takings already yield two independent metals on one sheet. (3) A second, stronger route also exists: UnarmedRider.add (types.ts:325-353, applied by applyUnarmedRiders at derive.ts:3011-3060) merges arbitrary trait strings into every unarmed Strike the character already has, and MainTab.tsx:377-385 renders that list on each strike row. (4) The claim that material must "feed the rules that key off material" is false in this app: item.material is read in exactly four places, all display — filterSpecs.ts:137, InventoryTab.tsx:285, ItemDetail.tsx:120-121, ItemEditorModal.tsx:183-184/519-520 — and by zero rules files. Resistance bypass, creature weakness and object Hardness are the TARGET's numbers, which the lane manual's NOT-lanes list explicitly excludes, and materials already sit in the IWR type vocabulary from the character side anyway (werecreature-dedication writes weaknesses [{type:'silver'}], Demon's Knot writes cold-iron 10). So the item `material` lane the reviewer calls the nearest neighbour is itself only a label, and there is no material-keyed computation for a strike material to be denied. What is genuinely absent is only wording precision — a static situational string cannot name WHICH metal this taking chose — but the chosen metal already prints on the sheet in the feat row, and the lane manual's own "What this method cannot catch" section classes value/wording gaps as defects inside a lane, not new systems.

refuted.name: spell-subsystem-retagging
refuted.why:
REFUTED on three independent grounds.

(1) The justification is factually wrong about PF2e. The reviewer's whole case is 'casting a revelation spell escalates the curse'. It does not. core-descriptions.json -> classFeatures/oracular-curse says escalation triggers on using a CURSEBOUND ABILITY ('Immediately after the first time you use a cursebound ability, you become cursebound 1...'), and classFeatures/revelation-spells says only 'Revelation spells are a type of focus spell.' The cursebound trait is what the curse rules key on, and exactly 5 spells in core.json carry it (call-to-arms, debilitating-dichotomy, heroic-feat, vision-of-weakness, ash-form). Domain Fluency's advanced domain spell is not cursebound and does not become cursebound by being cast as a revelation spell. Recording the 'revelation' sub-category would therefore change no curse behaviour, and wiring escalation to it would be a NEW BUG.

(2) There is no asymmetry between the granted spell and a native one. The oracle's own initial/advanced/greater revelation spells are stored in the identical untagged shape - core.json classes.oracle.subclass.options[n] carries focusSpells:['ancestral-touch'], advancedFocusSpell:'ancestral-defense', greaterFocusSpell:'ancestral-form', with no sub-category either. And nothing in src/ reads a revelation sub-category anywhere (the only 'revelation' hits in src are build.ts:1917-1918 mapping the advanced-/greater-revelation FEATS to the mystery's spell, plus unrelated item names). A retag would have no reader, so it cannot be what makes anything behave correctly.

(3) The lane that covers it is focusSpell (E. Magic), and it already carries the full mechanical content of 'you cast it as a revelation spell'. build.ts:2456-2486 builds the focus spellcasting entry with focusTradition and focusKey derived from the CLASS (oracle -> divine / Cha), NOT from the spell's own 'cleric' trait - so disperse-into-air in an oracle's list is cast at the oracle's focus DC/attack, out of the oracle's single shared focus pool. domain-fluency's focusPoolBonus:1 raises that pool; its effectChoices[].grant.focusSpells route is read at build.ts:2102-2105, which also sets focusSource, and SpellsTab.tsx:1299-1307 renders the card as 'rank N - from Domain Fluency'. Divine tradition + Cha + oracle focus DC + oracle focus pool + labelled origin IS being a revelation spell, for every purpose a character sheet computes.

Decisive corroboration: the app ALREADY handles the one record in this family where retagging does have a rules consequence. diverse-mystery (borrowing another mystery's revelation spell) is built with its effectChoices prompt reading '(it gains the cursebound trait, and casting it also inflicts that mystery's Cursebound 1)' and situationalBonuses.ts:176 carrying the -1 status penalty to all saves and Perception 'while Cursebound 1 from this spell'. paradoxical-mystery (L20) - the same 'you gain that spell as a revelation spell' shape - is built as an open daily choice with from.anyTraits:['cleric','oracle'] plus a note stating what the app cannot check. So the choice + note + situational lanes already express retagging wherever it bites; domain-fluency simply has no bite to express.

The curse subsystem itself is fully modelled and player-driven, not spell-triggered: classResources.ts:112-123 defines cursebound as a meter (max 2/3/4 at L1/11/17, dropping 1 on Refocus), modes.ts:150-154 gives the four exclusive cursebound stage modes, and each mystery's curse is real data - e.g. curse-of-creeping-ashes-1..4 in core.json modes carry actual weaknesses:[{type:'fire',value:2}] and modifiers, with situationalBonuses.ts:3299+ holding per-curse condition notes. No spell cast auto-increments that meter for ANY spell, native revelation spells included, so the granted spell is not disadvantaged relative to anything.

Finally, the stated cluster size overstates the evidence: both gold-freetext.json entries are the SAME feat and the SAME clause (feat 'domain-fluency', clause 'which you cast as a revelation spell'), counted once under lens 'numbers' and once under lens 'unmodellable'. This is one clause on one L12 feat, not a two-record pattern.

Residual (cosmetic, not a missing system): domain-fluency's effectChoices prompt reads 'you gain its ADVANCED domain spell' and could read '...which you cast as a revelation spell' - a one-string edit in the existing prompt/note lane, exactly as paradoxical-mystery and diverse-mystery already do. That is a wording nit inside an existing lane, not an absent capability.

refuted.name: rest-cycle-upkeep-obligations
refuted.why: The `dailyChoice` lane already covers it, and a shipped record does exactly this. cape-of-justice (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json) is a `choice.daily` whose note states the consequence of NOT doing the task: "Name none - or let 24 hours pass without slaying or capturing them - and you take a -1 item penalty to Perception for 24 hours instead." fortune-cord ships the same thing as chips: an option `none`/"None loaded" whose description is the consequence; transmute-weapon and warshard-rune both ship a "type none to skip" branch. So a do-it/didn't-do-it branch with a stated consequence is already live data, and the reviewer's "task, not a pick" distinction is UI copy, not a capability - a task with two outcomes IS a two-option pick in this model. The lane supplies every property claimed missing: (a) it surfaces at rest - CharacterSheet.tsx:231, default `dailyPrepPrompt` is 'ask' (CustomizationEditor.tsx:148) so every daily choice is re-shown at every rest; (b) it must be cleared - CharacterSheet.tsx:848 disables "Prepare for the day" until each asked choice has an answer; (c) the un-cleared branch carries live mechanics that expire nightly - derive.ts:1048-1071 dailyChoiceGrants applies an option's full EffectGrant only while it is today's stored answer; (d) wiring it is a data edit, not code (dailyChoices.ts:11). The Slowed 1 consequence is not a missing lane either: conditions.ts:13 rules action-economy conditions (Slowed/Stunned/Quickened) out of scope by design ("no flat number to display"); Slowed is a valued condition in core.json the player steps in ConditionsModal, and every other Slowed source in the app uses that same route - see modes.ts:178 (Unleash Psyche) carrying "afterward you're slowed 1" as a mode note. Finally the record's own text defeats a pure rest-hook reading: deterioration also starts MID-DAY ("some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body"), so the state itself is the `mode` lane (toggle on when it happens, off after repair; modes already interact with rest via duration/survivesRest, types.ts:2534-2543) and the repair is `grantsAction` with actionCost {type:'duration', text:'10 minutes'} (types.ts:135). One honest caveat, a display defect inside the existing lane rather than a missing system: FeatChoiceDef.note is not carried into the Rest sheet (DailyChoice interface, dailyChoices.ts:19-30, drops it) and option `description` renders only as a title tooltip (CharacterSheet.tsx:783), so the consequence must sit in the option LABEL to be visible - a one-field plumbing fix.
